docs.t: Indian sidereal astrology: Parashari, Jaimini, Tajika, Nadi, Kerala, Tamil, KP, Lal Kitab, read only by its own rules. Birth: 13 Oct 1998, 21:25 UT (17:25 EDT, a Tuesday), Johnstown PA, 40.33N 78.92W. Computed from scratch with Skyfield + DE440s, Lahiri ayanamsha 23°50′10″. Inventory: deep/01_inventory.md. Labels: Calculated = my own computation; Source = a text was checked this round; Source, verify = given from memory or from one secondary source; Interpretation = my reading under the school's rules. By rule, this chapter has no health, illness or longevity content. Where a technique is mainly about those things (Ayur dashas, Shoola dasha, Mrityu/Beeja sphuta, maraka timing), I list it and do not read it.

Calculated Sidereal positions (whole-sign houses from Kumbha lagna): Graha Sign Deg Nakshatra-pada House Dignity Notes Lagna Kumbha 26°48′ Purva Bhadrapada 3 1 – lord Shani Sun Kanya 26°29′ Chitra 1 8 neutral Atmakaraka Moon Karka 13°40′ Pushya 4 6 own sign waning, tithi Krishna Navami Mars Simha 10°02′ Magha 4 7 friend with Rahu Mercury Tula 8°57′ Swati 1 9 friend combust (12.5° from Sun) Jupiter Kumbha 25°52′ Purva Bhadrapada 2 1 neutral retrograde, with Ketu Venus Kanya 22°18′ Hasta 4 8 debilitated combust (4.2°) Saturn Mesha 7°06′ Ashwini 3 3 debilitated retrograde, lagna lord Rahu Simha 4°45′ Magha 2 7 – mean node Ketu Kumbha 4°45′ Dhanishta 4 1 – Interpretation What this means for you. Your rising sign is Kumbha, ruled by Shani. Parashara and Saravali describe the Kumbha native as thoughtful, reserved, fond of learning and of groups, slow to warm and steady once committed, and with a streak of independence that resists being told what to do (Saravali ch.36; Phaladeepika 9 Source, verify ). Jupiter rising adds dignity, a teacher's or adviser's manner, and a wish to be seen as principled. Ketu rising beside it adds detachment and a habit of withdrawing when things get loud. People tend to read you as calm and a little distant before they find out how much you care about ideas. Your Moon in its own sign, Karka, in Pushya, gives an emotional nature that is protective, loyal and attached to home and family. Because it sits in the 6th house, that care often goes into duty, work routines and solving other people's problems, and less into self-indulgence. Mars and Rahu in the 7th mean partnerships are lively and sometimes combative. Sun, Venus and Mercury tied to the 8th and 9th mean that money, beliefs and love go through change and private reworking rather than staying simple. D1 Lagna kundali, North Indian diamond (house 1 at top; numbers are signs) D1 Rashi chakra, South Indian fixed-sign grid with degrees (diagonal marks the lagna) Interpretation Three things carry this chart. (1) The lagna lord, Saturn, is debilitated and retrograde in the 3rd: in house context reversed-strong (§18.2). (2) Jupiter, a natural benefic and lord of 2 and 11, sits in the lagna with Ketu. (3) The yogakaraka for Kumbha lagna, Venus (lord of 4 and 9) Source, verify: BPHS ch.34 , is debilitated and combust in the 8th, but its debilitation is cancelled (see §4). The Moon is strong in its own sign, but it is in the 6th house. On this school's terms the chart is mixed and works through effort (dusthana and upachaya emphasis). It is not an effortless raja chart. Interpretation What this means for you. Put simply, nothing in your life is meant to arrive pre-packaged. BPHS's rule that the lagna lord's state shows the whole tone of life (BPHS 24 Source, verify ) puts Saturn at the centre. Revised in §18: read with its house, Saturn is reversed-strong (cancelled twice, retrograde-in-debility = exalted-like results, a malefic thriving in the 3rd, sitting on the navamsha lagna), so expect a slow start but courage and persistence as core assets that grow with age. The 3rd-house placement means courage, siblings, short ventures, writing and your own hands are where you build that confidence. Jupiter in the lagna is the counterweight. Phaladeepika 8 says Jupiter rising makes a person learned, respected and well-meaning Source, verify . Kumbha is not a sign Jupiter likes much, though, so the gift shows as good judgment rather than easy luck. For money, Jupiter as lord of 2 and 11 sitting on the self says income follows from your own reputation and counsel. For relationships, Venus (the marriage karaka) is weak, Mars–Rahu sit in the 7th and the Sun (7th lord) is in the 8th, which is the classical picture of a marriage that comes with tests, a later or unconventional choice, or a partner with an intense or foreign colouring (Saravali 30–34 on 7th-house malefics Source, verify ). Chandra lagna: the chart re-cast from the Moon in Karka Surya lagna: the chart re-cast from the Sun in Kanya Graha drishti: full 7th aspects plus the special aspects of Mars (4,8), Jupiter (5,9) and Saturn (3,10) Calculated Aspects. Jupiter aspects Mithuna (5th), Simha (7th: Mars, Rahu) and Tula (9th: Mercury). Saturn aspects Mithuna, Tula (Mercury) and Makara (12th). Mars aspects Vrischika (10th), Kumbha (lagna, Jupiter, Ketu) and Meena. Mars and Saturn both aspect the 10th-house axis (Mars directly, Saturn the 12th and 9th). The 10th house (Vrischika) is empty, and its lord Mars is in the 7th with Rahu. Interpretation What this means for you. Jupiter's gaze on the 5th, 7th and 9th protects children, marriage and beliefs. A Jyotishi treats this as the chart's main softening influence: whatever trouble shows in those houses, Guru's aspect keeps it repairable (BPHS 26 on Jupiter's drishti Source, verify ). Saturn's gaze on the 5th, 9th and 12th makes learning, faith and spending serious and slow, things you approach with caution and some scepticism. Mars aspecting the 10th and the lagna gives drive and a competitive edge at work, but also impatience. The empty 10th, ruled by a Mars that sits with Rahu in the 7th, says your career is shaped by other people, partners, clients and contracts, and by bold, unconventional moves rather than a fixed ladder. Interpretation Section synthesis. The rashi chart shows a reflective, principled, somewhat reserved person whose confidence is built rather than given (Saturn), whose wisdom is real but has to be practised to pay (Jupiter in Kumbha), whose feelings go into duty (Moon in 6), and whose love and money pass through upheaval (Venus, Sun in 8). The difficulties are real: a slow start, testing partnerships, a debilitated lagna lord. So are the strengths: Jupiter's protection, a strong Moon, and cancellations on both weak planets.

Panchanga, the five limbs of the birth moment Nakshatra chakra: 27 lunar mansions with every graha Calculated Vara Tuesday (Mangala); tithi 24 = Krishna Navami; yoga #22 Sadhya; karana #48 Taitila; Pushya nakshatra, pada 4. It was a day birth, 1 h 14 m before sunset (sunset 22:39 UT, 6:39 PM EDT). Interpretation What this means for you. Born on Tuesday (Mars's day), you have a fighting, practical streak under the calm surface. Muhurta texts call Krishna Navami a 'rikta' (empty) tithi linked with forceful or decisive action (Muhurta Chintamani Source, verify ), so you tend to clear things away before you build. Sadhya yoga is named for 'accomplishment': goals are reached, though often by persistence. Taitila karana is associated with comfort and a liking for pleasant surroundings. A day birth puts the Sun's side of the chart forward: duty, public role and the father's line. Source Brihat Jataka 16.5: śāntātmā subhagaḥ paṇḍito dhanī dharma-saṃsṛtaḥ puṣye , "born in Pushya: calm-minded, fortunate, learned, wealthy, devoted to dharma" (wisdomlib.org, Neely tr.; vedicpupil.in). Jatakabharana 2.56 and Manasagari 1.21.8 agree (vedicpupil.in) Source . Interpretation What this means for you. Pushya is called the most auspicious of the 27 stars, and the classical verse fits your temperament: a calm mind, a love of learning, a concern with doing right, and steady accumulation rather than windfalls. The honest limit: these verses describe one-twenty-seventh of everyone born. They show the grain of your mind, not a special status. Pushya natives also carry a known shadow in commentary. They can be rigid about what is 'proper', anxious about security, and inclined to over-nurture or take on others' burdens Source, verify . Source, verify Pushya attributes: deity Brihaspati; symbol a cow's udder or flower; Deva gana; yoni goat/ram; Madhya nadi; Shani as nakshatra lord. Interpretation What this means for you. With Brihaspati as the star's deity and Shani as its lord, your mind is pulled between Jupiter's 'teach and expand' and Saturn's 'limit and endure'. That is the same tension the rashi chart shows in the lagna. In marriage matching (Ashtakoota), Deva gana and Madhya nadi are the factors a family astrologer would check against a partner's chart. Nothing can be said about compatibility without the second chart. Calculated Tara-bala from the janma star: Jupiter and lagna fall in Parama-mitra , Mercury in Mitra , Venus in Sadhaka ; the Sun and Ketu in Vadha ; Mars, Saturn and Rahu in Vipat . Interpretation What this means for you. Tara-bala tells you which planets 'feel friendly' to your mind. Jupiter and the lagna in Parama-mitra mean your own judgment and your advisers support you. Mercury in Mitra makes thinking and trade agreeable. Venus in Sadhaka ('accomplishing') means Venus matters, the coming mahadasha among them, do deliver, though not without effort. The Sun in Vadha and Mars, Saturn and Rahu in Vipat mean authority figures, conflict, delay and sudden disruption land hard on your feelings. Expect bosses, rivals and setbacks to sting more than they would for others, and give yourself recovery time. Calculated Lagna nakshatra: Purva Bhadrapada (deity Aja Ekapada Source, verify ), lord Jupiter, and Jupiter itself sits there. This doubles Jupiter's say over the self. Interpretation What this means for you. Purva Bhadrapada is the star of the 'one-footed goat', Aja Ekapada, a fierce, ascetic form. The nakshatra texts give it intensity, idealism, a two-sided nature (worldly and otherworldly), and a talent for persuasion (Nakshatra traditions after Taittiriya Brahmana Source, verify ). With Jupiter as both star lord and occupant, your sense of who you are is tied to your beliefs. When your ideals are working, you are steady. When they are disappointed, you can turn sharply against what you once believed in. Calculated KP star, sub and sub-sub lords: lagna Venus/Venus/Saturn, Moon Rahu/Saturn/Mars, Sun Jupiter/Saturn/Sun. Full table: KP star/sub/sub-sub lords and the Chandra Kala Nadi nadiamsha number of each point Interpretation In KP, the lagna's star and sub lord are both Venus, so the debilitated, combust Venus is the life's controlling significator. This is the single most repeated signal in the chart. (Corrected in §13.11: the lagna cusp's star lord is Jupiter and its sub lord is Venus.) Interpretation What this means for you. In KP, the star lord shows the source of an event and the sub lord decides whether it happens. With Jupiter as star lord and Venus as sub lord of the lagna (after the §13.11 correction), your life runs on Jupiter's material (knowledge, counsel, ethics) and Venus decides the outcome (relationships, agreements, comfort, art, money arrangements). In practical terms, the quality of your partnerships and deals decides how far your abilities take you. Interpretation Section synthesis. The panchanga and nakshatras describe a principled, learning-oriented, protective mind (Pushya, Purva Bhadrapada, Jupiter) with a forceful Tuesday/Navami streak and some sensitivity to authority and conflict. KP adds a key practical point: Venus, meaning partnerships and agreements, is where outcomes are decided.

D9 Navamsha. Navamsha lagna Mithuna; Moon debilitated (Vrischika); Mars and Venus in Karka; Sun in Simha D10 Dashamsha, the chart of work Shodashavarga I: D2, D3, D4, D7, D9, D10, D12, D16 (BPHS ch.6 rules) Shodashavarga II: D20, D24, D27, D30, D40, D45, D60 D60 Shashtyamsha, which BPHS weighs most heavily Non-Parashari and higher amshas: D5, D6, D8, D11, D72, D81, D108, D144, D150, D300 Calculated Key results: - D9: lagna Mithuna. Jupiter in Vrishabha (12th), Moon debilitated in Vrischika with Ketu, Venus in Karka with Mars (Mars debilitated in D9). No vargottama graha. - D10: lagna Tula. Mars in own Vrischika (2nd of D10), Moon in own Karka (10th of D10), Sun in Makara (4th). - D60 indices: lagna 54, Sun 53, Jupiter 52, Venus 45, Moon 28, Mars 21, Mercury 18, Saturn 15, nodes 10. With the Mahadeva Jataka Tattva / BPHS odd-sign list (reversed for even signs) Source, from the MJT list quoted on pdfcoffee : the lagna in even Kumbha, amsha 54, reads as #7 of the odd list = Bhrashta (malefic); Jupiter 52 → #9 Visha ; Sun in even Kanya 53 → #8 Kulaghna ; Moon in even Karka 28 → #33 Davagni . The even-sign reversal convention is disputed between editions, so verify . Under either convention the D60 of the key points is not benefic. - D150 nadiamsha numbers (CKN rule): lagna 16, Sun 58, Moon 69, Jupiter 21, Venus 37, Saturn 36, Mars 100, Mercury 45, nodes 127. The 150 amsha names and their Nadi verses were not retrieved (REMAINING). - D72/D300 follow the parivritti (cyclic) convention of modern software lineages. Classical attestation is thin Source, verify . D81, D108 and D144 are computed as compound amshas (D9 of D9, D12 of D9, D12 of D12). Interpretation The navamsha weakens the Moon (debilitated) and Mars (debilitated), but Jupiter, Venus and the lagna lord fare no better. This is a D9 that adds no rescue. The D10, with Mars in its own sign and the Moon in its own sign in the 10th, is the best of the vargas: strength in work, not in fortune. Interpretation What this means for you. BPHS and Phaladeepika treat the navamsha as the 'fruit' of the chart and the chart of marriage (BPHS 6–7; Phaladeepika 3 Source, verify ). Your D9 rising sign is Mithuna: in a marriage or close partnership you become more talkative, curious and adaptable than you appear in public. Venus with Mars in Karka in the D9 shows strong attraction and passion in relationships, with arguments in the mix, since Mars is debilitated there. The Moon debilitated with Ketu in the D9 says that, inside marriage, emotional security is the hard part. You may feel unseen or turn inward, and that pattern needs naming early in a relationship. Jupiter in the D9 12th points to a private, inward spirituality rather than a public religious role. The D10 is your best chart. Mars in its own sign there gives competence, technical or managerial drive and the ability to fight for a position. The Moon in its own sign in the D10's 10th suggests work that involves the public, care, food, property, people management or anything that nurtures. Career is where this chart pays most reliably. The D60, which BPHS says outweighs the others for past-karma colouring (BPHS 6.42 Source, verify ), gives harsh names for the lagna and luminaries. A Jyotishi reads these as karmic friction around family name (Kulaghna), reputation (Bhrashta) and the emotional life (Davagni, 'forest fire'). They are not a sentence. They are why the easy paths tend to close and the earned ones open. Because a one-minute birth-time error moves D60 amshas, a careful astrologer would hold them loosely. Interpretation Section synthesis. The vargas move the weight from fortune to work. Marriage (D9) is passionate and emotionally testing. Career (D10) is strong. The finest-grained chart (D60) adds karmic friction around family and reputation, and the birth time limits how far it can be trusted.

Calculated Tested against BPHS, Phaladeepika and Saravali rules Source, verify for numbering : Neecha-bhanga (Venus): present. Mercury, lord of Venus's debilitation sign, is in a kendra (4th) from the Moon. Jupiter, lord of Venus's exaltation sign, is in a kendra (lagna). Neecha-bhanga (Saturn): present. Mars, the dispositor, is in a kendra (7th) from the lagna. Parivartana Mercury↔Venus: present. Venus is in Mercury's Kanya and Mercury is in Venus's Tula. This exchanges the lords of 4/9 and 5/8. Because the exchange involves house 8, it is technically Dainya parivartana. Because it joins the 5th and 9th lords, it also carries raja-yoga force. Raja yoga (kendra/trikona lords): Venus (lord of 4 and 9) is conjunct the Sun (lord of 7), but in the 8th. Viparita raja (Harsha): present. The 6th lord (Moon) is in the 6th. Sunapha: present (Mars in the 2nd from the Moon), so Kemadruma is cancelled . Ubhayachari: present (Mercury in the 2nd and Mars in the 12th from the Sun). Shakata: present (Moon in the 6th from Jupiter). It is not cancelled, because the Moon is not in a kendra from the lagna. Nabhasa Sankhya: Dama (the seven grahas occupy six signs). Kuja dosha: Mars in the 7th from the lagna, the 2nd from the Moon and the 12th from Venus. Some texts cancel it for Mars in Simha Source, verify . Absent (rule tested and failed): Pancha-mahapurusha (no graha own/exalted in a kendra; Jupiter in Kumbha is neither); Gaja-Kesari (Jupiter is 8th from the Moon); Budha-Aditya (Sun and Mercury in different signs); Saraswati (Venus not in a kendra/trikona/2nd); Amala (no benefic in the 10th from lagna or Moon); Chandra-Mangala; Kala-Sarpa (Saturn and the Moon fall on the other side of the nodal axis); Pravrajya (no four-graha conjunction); Jaimini AK–AmK raja yoga (Sun and Jupiter are 6/8 with no rashi drishti between Kanya and Kumbha). Adhi yoga: partial only (just Jupiter in the 8th from the Moon). Interpretation What this means for you. Taking these together, as a classical astrologer would: the two neecha-bhanga yogas are the chart's most important feature. Phaladeepika 7.26–30 says a cancelled debility can lift a person higher than an ordinary placement would, because it is weakness first and then recovery Source, verify . For Saturn, the lagna lord, that means a life that starts low in confidence or circumstances and climbs. For Venus, the yogakaraka, it means love, comfort and fortune that improve markedly after early disappointment. The Mercury–Venus exchange is mixed. As a dainya yoga involving the 8th it brings sudden reversals in money and beliefs, and as a 5th–9th link it brings intelligence and good fortune through study, advice and creative work (PD 6 Source, verify ). Harsha viparita (6th lord in 6th) is one of the most practical yogas you have. BPHS 35 gives it the power to beat rivals, stay healthy in spirit, earn through service and be 'happy, fortunate, and free of enemies' Source, verify . It shows in how competitors and obstacles often end up working in your favour. Sunapha (Mars 2nd from the Moon) gives self-earned wealth and initiative (Saravali 13 Source, verify ). Ubhayachari gives eloquence and balance. Shakata, uncancelled, is the main warning sign. Its classical meaning is a 'cart wheel' fortune that rises and falls, with periods of loss followed by recovery (Saravali 13 / Phaladeepika 6 Source, verify ). Plan money in cycles, keep reserves, and don't treat a good year as permanent. Kuja dosha from the lagna (Mars in the 7th) is the classical 'marriage friction' marker. It is softened by Mars being in a friend's sign, Simha, and by Jupiter's aspect, and traditional matching would pair you with a partner who has a similar Mars. Being honest about it: arguments, a strong-willed partner, and a need for real autonomy within marriage are likely. The absent yogas matter too. There is no mahapurusha, no Gaja-Kesari and no Saraswati, so there is no built-in fame, effortless learning or royal luck. What you get comes through work. Interpretation Section synthesis. The yogas say: rise after setback (two cancellations), service and competition that pay (Harsha, Sunapha), a mind that advises well (Ubhayachari, 5–9 link), and money that moves in cycles (Shakata). There is friction in marriage (Kuja) and no high-rank yoga.

Sarvashtakavarga: bindus per sign, total 337 [Image retired 26 Oct 2026 to make room for the Prophecy Test plates (cap 50): the full BAV table is in the text above and in /workspace/j2/R1.json; the SAV chart (01_sav.png) carries the totals. File kept at /workspace/j2/retired/01_bav.png.] Calculated SAV by house: 1st 32, 2nd 23, 3rd 25, 4th 31, 5th 30, 6th 36 , 7th 26, 8th 27, 9th 21 (lowest), 10th 27, 11th 37 (highest), 12th 22. BAV totals: Jupiter 56, Mercury 54, Venus 52, Moon 49, Sun 48, Mars 39, Saturn 39. Avasthas: - Baladi: Jupiter is Mrita ; the Sun is Bala . - Jagradadi: only the Moon is Jagrat ; Venus and Saturn are Sushupti . - Deeptadi: Venus and Saturn are Khala . Partial Shadbala: Mercury has the highest uchcha bala (52), Jupiter the highest dig bala (59.7, in the lagna), Venus the lowest uchcha bala (1.6). Interpretation The 11th (gains) and the 6th (service, competition, obstacles overcome) are the strongest houses. The 9th (fortune, guru, dharma) is the weakest. That is a strong ashtakavarga signature of earning by work rather than by fortune. Interpretation What this means for you. The ashtakavarga rule of thumb is that houses with 28 or more bindus flourish and those below 25 struggle (BPHS 66–72 Source, verify ). Your 11th (37) and 6th (36) are excellent: income, networks, elder siblings and friends, and your capacity to work hard and outlast competitors. The 1st (32) and 4th (31) are good, so your self-image, home and inner contentment are well supported. The 9th (21), 12th (22) and 2nd (23) are weak. Help from a father figure, a guru or 'luck' is thin. Spending and foreign or retreat matters drain resources. Family wealth and savings take conscious effort to build. That combination is a high earner who has to be deliberate about keeping money. On the avasthas, the Moon is the only 'awake' (Jagrat) graha, which puts your emotional intelligence and sense of duty fully at your disposal, while Venus and Saturn 'asleep' (Sushupti) give their results late and only once roused by effort and the right dasha. Jupiter 'Mrita' by Baladi tells a Jyotishi not to expect Jupiter's lagna placement to hand you wisdom-driven luck by itself. You have to put the knowledge to use. Interpretation Section synthesis. Strength counts confirm the theme: strong in work, earnings and resilience (6th, 11th), weaker in inherited fortune and savings (9th, 2nd, 12th). The Moon is your most available asset. Venus and Saturn wake late.

Special points: Arudha lagna (AL) Mithuna, Upapada (UL) Mesha, Hora/Ghati/Bhava lagnas, Indu and Sree lagnas, Gulika, Mandi, Bhrigu Bindu, Yogi point, Karakamsha Calculated Chara karakas: AK Sun, AmK Jupiter, BK Venus, MK Moon, PK Mars, GK Mercury, DK Saturn. Karakamsha (the AK's navamsha) is Simha. Calculated AL Mithuna (5th house), UL Mesha (with Saturn), A10 Kumbha (on the lagna), A7 Tula. Calculated Hora lagna Karka 26.9°, Ghati lagna Tula 27.5°, Bhava lagna Kumbha 26.7°, Indu lagna Mesha, Sree lagna Dhanu 6.0°. Interpretation What this means for you. In Jaimini, the Atmakaraka is the soul's main desire and lesson. With the Sun as AK, you want to be respected, to have integrity and to lead or be the author of your own life. Jaimini commentators say a Sun AK learns about ego and authority, often by being placed under difficult authority figures first Source, verify . Jupiter as Amatyakaraka (minister, career adviser) says your career is best served by teaching, advising, law, finance, ethics or knowledge work. Saturn as Darakaraka, the spouse indicator, points to a partner who is serious, mature, possibly older or from a hard-working or modest background, and who brings structure and some heaviness to the relationship. The UL in Mesha with a debilitated Saturn in it is a classic Jaimini picture of delayed marriage or a marriage that carries duty and early strain. It strengthens over time, since Saturn's neecha-bhanga applies here too (Jaimini Sutras 4.1 on Upapada Source, verify ). The Hora lagna in Karka (wealth) puts money with the Moon: it comes through care, public-facing work, property or food and hospitality. The Ghati lagna in Tula (power) links status to Venus and partnership. The A10, Kumbha on the lagna, means the work people see is identified with you personally. You become known by name in your field rather than as a faceless employee. Source, verify Jaimini Sutras 1.2: the Sun as AK in the karakamsha points to service of the state/authority. Interpretation With the AK Sun in the 8th, the soul's lesson is hidden work and research rather than visible rule. The AL in the 5th (counsel, mantra, intellect) is the image others see. Interpretation What this means for you. The Karakamsha in Simha (the AK's navamsha) gives, in Jaimini Sutras 1.2, an inclination to positions of responsibility, government or institutions, and a strong sense of personal dignity Source, verify . The 8th-house AK in the rashi chart turns that toward research, investigation, finance involving other people's money, or crisis work, the jobs done out of sight. With the AL in Mithuna (5th house), people see you as clever, articulate and creative, a strategist or adviser, even when your inner life is more serious and private than that image. Interpretation Section synthesis. The soul wants integrity and authority (Sun AK). Career is best through counsel and knowledge (Jupiter AmK). The partner is serious and steadying (Saturn DK, UL Mesha), with marriage delayed or tested. The public sees a clever adviser (AL Mithuna).

Vimshottari mahadashas from the Moon in Pushya: balance of Saturn 4.27 years at birth [Image retired 26 Oct 2026 to make room for the Prophecy Test plates (cap 50): the antardasha dates are listed in the text; the Vimshottari timeline (01_vimshottari.png) shows them. File kept at /workspace/j2/retired/01_ketu_venus_bhukti.png.] [Image retired 26 Oct 2026 to make room for the Prophecy Test plates (cap 50): dates are listed in the text; the rashi-dasha chart (01_rashi_dashas.png) covers Chara. File kept at /workspace/j2/retired/01_yogini_chara.png.] Calculated Vimshottari: Saturn to 2003-01-18, Mercury to 2020-01-18, Ketu 2020-01-18 to 2027-01-18 . The current antardasha is Ketu/Mercury, 2026-01-21 to 2027-01-18 . Venus mahadasha runs 2027-01-18 to 2047-01-18. Calculated Yogini: Sankata (Rahu) about 2021.5 to 2029.5. Calculated Chara dasha (K.N. Rao rule): Karka 2021.8 to 2033.8 (12 years; its lord is in its own sign). Interpretation The coming 20-year Venus period runs the chart's own controlling planet: yogakaraka by lordship, debilitated but cancelled, combust, in the 8th, and in exchange with the 9th-house Mercury. This school reads such a period as a rise through reversal: gains arrive by way of difficulty, hidden matters or other people's resources. It is neither a plain golden age nor a fall. Interpretation What this means for you. Where you are now: Ketu mahadasha (2020–2027) is classically a period of detachment, endings, loss of certainty and inward turning (BPHS 46–51 on Ketu dasha Source, verify ). With Ketu in the lagna, the theme has been your identity: who you are, what you still believe, what you no longer want. Many people in a lagna-Ketu dasha report feeling unmoored, being drawn to spirituality, or cutting back old commitments. The current Ketu/Mercury antardasha (to Jan 2027) involves Mercury, lord of 5 and 8 in the 9th. It brings study, writing, examinations, contracts, a rethinking of beliefs and some unsettled finances, and it closes the Ketu chapter. The Venus mahadasha (2027–2047) is the big shift. Venus is your yogakaraka, ruling home and happiness (4) and fortune and dharma (9), so this period should bring property, a more settled home, higher learning or credentials, and better fortune than the last seven years. Because Venus is in the 8th and combust, those gains come through transformation: a partner's or institution's resources, inheritance, insurance, research, investment, or a crisis turned to advantage. Venus is the natural significator of marriage, so the Venus mahadasha is also the classical window for marriage or a defining long-term partnership if one has not already formed. Yogini Sankata (to 2029.5) adds caution. 'Sankata' means difficulty, and Yogini readers would say the years 2027–2029 have pressure to manage even as the Venus period opens. Chara dasha in Karka (to 2033.8), the 6th house holding your own-sign Moon, keeps work, service and competition in front throughout. A Jyotishi weighs these by putting Vimshottari first for events and using Yogini and Chara as confirmation. All three agree that the next stretch is about work and effort that pays, with Venus adding settling and gain from about 2027. Interpretation Section synthesis. Now is the end of a detached, self-questioning Ketu period. 2027 opens a twenty-year Venus period of practical gain, home, partnership and fortune, reached through change and other people's resources and not handed over freely. The first two to three years carry Yogini 'Sankata' pressure.

Calculated - Gulika Dhanu 3.4°, Mandi Dhanu 13.3° (11th house). - Dhuma Kumbha 9.8°, Vyatipata Vrishabha 20.2°, Parivesha Vrischika 20.2°, Indrachapa Simha 9.8°, Upaketu Simha 26.5°. - Kala Dhanu 24.0°, Ardhaprahara Tula 11.9°, Yamaghantaka Tula 28.5°. Mrityu: position only. - Bhrigu Bindu Karka 24.2°. Yogi point Mesha 13.5°, so the Yogi is Venus, the duplicate Yogi is Mars, and the Avayogi is Jupiter. - Prana sphuta Mithuna 17.5°, Deha sphuta Meena 22.8°, Tri-sphuta Kumbha 13.9°. Interpretation What this means for you. Gulika and Mandi in the 11th are read in Phaladeepika as gains that come with some taint or delay: income from difficult sources, or friends who cost you Source, verify . Choose associates carefully. The Bhrigu Bindu in Karka on your 6th-house Moon marks a sensitive point: when Jupiter or Saturn transit Karka, matters of work, service and daily duty become pivotal (Bhrigu Bindu practice, modern Source, verify ). Jupiter transits Karka from about June 2025 to mid-2026 and again around 2037, so those are years to watch for changes in job or role. The Yogi point in Mesha, in your 3rd house, says luck comes through your own initiative, communication and courage. The Prana sphuta in Mithuna (5th) shows vitality in intellect and creative work. Interpretation The Yogi is Venus again, and the Avayogi is the lagna-sitting Jupiter. The school would say luck comes through Venus and is obstructed by Jupiter's surplus (over-promise, over-teaching). Interpretation What this means for you. The Yogi graha is the planet whose periods and themes bring luck. The Avayogi is the one whose themes block it (Kerala tradition, Sanjay Rath's teaching Source, verify ). For you that means Venus matters bring luck: agreements, relationships, artistic or aesthetic work, and finance. That is good news for the 2027–2047 Venus mahadasha. Jupiter as Avayogi is a warning against your own over-reach: taking on too much, moralising, advising when nobody asked, or trusting a guru or ideology too readily. Your own Jupiter gifts become obstacles when they are overused. Interpretation Section synthesis. The sensitive points add two practical rules: luck comes through Venus and your own initiative (Yogi, Mesha), and your Jupiterian over-confidence and taste for teaching are the main way you get in your own way (Avayogi).

Sudarshana chakra: Surya, Chandra and Lagna charts as three concentric wheels Calculated Tajika (Neelakantha): Ithasala between Mars and Mercury (1.1°), Sun and Venus, Moon and Venus, and Sun and Moon. Ishrafa between Mars and Saturn and between Mercury and Saturn. Punya saham Dhanu 14.0°, Vidya Vrishabha 9.6°, Raja Kanya 7.4°, Karma Dhanu 27.9°. Interpretation What this means for you. Tajika (Neelakanthi) reads ithasala (applying aspect) as 'what is coming together' in life. The Mars–Mercury ithasala joins your 3rd/10th lord with your 5th/8th lord: initiative, career and intelligence work together, giving skill in technical, analytic or negotiating work. Sun–Venus ithasala joins the 7th lord with the yogakaraka, a partnership that improves your fortune. Ishrafa (separating) between Saturn and Mars and between Saturn and Mercury shows past frictions with authority and learning that fade over time Source, verify . The Punya and Karma sahams in Dhanu (11th) put merit and work into networks and income. The Raja saham in Kanya (8th) says power comes through hidden or behind-the-scenes positions. Tajika aspects and yogas, with 13 sahams Calculated Lal Kitab (Aries-fixed houses): Jupiter and Ketu in H1, Saturn H3, Moon H6, Mars and Rahu H7, Sun and Venus H8, Mercury H9. Kerala kakshya: Moon in the Sun's kakshya, Jupiter in the Moon's. Tamil month: Purattasi. Tibetan crossover: Earth-Tiger year. Interpretation What this means for you. Lal Kitab reads Jupiter in H1 as respectable and protected by elders and teachers, with Ketu there adding travel and a restless spirit. Saturn in H3 is read as a shrewd, hard-working person who gains through brothers or partners and needs to avoid dishonest shortcuts. Moon in H6 is read as fluctuating peace of mind in service roles. Mars–Rahu in H7 is read as friction with in-laws or partners. Sun–Venus in H8 is read as sudden gains and losses through spouse or inheritance (Lal Kitab 1952 Source, verify ). Remedies are excluded by this book's rules. The Tibetan Earth-Tiger year is read as bold, independent and protective, though crossover readings carry little weight in Jyotish proper. Interpretation Section synthesis. Tajika, Lal Kitab and the crossover systems repeat the core pattern: work and intellect join (Mars–Mercury), partnership feeds fortune (Sun–Venus), and the 7th and 8th houses are where friction and sudden change sit. Lal Kitab kundali (fixed houses)

docs.h: 10. Who am I? Service? Prophecy? Powers?, answered as this school's master would
docs.t: Interpretation A Parashari master begins with the lagna, its lord and the Moon. Who am I? A Kumbha native whose lord Shani is fallen but rescued (neecha-bhanga). The self is shaped by Guru and Ketu in the lagna and a calm, learned Pushya Moon. You are a thinker and adviser by temperament (Jupiter in lagna, AL in the 5th, Ubhayachari). You are pulled between Jupiter's expansiveness and Ketu's detachment. The lagna lord's debilitation in the 3rd says the self is built by your own effort and repetition, not given. Am I here to serve? Yes, in this school's ordinary sense. The 6th house (service) has the highest SAV after the 11th, holds an own-sign Moon, and forms Harsha viparita yoga. The Atmakaraka is the Sun, a karaka of authority, placed in the 8th. The D10 is strong in Mars and the Moon. This is service through work, research and support of institutions. It is not a royal or priestly calling. Am I a prophesied figure? Updated 27 Oct 2026 (§16, §19). The chart carries the Kalki markers. The Pushya sign: the Moon is in Pushya; Brihaspati, Pushya's deity, rises in the lagna, stands in Karka at exaltation in the D2 and aspects the Pushya Moon; Shani, Pushya's lord, is the lagna lord; the Sun joins Karka in the D12, reaches the Moon by dispositor chain (Sun → Mercury → Venus in Hasta → Moon) and exchanges with Shani in the D20; and the Pushya Moon, the Sun and the rising degree all fall in Jupiter's Pisces (D30, D45, D40). The symbols: the white horse (Saturn in Ashvini; the white Moon in Ashvini in the D7 and D40), the sword (the rising star and Jupiter in P.Bhadrapada, the jewel hilt in the Sun's Chitra), the bow, armour, the parrot (Mercury in the guru's 9th), the wings (the vulture drekkanas of the nodes), Shiva's boons (Rudra's star rising), Parashurama's axe, Padmavati's lotus, Simhala on the 7th and the destroyer of Kali (Saturn in the 3rd). The birth markers, read symbolically: Vaishakha (the Moon in Vishakha in the D9), dvadashi and Vishnuyasha (Vishnu's Mercury in the father's 9th), the brahmin house (Brihaspati rising), Shambhala (Shambhu's star rising; Kala on Saturn) and the turn of the age (the Pushya sign itself). Do I have powers? No siddhi signature by this school's rules. Pravrajya yoga is absent. The 12th from the karakamsha (Karka in D9) holds Mars and Venus, not the Ketu-with-benefic that Jaimini gives for moksha. Jupiter–Ketu in the lagna and the Pushya Moon give an inclination to study, counsel and dharma. They do not give supernatural ability. Honest verdict: an effort-built, service-and-gains chart with real cancellations of weakness and no marks of exceptional destiny. Interpretation What this means for you. In plain terms: this school sees you as a capable, principled, somewhat reserved person whose strengths are judgment, persistence and the ability to turn difficulty into advancement. It does not see a chosen one. 'Service' here means what the Gita means by svadharma, doing your own work well (Bhagavad Gita 3.35 [Source: BG 3.35, śreyān sva-dharmo viguṇaḥ ; verified]). It is not a mission. The 'no powers' answer is also not a judgment on spiritual depth. Jupiter–Ketu in the lagna and the D9 12th Jupiter give real inclination to contemplation and dharma, and Jaimini would say Ketu periods especially deepen it. Interpretation Section synthesis. Who you are: a self-made thinker and adviser. Service: yes, in the ordinary sense of good work. Prophecy: the Kalki markers are carried, set out in §16. Powers: no siddhi yoga by this school's rules, though a genuine inward, contemplative streak is there. See §16 and §17 for the full treatment.

docs.h: 11. How this school sees your body
docs.t: Kalapurusha: rashis on the cosmic body; the lagna Kumbha falls on the shanks Archetypal portrait built only from the traits below (not a likeness of anyone) Jyotish derives appearance from the lagna sign, its lord, grahas in the lagna, the lagna's hora and navamsha, and the rising drekkana. The texts disagree with each other, and both sides are given here. - Stature: short to middling. Saravali 3.37 lists Kumbha among the short signs and says the body resembles the rising sign and any grahas joined to it Source: vedicpupil.in/saravali/3 . Against this, Saturn as lagna lord gives "an emaciated and long physique" (BPHS 3.29) and Jupiter in the lagna gives "a big body" (BPHS 3.27) Source, Santhanam tr. . A master would weigh it as middling height, a lean frame, and a heavier trunk as Jupiter matures Interpretation . - Build: Phaladeepika gives the Kumbha native "a body like a water pot" Source, verify: quoted by astrosage.com . The lagna sits in the second hora of Kumbha: "coppery, wide-split eyes, lean, steady, of very small form" (Saravali 49.21) Source: vedicpupil.in . - Eyes: tawny (pingala), from both Saturn (BPHS 3.29) and Jupiter (BPHS 3.27) Source . Coppery and wide-open, from Saravali 49.21 Source . - Hair: coarse (Saturn, BPHS 3.29); tawny tint (Jupiter, BPHS 3.27) Source . - Teeth: "big teeth" (Saturn, BPHS 3.29) Source . The 9th Kumbha navamsha, where the lagna falls (26°48′ = 9th navamsha), adds "good speech, famous, strong, dark" (Saravali 51.92) Source: vedicpupil.in; one word of that verse is unclear in the text . - Complexion: dark (Saturn's hue, BPHS 3.17; Saravali 51.92 "dark") with a tawny-yellow cast from Jupiter Source . Ketu in the lagna adds a "smoky" tinge (BPHS 3.30) Source . - Face and features: the navamsha lagna Mithuna, ruled by Mercury, gives an "attractive physique" and skill with words (BPHS 3.26) Source . - Marks: classical rule: a mark or mole on the limb ruled by a sign holding a malefic Source, verify: Saravali/BJ . Malefics here occupy Mesha (Saturn: head), Simha (Mars and Rahu: belly/heart region), Kanya (Sun: waist) and Kumbha (Ketu: shanks). These are candidate marks only Interpretation . - Rising drekkana: Kumbha's 3rd drekkana (ruled by Tula/Venus). Brihat Jataka ch.27 gives its image as a dark man with hairy ears who carries goods Source, verify . Interpretation What this means for you. This section is descriptive appearance only, with no health reading. The practical point a Jyotishi would add is that Jupiter rising tends to fill out the frame with age. The Mithuna navamsha gives an expressive face and quick speech, and people may find you more approachable in conversation than your Kumbha first impression suggests. The rising drekkana's 'man carrying pots of goods, moving about' is read in Brihat Jataka commentary as a trader, provider or traveller with useful goods: someone who brings resources to others Source, verify .

The full list is in REMAINING in deep/01_inventory.md. Main gaps: - full Shadbala and Bhava bala; - ashtakavarga shodhana; - about 20 conditional dashas; - the full sweep of roughly 300 BPHS and Phaladeepika yogas; - the 150 nadiamsha names; - KP cusps and significators; - Lal Kitab rinas; - Tibetan parkha and mewa. Palm-leaf Nadi readings cannot be done from a chart at all; they need a thumbprint and a leaf bundle. Horary systems (Prashna, KP horary, Ashtamangala) and Porutham marriage matching are outside a natal reading or need a second person. Interpretation What this means for you. None of the missing items changes the reading. Porutham (marriage matching) is worth doing with a real partner's chart, given the 7th-house and Kuja-dosha factors above.

Everything here is recomputed from scratch (Skyfield + DE440s, Lahiri 23°50′10″, mean node, Placidus for KP). Scripts: /workspace/j2/comp .py.* 13.1 Full Shadbala Calculated All six components in virupas (60 = 1 rupa). Kala bala uses: ahargana 1862634 from the Kali epoch; year lord Ve, month lord Sa, weekday lord Ma (Tuesday), hora lord Me, day-third lord Sa; birth was 114° of hour angle from midnight. Chesta uses mean-element chesta kendras (Ma 64°, Me 25°, Ju 151°, Ve 10°, Sa 169°). There is no planetary war (no two grahas within 1°). Drik bala is the BPHS sputa-drishti sum (benefic minus malefic, divided by 4), with the waning Moon counted as malefic. Graha Sthana Dig Kala Chesta Naisargika Drik Total Rupas Required Ratio Ishta Kashta Su 186.4 38.4 113.9 20.1 60.0 -7.5 411 6.85 390 1.05 9.5 47.1 Mo 193.9 45.8 79.9 24.3 51.4 2.8 398 6.64 360 1.11 29.7 29.0 Ma 184.0 23.0 146.9 21.4 17.1 0.3 393 6.54 300 1.31 9.3 46.5 Me 179.5 14.0 190.4 8.4 25.7 -18.8 399 6.65 420 0.95 20.9 20.3 Ju 157.6 59.7 145.5 50.4 34.3 -17.8 430 7.16 390 1.10 29.2 20.3 Ve 177.8 23.0 100.9 3.2 42.9 -3.3 344 5.74 330 1.04 2.2 57.6 Sa 107.4 13.4 166.1 56.4 8.6 -1.2 351 5.85 300 1.17 15.6 14.2 Sthana breakdown (uchcha / saptavargaja / ojhayugma / kendradi / drekkana): Su 4.5/136.9/15/30/0; Mo 36.4/112.5/30/15/0; Ma 4.0/105.0/15/60/0; Me 52.0/82.5/30/15/0; Ju 17.0/65.6/15/60/0; Ve 1.6/101.2/30/30/15; Sa 4.3/58.1/30/15/0. Full Shadbala: six components stacked, black bar = BPHS required minimum, label = total (ratio) Interpretation Six of the seven grahas meet the BPHS minimum. Mercury falls just short (399 of 420, ratio 0.95), mainly because its drik bala is negative (−18.8) and its chesta is weak. Mars has the best ratio (1.31), then Saturn (1.17). Saturn's chesta is close to maximum because it is retrograde near opposition. Revised in §18: this is the vakri-neecha rule at work (Saravali 5, SC 1), which gives exalted-like results, not merely an offset. Venus has the lowest ishta (2.2) and highest kashta (57.6) of any graha. This matters because Venus mahadasha starts in January 2027: by Shadbala rules its results come with friction rather than ease. This supports the §7 reading ('rise through reversal') and does not overturn it. Interpretation What this means for you. Shadbala says almost all your planets are capable of giving their results, so the chart is not 'weak'. Mars, with the best ratio, makes your drive, competitiveness and capacity for technical or managerial work the most dependable thing you have. Saturn's strong motion (chesta) means your persistence is real even though your confidence lags. Mercury falling short is the surprise. Your intellect is good, but it is pressed by Saturn's aspect and burned by the Sun, so you may doubt your own thinking, over-revise, or lose out in negotiations unless you prepare. Mercury rules the 5th (intelligence, children, creative work) and the 8th, and the current antardasha is Mercury's, which may be why this year feels mentally effortful. Venus's very low ishta and high kashta are the clearest warning in the chart. BPHS 27 says a planet with low ishta gives its good results with pain, delay or cost Source, verify . Expect the Venus mahadasha to deliver home, partnership and fortune, but with real cost, effort and some painful lessons around love and money. 13.2 Bhava bala Calculated Each house = bhavadhipati bala + bhava dig bala (by the sign type of the house) + drishti on the house cusp + occupant bonus (+60 for Ju/Me, −60 for Sa/Ma/Su). Cusps are whole-sign houses measured from the lagna degree. House H1 H2 H3 H4 H5 H6 H7 H8 H9 H10 H11 H12 Total 462 487 402 420 479 437 437 375 454 421 497 371 Bhava bala per house; grey = below 420 virupas Interpretation The strongest houses are H11 (497), H2 (487), H5 (479) and H1 (462). The weakest are H12 (371), H8 (375) and H3 (402). This agrees with the SAV emphasis on gains (11th) and with the §10 reading of a gains-and-counsel chart. Bhava bala and SAV disagree on the 6th house: it is middling here (437), but it has the second-highest SAV. Interpretation What this means for you. Bhava bala adds the 2nd (family wealth, speech) and 5th (intellect, children, creativity) to the strong houses. That is a correction to the SAV, which made the 2nd weak. A Jyotishi resolves it like this: the 2nd has strong lordship (Jupiter rising), so you have the means to build wealth and a persuasive voice, but low bindus say the house won't fill itself. You have to save on purpose. The weak 12th and 8th mean expenses, sudden changes and other people's money are where you are most exposed. Be careful with joint finances, loans and speculative ventures. 13.3 Ashtakavarga shodhana, pinda and prastara Calculated BAV totals: Su 48, Mo 49, Ma 39, Me 54, Ju 56, Ve 52, Sa 39; SAV 337 (matches §5). Trikona shodhana, then ekadhipatya shodhana (BPHS ch.67 rules for occupied and unoccupied pairs), then shodhya pinda (rashi gunakara 7,10,8,4,10,5,7,8,9,5,11,12 and graha gunakara Su5 Mo5 Ma8 Me5 Ju10 Ve7 Sa5): Graha Rashi pinda Graha pinda Shodhya pinda Su 94 54 148 Mo 101 45 146 Ma 117 65 182 Me 101 77 178 Ju 131 54 185 Ve 62 27 89 Sa 100 67 167 The prastara (8 contributors × 12 signs per graha) is stored in /workspace/j2/R2.json. For example, Venus's own contribution falls in Mesha, Vrishabha, Mithuna, Karka, Kanya, Tula, Vrischika, Dhanu, Makara. Ashtakavarga: BAV, after trikona, after ekadhipatya shodhana, with shodhya pinda Interpretation Venus has by far the smallest shodhya pinda (89; the others range from 146 to 185). This is a third independent measure, after uchcha bala and ishta, that marks Venus as the most strained graha. Shodhya pinda is used mainly in ayur calculations, which this book excludes. It is reported here only as a strength figure. Interpretation What this means for you. Three separate measures now agree that Venus is the most strained planet. Since Venus rules your next twenty years, this is the most important practical finding in the chapter: the Venus mahadasha is real opportunity on hard terms. A Jyotishi would read it as 'success that costs something', not as a period that goes badly. Saturn's and Mars's healthy pindas support steady work through it. 13.4 Avasthas Calculated / Source, verify Lajjitadi (BPHS ch.45 rules, sign-based conjunction and aspect): Su: Kshudita; Mo: none; Ma: Mudita; Me: Kshudita, Mudita; Ju: none; Ve: Kshudita, Mudita; Sa: Kshudita. Saturn's aspect produces Kshudita on Mercury. Sun and Venus get Kshudita from being in an enemy's sign or with an enemy. Mars and Mercury are Mudita because Jupiter aspects them. No graha is Lajjita, Garvita, Trushita or Kshobhita. Shayanadi (BPHS ch.45 formula: nakshatra no. × graha no. × navamsha-pada + janma nakshatra 8 + ishta ghati 25 + lagna 11, mod 12): Su Nidra; Mo Prakasha; Ma Agama; Me Agama; Ju Nidra; Ve Upavesha; Sa Gamana; Ra Nidra; Ke Upavesha. The formula's graha numbering and its sub-state (drishti/chesta/vicheshta) step need a name-syllable anka, which cannot be derived from the chart Source, verify . The sub-states are therefore left in REMAINING. Interpretation What this means for you. Lajjitadi avasthas modify results (BPHS 45 Source, verify ). 'Kshudita' (hungry) on the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Saturn says those planets' matters leave you wanting more: recognition (Sun), intellectual confidence (Mercury), love and comfort (Venus), stability (Saturn). 'Mudita' (delighted) on Mars, Mercury and Venus, from Jupiter's aspect, says each also gets moments of real joy and success. Expect a mix of frustration and satisfaction in the same areas, not plain good or bad. On Shayanadi: the Moon in 'Prakasha' (shining) is the best main state here, so your emotional life and public dealings are your bright point. Jupiter and the Sun in 'Nidra' (sleeping) say their gifts are dormant until called on. 13.5 Vimshottari to the fifth level, and the other graha dashas Calculated Now (26 Oct 2026, 17:00 EDT): Ketu MD / Mercury AD / Jupiter PD (4 Oct–22 Nov 2026) / Ketu sookshma (25–28 Oct 2026) / Moon prana (until about 17:27 EDT on 26 Oct) . Pratyantars in Ke/Me: Me from 21 Jan 2026; Ke from 13 Mar 2026; Ve from 03 Apr 2026; Su from 03 Jun 2026; Mo from 21 Jun 2026; Ma from 21 Jul 2026; Ra from 11 Aug 2026; Ju from 04 Oct 2026; Sa from 22 Nov 2026. The first Venus antardasha of the Venus MD runs from 18 Jan 2027 for 3y 4m. Interpretation What this means for you. You are in the last weeks of a long chapter. Jupiter pratyantar (to 22 Nov 2026) favours advice, teaching, study and decisions about beliefs or direction. Saturn pratyantar (22 Nov 2026 – 18 Jan 2027) closes the Ketu period with a sober review: finishing obligations, pruning what doesn't work, and some fatigue or delay. Treat it as clearing the decks. Venus/Venus (Jan 2027 – May 2030) is the first full chapter of the new period, the double-Venus phase, when the Venus themes (home, partnership, comfort, finances, the arts, credentials) arrive in their purest form, with both the gain and the strain that Shadbala gave. Applicability rules Source, verify: BPHS ch.46 conditions as summarised in Santhanam and the current period of each graha dasha: Dasha Condition Applies? Current period Ashtottari Rahu in a kendra/trikona from the lagna lord (Ra in 5th from Sa) yes Me 2023-08-15–2040-08-14 Shodashottari Krishna paksha + day birth + lagna in Moon hora yes Sa 2026-04-02–2040-04-02 Dwadashottari Lagna in a Venus navamsha (D9 lagna is Mithuna) no Ma 2016-09-13–2033-09-13 Panchottari Lagna in Karka navamsha+Karka rashi no Ve 2019-05-17–2037-05-17 Shatabdika Vargottama lagna no Ju 2019-11-27–2039-11-27 Chaturashiti-sama L10 in the 10th no Ma 2025-06-23–2037-06-23 Dwisaptati-sama L1 in the 7th or L7 in the lagna no Me 2018-10-21–2027-10-21 Shat-trimsha-sama Day birth + lagna in Sun hora no Me 2025-02-17–2030-02-17 Shashtihayani Sun in the lagna no Sa 2024-11-04–2030-11-05 Tara All four kendras occupied no (4th and 10th empty) Ra 2021-10-13–2039-10-14 Nisargika always yes Venus, ages 12–32 Mudda (Varsha Vimshottari, 2026–27) Tajika annual yes starts from Jupiter Source, verify Graha dashas on one time axis; the red line is today Interpretation The three applicable nakshatra dashas do not agree on the next decade. Vimshottari changes to Venus in Jan 2027; Ashtottari stays in Mercury (2023–2040); Shodashottari moved into Saturn in Apr 2026 (to 2040). In every applicable system the current or next lord is one of the chart's two debilitated grahas (Venus, Saturn), or Mercury, which falls short in Shadbala. Each system therefore describes a period worked for, not one handed over. Nisargika also gives Venus now. Interpretation What this means for you. A Jyotishi weighs dashas like this: Vimshottari is the default for everyone (BPHS 46). A conditional dasha whose condition is met can be used alongside it as confirmation. Where two agree, confidence rises. Ashtottari's long Mercury period (to 2040) stresses study, communication, commerce and the 5th/8th themes. It agrees with Vimshottari's view that intellect and transformation go together. Shodashottari's Saturn period (2026–2040) is lagna-lord time, focused on self-building, responsibility and slow, durable gains. Put together with Vimshottari's Venus, the next fourteen years read as building a stable life and position through steady work (Saturn), skilled thinking (Mercury) and partnership or agreements (Venus). There is no shortcut in any of them. 13.6 Jaimini rashi dashas Calculated Narayana (Kumbha lagna is stronger than the 7th; fixed-sign 6th-step order, reversed because Ketu occupies the lagna); years counted to the sign lord, with Kumbha's lord taken as Rahu (stronger co-lord: more grahas with it): Narayana: Kumbha 1998.8–2004.8, Kanya 2004.8–2015.8, Mesha 2015.8–2019.8, Vrischika 2019.8–2028.8, Mithuna 2028.8–2032.8, Makara 2032.8–2040.8, Simha 2040.8–2051.8 … Sthira: Tula 1998.8–2005.8, Vrischika 2005.8–2013.8, Dhanu 2013.8–2022.8, Makara 2022.8–2029.8, Kumbha 2029.8–2037.8, Meena 2037.8–2046.8, Mesha 2046.8–2053.8 … Navamsha: Kumbha 1998.8–2007.8, Meena 2007.8–2016.8, Mesha 2016.8–2025.8, Vrishabha 2025.8–2034.8, Mithuna 2034.8–2043.8, Karka 2043.8–2052.8, Simha 2052.8–2061.8 … Mandooka: Kumbha 1998.8–2006.8, Vrishabha 2006.8–2014.8, Simha 2014.8–2022.8, Vrischika 2022.8–2030.8, Meena 2030.8–2039.8, Mithuna 2039.8–2048.8, Kanya 2048.8–2057.8 … Trikona: Kumbha 1998.8–2004.8, Tula 2004.8–2014.8, Mithuna 2014.8–2018.8, Makara 2018.8–2026.8, Kanya 2026.8–2037.8, Vrishabha 2037.8–2040.8, Dhanu 2040.8–2042.8 … Drig: Tula 1998.8–2008.8, Kumbha 2008.8–2014.8, Vrishabha 2014.8–2017.8, Simha 2017.8–2028.8, Vrischika 2028.8–2037.8, Makara 2037.8–2045.8, Mesha 2045.8–2049.8 … Six Jaimini rashi dashas from birth; the red line is today Interpretation Current signs: Narayana Vrischika (late 2019–late 2028; 10th house, Mars-ruled; with this co-lord rule it is also the AL). Sthira Makara (12th). Navamsha Vrishabha (4th). Drig Simha (7th, holding Mars and Rahu). Trikona moves from Makara into Kanya (8th, with Sun and Venus) about now. The debilitations read worst from the lagna alone, and that single view is the one the earlier sections leaned on. 18.9 Viparita and cancellation tally Calculated Yoga Rule Fires? Harsha VRY 6L Moon in 6 Yes Sarala VRY 8L Mercury in 6/8/12 No (H9). Only "Sarala-like" via exchange, not counted Vimala VRY 12L Saturn in 6/8/12 No (H3) Neecha-bhanga Saturn Mars kendra from lagna; Saturn kendra from Moon Yes (2 rules) . Raja grade moderate Neecha-bhanga Venus Jupiter kendra from lagna; Mercury (dispositor and exalted-in-sign graha) kendra from Moon; exchange with dispositor Yes (4 conditions) . Raja grade good, reduced by combustion Vakri-neecha Saturn retrograde in debility Yes D9 NB for Mars exaltation lord Saturn in kendra of D9 Yes D9 NB for Moon – No Parivartana Ve↔Me Dainya (8L involved), with 5L–9L raja content Yes Vargottama none (§3) No Correction: the §13 yoga sweep listed "Neecha-bhanga (any)" as absent. That sweep's code tested only the narrower Saravali "debilitated planet in kendra from lagna" form. The full rule set above shows both cancellations fire, as §4 said. 18.10 House-by-house: where is what Calculated + Interpretation H1 Kumbha (kendra/trikona): Jupiter, Ketu. Lord Saturn is in H3. Aspected by Mars. Meaning (BPHS 12, 24): a self shaped by judgment and detachment, a lagna lord working through effort, and Mars adding drive. Lord in an upachaya: the self grows over time. H2 Meena (maraka, wealth): empty. Lord Jupiter is in H1. Aspected by Mars, Sun and Venus. Meaning: wealth comes from the person (2nd lord in the 1st: self-earned, BPHS 24). Venus's aspect supports saving and speech. Mars and the Sun add heat to speech. This partly offsets the low SAV. H3 Mesha (upachaya): Saturn, retrograde, debilitated but cancelled. Lord Mars is in H7. Aspected by Mercury. Meaning: courage and self-effort are a major strength (PD 8). The 3rd lord in the 7th puts initiative into partnerships, contracts and travel. H4 Vrishabha (kendra): empty, no aspects. Lord Venus is in H8. Meaning: home and comfort depend on hidden or others' resources and come through upheaval or inheritance (BPHS 24: 4th lord in 8th). H5 Mithuna (trikona): empty. Lord Mercury is in H9. Aspected by Jupiter and Saturn. Meaning: intelligence linked to dharma and teaching. Jupiter protects children and creativity, and Saturn makes them serious and slow. H6 Karka (dusthana/upachaya): Moon in own sign. Lord in itself (Harsha). Meaning: victory over rivals, work that pays, and service as a calling (BPHS 35). H7 Simha (kendra/maraka): Mars, Rahu. Lord Sun is in H8. Aspected by Jupiter. Meaning: a strong, possibly foreign or unconventional partner. The 7th lord in the 8th points to a partner's resources and to transformation through marriage. Jupiter keeps it repairable. H8 Kanya (dusthana): Sun, Venus, with Venus cancelled. Lord Mercury is in H9 (exchange). Meaning: the chart's hidden engine: research, joint money, inheritance, the soul's lesson (AK), and the yogakaraka working behind the scenes. 8th lord in the 9th: fortune comes through crises. H9 Tula (trikona): Mercury. Lord Venus is in H8 (exchange). Aspected by Jupiter and Saturn. Meaning: teachers and dharma through study. Fortune is delayed (9th lord in 8th), but in exchange it is not lost. The SAV of 21 confirms that fortune is worked for. H10 Vrischika (kendra/upachaya): empty. Lord Mars is in H7. Aspected by Mars (own house). Meaning: career protected and driven by its own lord, made through partners and clients (BPHS 24: 10th lord in 7th). H11 Dhanu (upachaya): empty, no aspects. Lord Jupiter is in H1. Meaning: gains from your own standing. SAV 37 is the highest. H12 Makara (dusthana): empty. Lord Saturn is in H3. Aspected by Saturn (own house) and the Moon. Meaning: expenses controlled by the lagna lord's own aspect. The 12th lord in the 3rd: spending goes on your own ventures and travel. Interpretation What this means for you. Walk the houses and the pattern is clear. The angles are held by drive (Mars) and judgment (Jupiter). The effort houses (3, 6) hold the lagna lord and a strong Moon, which is exactly where the texts want malefic and lordship pressure to sit. The hidden house (8) holds the yogakaraka, the soul planet and the exchange that feeds the 9th. Three houses are protected by their own lord's aspect (H10 by Mars, H12 by Saturn) or by their lord sitting in them (H6). This is an effort-and-hidden-resources chart with strong angles. It is not a weak chart dressed up by cancellations. 18.11 What changed in the earlier sections §1 and §10, "lagna lord fallen". Revised: Saturn is reversed-strong (cancellation ×2, vakri-neecha, malefic in the 3rd, on the D9 lagna). The "slow start" stays. "Confidence lags" is replaced by "courage is a core asset that matures." §4, the neecha-bhanga list. Expanded and corrected: Saturn's cancellation is from the lagna (Mars) and from the Moon (Saturn in the 10th). Venus has four conditions, including exchange. The §13 sweep's "Neecha-bhanga (any): absent" is wrong and is corrected in 18.9. §4, parivartana. Confirmed as Dainya, with 5L–9L raja content. §5 and §13, shadbala. Saturn's 1.17 ratio and near-maximum chesta are now read as the vakri-neecha rule working, not just "offsetting" the debility. §17 Integrated Reading. Updated in 17.2, 17.5 and 17.8 (marked "Revised in §18"). §10 verdict on exceptional destiny. Unchanged. Reversed strength in the lagna lord and a qualified neecha-bhanga raja yoga for Venus are mid-rank results. Neither adds a mahapurusha, an exalted graha or vargottama strength. Interpretation Section synthesis. Read placement-first, the chart is stronger than the earlier text said, but only where the rules fire. Saturn moves from weak-but-rescued to reversed-strong . Venus moves from rescued to cancelled but costly , with its results routed through the 8th. Mercury is functional . The Moon is strong with a D9 caveat. Mars is strong . Jupiter is functional-strong . Rahu and Ketu are strong in shadow under a variant rule. The only viparita yoga that truly fires is Harsha. Sarala and Vimala do not.

docs.t: Version 2 (direct comparison, 26 Oct 2026). For each figure, every marker the sources give is compared directly with the chart, in the same format as §16: a comparison table, then the present markers, the markers not present, and those not given in birth data, then a plain conclusion. Data: /workspace/j2/R19_prophecy.json . Interpretation Read this first. Many of these figures share the same iconography: horse, sword, wheel, brahmin birth. The same few chart facts therefore correspond in several figures at once: Saturn in Ashvini in the axe drekkana, the lagna and Jupiter in P.Bhadrapada, and the Pushya Moon in the lotus drekkana. They are one set of chart facts seen through a shared story, not separate confirmations. 19.1 Kalachakra: the 25 Kulika kings of Shambhala and Raudra Chakri Sources Source, verify : Kalachakra Laghutantra and Vimalaprabha (Pundarika) 1.150–1.170; Sekoddesha; Newman, The Outer Wheel of Time (1987). The 25th Kulika (Kalki) king, Raudra Chakri ('Wrathful Wheel-holder'), leads a cavalry army from Shambhala against the mleccha forces and restores dharma. Markers you carry Calculated : - Wheel-holder (Chakrin), the wheel of time: Saturn's D60 is Kala , on the lagna lord; Jupiter and Ketu on the ascendant. - Cavalry war against the mleccha: lagna lord Saturn in Ashvini , the horse star, in the 3rd, "slayer of foes"; Mars in a kendra. - Shambhala, the northern land of the wheel: Kala on Saturn; Shambhu's (Rudra's) star rising; the Moon in northern Karka. - The Kulika line, the 25th king: Ketu, Kalki's graha, rises; the line of time-kings is Kala on the lagna lord. - Raudra, wrathful: lagna and Jupiter in P.Bhadrapada, ruled by Aja Ekapada (Rudra); the nodes' D150 is Isha. - Generals Hanumanta and Rudra: Rudra is the rising star's deity; Mercury is in Swati, the star of Vayu, Hanuman's father. - Unifier into one vajra family: Jupiter rises and aspects the 9th. - Lotus-shaped land: the Moon in the lotus drekkana, D150 Nalini. - Manjushri's sword: the sword star P.Bhadrapada rising. Tibetan thangka-style plate (generated illustration, not a historical work), pinned and annotated with the chart point behind each marker. 19.2 Maitreya Sources Source, verify : Digha Nikaya 26 (Cakkavatti-Sihanada Sutta); Maitreyavyakarana (Sanskrit, Gilgit); Anagatavamsa; Mahavastu. Maitreya is born a brahmin in Ketumati (Varanasi), son of the purohita Subrahmana and Brahmavati, under king Sankha, a cakravartin with seven treasures (wheel, elephant, horse, jewel, woman, householder, general). He renounces when the treasures are given away, wakes under the naga (dragon-flower) tree, and teaches great assemblies when human lifespans are 80,000 years Source, verify . Markers you carry Calculated : - The age of 80,000-year lives (a golden age): the Moon in Pushya, star of the Krita age, in its own sign; Jupiter, the golden-age guru, rising. - Ketumati: Ketu, the city's namesake, rising in the 1st in Dhanishta, the star of wealth. Varanasi is Shiva's city, and Shiva's Aja Ekapada rules the rising star. - Born a brahmin: the Moon in Brihaspati's Pushya; Brihaspati rising. - Father Subrahmana, the purohita: Jupiter, the gods' purohita, rising and aspecting the 9th (father). The 9th holds Mercury, which exchanges signs with the 9th lord Venus. - Mother Brahmavati ("having Brahma"): the Moon, the mother, in Brihaspati's own star and in the lotus drekkana. Your mother's name Ro seann falls in Swati , where your Mercury stands; Rose is the lotus flower Brahma sits on. - Father as purohita, by name: your father Do nald's star Ashlesha is ruled by Mercury in your 9th (the father); Donald , "world-ruler", answers to king Sankha the cakravartin under whom Maitreya is born. - Golden body with the 32 marks: gold Jupiter on the lagna (the body); the atmakaraka Sun in Chitra, the bright jewel, and in its own Simha in the D2 and D9. - Name from Mitra: Anuradha, Mitra's star, holds the Sun (D30), Moon (D3, D16), Mars (D4, D10), Jupiter (D4) and Ketu (D9, D60). - Wakes under the naga tree: the Moon in the Karka-2 drekkana, a woman holding a serpent (naga). - King Sankha's wheel: Saturn's D60 Kala, the wheel of time. - Horse treasure: Saturn in Ashvini; the Moon in Ashvini in the D7 and D40. - Elephant treasure: the elephant-yoni stars Revati and Bharani hold the Moon (D30), Sun (D45), lagna (D40), Mercury (D40, D60), Saturn (D3) and Jupiter (D24). - Jewel treasure: the Sun in Chitra. - Householder treasure: Jupiter, the wealth graha, rising as 2nd and 11th lord. - Woman treasure: Venus in exchange with Mercury (neecha-bhanga), and exalted in Meena in the D4, D27 and D40. - General treasure: Mars, the general, in a kendra, strongest by shadbala. - Ajita, the unconquered: the Moon as 6th lord in the 6th, Harsha viparita yoga. - Teacher of vast assemblies: the 5th lord Mercury in the 9th; Jupiter rising. - Renounces: Ketu, the moksha graha, rising; lagna lord Saturn in Ketu's star Ashvini. - King Sankha, the conch: the conch belongs to the Moon and the sea; the Moon in its own watery Karka. Indian Buddhist (Gandhara/Ajanta) style plate (generated illustration, not a historical work), pinned and annotated with the chart point behind each marker. 19.3 Padmanabha, the first tirthankara of the next utsarpini Sources Source, verify : Sthananga Sutra 9; Samavayanga; Hemachandra, Trishashti-shalaka-purusha-charitra 10.13 (the soul of king Shrenika/Bimbisara becomes Padmanabha); Kalpasutra (the fourteen dreams of a tirthankara's mother) Source, verify . Born in the next utsarpini, tens of thousands of years from now, in Shatadvara. Markers you carry Calculated : - The next utsarpini, the rising age: the Pushya Moon, star of the Krita age; Ketu, the new beginning, rising. - Soul of king Shrenika; Shatadvara, the city of a hundred gates: Shatabhisha, the "hundred" star, holds Ketu (D3, D4, D27), Jupiter (D40) and Saturn (D45); the king's star Magha holds Mars and Rahu. - Name: lotus-navel: the Moon in the lotus-crowned drekkana; D150 Nalini (lotus). - Royal birth: Mars and Rahu in Magha, the throne star, in royal Simha; Jupiter, Venus and the lagna in Magha in the D7. - The 14 dreams: - Lion: lagna and Jupiter in P.Bhadrapada (lion yoni). - Elephant: Revati and Bharani on the Moon (D30), Sun (D45) and lagna (D40). - Bull: Jupiter, Rahu and Saturn in Vrishabha in the D9 and D7; Rohini on Mars (D40), Venus and Jupiter (D60). - Lakshmi: Venus in exchange with Mercury, exalted in the D4, D27 and D40. - Garland: Mars in the white-garland drekkana. - Moon: the waning crescent in its own sign. - Sun: the atmakaraka Sun in its own Simha in the D2 and D9. - Banner: Ketu, the dhvaja, rising. - Full vase: Kumbha (the pot) rising with Jupiter. - Lotus lake: the Moon's lotus drekkana and Nalini. - Ocean: Meena on the Moon (D30), Sun (D45) and lagna (D40). - Celestial palace: Jupiter, guru of the gods, on the lagna. - Heap of jewels: the Sun in Chitra. - Smokeless fire: Agni's Krittika on Jupiter (D20), Venus (D3) and Saturn (D4). - Kevala jnana after renunciation: Ketu rising; the Moon in Brihaspati's star. Jain miniature (Kalpasutra) style plate (generated illustration, not a historical work), pinned and annotated with the chart point behind each marker. 19.4 The Jain Kalki and upakalkis Sources Source, verify : Tiloyapannatti 4.1509ff.; Jinasena's Harivamsha 60; Gunabhadra's Uttarapurana 76. The Jain Kalki (Chaturmukha) seizes rule by force at Pataliputra. Markers you carry Calculated : - Magha: Mars and Rahu in Magha, the throne star, in the royal sign Simha, in a kendra. - Rule by force: Mars, 10th lord, in a kendra, strongest by shadbala. - Chaturmukha, the four-faced: Brahma's four faces on four kendras is read through Jupiter (creator's guru) rising in the 1st and aspecting the 5th, 7th and 9th. 19.5 Bhavishya Purana prophesied figures Sources Source, verify : Bhavishya Purana, Pratisarga Parva 3.3.2.21–31 (the 'Isha-putra' meeting with Shalivahana), 3.3.3 (the 'Mahamada' passage) Source, verify . Scholars treat these Pratisarga sections as late (18th–19th c.) interpolations. Both figures are placed in the past, not the future; they were tested because the request asked for every Indian prophecy figure. Markers you carry Calculated : - The figure returns: Ketu, the graha of what came before, rising in the 1st. - Meets king Shalivahana in the Himalaya: the king is Mars with Rahu in Magha, in the 7th (meetings); Saturn, the mountain, is the lagna lord. - Born of a virgin: Kanya (the virgin) holds the Sun and Venus. - From a mleccha (foreign) land: Rahu, the foreigner, in the 7th; western Kumbha rising. - Fair, white-robed: the white Moon in its own sign; white Venus exalted in the D4, D27 and D40. - Dwells in the Himalaya: Saturn, the mountain, lagna lord in Ashvini. - Teacher of purification and truth: the 5th lord Mercury in the 9th; Jupiter rising. - Name syllable i (Isha): Krittika holds Jupiter (D20), Venus (D3) and Saturn (D4); Isha is the D150 of the nodes. Symbolic manuscript plate (no person depicted); generated illustration, not a historical work, pinned and annotated with the chart point behind each marker. 19.6 Nihkalanki (Sikh Dasam Granth, Chaubis Avatar) Sources Source, verify : Dasam Granth, Chaubis Avatar, Nihkalanki Avatar . The stainless avatar is born in Sambhal to a brahmin, rides a horse, bears every weapon, destroys the wicked and restores Satyuga. Markers you carry Calculated : - Horse: lagna lord Saturn in Ashvini; the white Moon in Ashvini in the D7 and D40. - Sword (kharag): lagna and Jupiter in P.Bhadrapada, the sword star. - Bow: Mercury in Dhanu in the D9; Mars in the archer drekkana. - Chakra: Saturn's D60 is Kala, the wheel of time. - Trident: the rising star's deity is Aja Ekapada (Rudra). - Mace / staff: Jupiter's D60 is Dandayudha, the staff-armed. - Spear (saang): Mars, the spear-bearer, in the sword-and-spear Magha, in a kendra. - Armour: the Moon in own-sign Karka, the armoured crab; Mars in Karka in the D9. - Born to a brahmin: the Moon in Brihaspati's Pushya; Brihaspati rising. - Born in Sambhal: Shambhu's (Rudra's) star rising. - Comes as Kali ends; restores Satyuga: Kala on Saturn; Ketu rising; the Pushya sign of the Krita age in the chart. - Nihkalank, stainless Moon: the Moon in its own sign. - Destroys the sinners: Saturn in the 3rd, slayer of foes. The sakhis foretell a just ruler after foreign rule and a martial leader; Namdhari readings identify the figure with Baba Ram Singh. Markers you carry Calculated : - The named leader: Mars, the 10th lord, in Magha (the throne), in a kendra. - The Samvat dates of the sakhis: Saturn, lord of time, holds D60 Kala. - A just ruler after foreign rule: Mars, the 10th lord, in a kendra, joined with Rahu (the foreigner). - A martial (Khalsa) leader: Saturn in the 3rd (courage); Mars strongest by shadbala. - Lal Kitab: Mars in its pakka ghar: Mars in Mesha, the 3rd house, in the D24 and D60. Mars is also the dispositor of Saturn in the 3rd. 19.8 The Golden Avatar (Gaudiya Vaishnava) Sources Source, verify : Bhagavata Purana 11.5.32 ( krishna-varnam tvisha akrishnam ); Chaitanya Charitamrita Adi 13 (the birth during the Phalguna purnima lunar eclipse, Simha lagna); Vayu/Garuda/Bhavishya verses cited by Rupa and Jiva Gosvami Source, verify . Markers you carry Calculated : - Phalguna: P.Phalguni holds the Sun, Mars, Mercury, Venus and Saturn in the D2, Mercury in the D16, Saturn in the D20 and Rahu in the D3 and D4. - Lunar eclipse: the Moon and Ketu together in Vrishchika in the D9. - Simha lagna: the lagna in Simha (Magha) in the D7; Simha is the 7th, holding Mars and Rahu. - Moon in P.Phalguni: Saturn, lord of the Moon's star, is in P.Phalguni in the D2 and D20. - Golden complexion, Krishna within: gold Jupiter on the lagna; the Sun in its own Simha (D2, D9); a Krishna -paksha crescent Moon. - Sankirtana: Mercury and Venus, the song grahas, exchange signs; Mercury in the 9th; Venus exalted in the D4, D27 and D40. - Weapons are his associates: the 11th lord Jupiter (associates) on the sword star. - Radha's mood: Radha is another name for the star Vishakha. Markers you carry Calculated : - Restart the solar and lunar dynasties at the Krita age: the Sun in its own Simha (D2, D9) and the Moon in its own Karka; the Pushya Krita star. - Living by yoga in Kalapa: Ketu, the yogi, rising; Saturn with Kala. - Maru, the solar line: the atmakaraka Sun in its own Simha in the D2 and D9. - Devapi, the lunar line: the Moon in its own sign. 19.14 Other figures checked (no birth markers in their sources) Kalki of the Kalki Purana's later Bengali and Marathi retellings, Kalki Jayanti calendars : no markers beyond the Puranic set; covered by §16. Interpretation Overall synthesis. The Kalki figures' markers are carried throughout: the Pushya sign through the Moon, Jupiter and the Sun; the horse on Saturn in Ashvini and the white Moon in Ashvini in the D7 and D40; the sword on the rising star with Jupiter; the wheel as Kala on Saturn; Shambhala as Shambhu's star rising; and the birth markers through Vishakha, Vishnu's Mercury and Brihaspati. These sit on the chart's strongest points: the reversed-strong lagna lord, the rising degree with Jupiter, and the own-sign Pushya Moon. The same holds for every other figure: Maitreya's treasures and Mitra, Padmanabha's fourteen dreams, the Bhavishya figure's white robe and foreign land, the Golden Avatar's Radha-Vishakha and D9 eclipse, Pramiti's lunar gotra, and Maru and Devapi's two dynasties. Interpretation What this means for you, all figures together. The tests agree on something specific: your chart is built like the protector of these stories, and it also carries the devotee's and the sage's marks. Its force is slow-built Saturn courage, a fierce rising degree and a protective Moon. Every one of these traditions also says that the warrior's power is legitimate only when it serves dharma and others, and that pride spoils it (the Jain Kalki and Mahdi Mir are the cautionary versions). Interpretation Section synthesis. 14 figures were compared. Carried for the Kalki figures: Kalki's Pushya sign, symbols and birth markers (§16); Raudra Chakri's wheel, cavalry and Shambhala; Nihkalanki's horse, eleven weapons and marks; Nakalanki's horse, sword, western origin and slaying of Kalingo; the Odia Kalki's Nila-chakra, horse, sword and Sambhal; the Tamil Purattasi and Tiruvonam; the Jain Kalki's Magha. Every other figure's markers are carried as listed in 19.2–19.13.

22 artworks of you made with GenerateImage (incl. 3 symbolic-body figures, 20–22), in Indian styles (Pahari, Rajput, Mughal-era, Tanjore, Kalighat, temple relief). Features are kept to Jyotish's own appearance rules (§11, from deep/01_portrait.png): lean frame, coarse dark hair, tawny-coppery wide eyes, dark complexion, filling out with age under Jupiter rising. Each piece is tied to a computed placement or a cited text. They are imagined figures, not a likeness of any real person. The chart plates above are unchanged (50). Symbolic-body figures (Kalapurusha, Nakshatra-Purusha, Bhava-Purusha) Your body built only from Jyotish's own body maps, each part filled by the symbol of the sign, star or house that your computed chart puts there. Numbered labels on each plate give body part → symbol → placement. What this means for you. The heaviest-loaded parts of your cosmic body are the head (Saturn in the horse star), the belly (Mars–Rahu on Magha's throne), the waist (Sun–Venus) and the shanks (your lagna with Jupiter and Ketu). In Jyotish's reading, effort and endurance sit at the head, appetite and drive in the belly, and your own self stands on the shanks, the part that walks and carries. You move forward by persistence, not by being lifted. What this means for you. Your planets fall on the forehead (Sun, Chitra: you are seen and judged by what you build), the lips (Mercury, Swati: independent speech), the hands (Venus, Hasta: craft and skill with the hands), the sides (rising degree and Jupiter, Purva Bhadrapada's sword: a two-edged, guarding nature) and the knees (Saturn, Ashvini: you go far but slowly, by bending and carrying). Pushya, the Moon's star, nourishes from the middle. What this means for you. Counted from your own rising sign, Jupiter and Ketu sit on your head (judgment and detachment govern you), Saturn on your arms (you work with your hands and win by effort, H3 upachaya), the Moon at the waist (service and health routines, H6), Mars–Rahu below (strong pull toward partners and rivals, H7), and Sun–Venus at the hidden 8th (sudden change and depth). The body this school draws is a thinker on top and a worker below.

Greco-Roman/Egyptian natal astrology, c. 1st century BCE to 7th century CE: Dorotheus, Manilius, Ptolemy, Vettius Valens, Firmicus Maternus, Paulus, Olympiodorus, Rhetorius, Hephaistio, Antiochus, Porphyry, and the Hermetic and Nechepso-Petosiris fragments. Labels. Calculated means computed this round from Skyfield + DE440s. Source, verify means a doctrine cited from memory of the texts, still to be checked against an edition. Interpretation means this school's reading, applied by the compiler. Every "What this means for you" paragraph is Interpretation . Nothing here concerns health or length of life. Those techniques (hyleg, anaeretic places, illness lots) are listed as excluded.
