docs.h: 4. Albertus Magnus: Speculum astronomiae and De mineralibus, with the planetary stones
docs.t: Source, verified The Speculum astronomiae (attributed to Albertus, c.1260) defends licit astrology, meaning the judicial study of nativities, revolutions and elections. It separates this from image-magic, and it lists the approved authors: Ptolemy, Abū Maʿshar, Alchabitius, Messahallah and others. De mineralibus (Book II) discusses the powers of stones and their sigils. Planetary stones [Source, verified against Agrippa, De occulta philosophia I.23–29 and II.14, esotericarchives.com] : - Saturn: onyx, ziazaa, camonius, sapphire, brown jasper, chalcedony, loadstone - Jupiter: hyacinth, beryl, sapphire, tutia, emerald, green jasper ( correction: not topaz or amethyst) - Mars: diamond, loadstone, bloodstone, jasper, amethyst - Sun: aetites, eye of the sun, carbuncle, chrysolite, iris, heliotrope, hyacinth, pyrophilus, pantaura, topaz, chrysoprase, ruby, balas - Venus: beryl, chrysolite, emerald, sapphire, green jasper, carnelian, aetites, lapis lazuli, coral - Mercury: emerald, agate, red marble, topaz, mixed-colour stones - Moon: crystal, silver marcasite, selenite, pearls, beryl - Signs (II.14, scale of twelve): Aries sardonyx, Taurus carnelian, Gemini topaz, Cancer chalcedony, Leo jasper, Virgo emerald, Libra beryl, Scorpio amethyst, Sagittarius hyacinth, Capricorn chrysoprase, Aquarius crystal, Pisces sapphire ( correction: amethyst belongs to Scorpio, not Pisces) - Fixed stars (I.32): Regulus garnet, Spica emerald, Arcturus jasper, Algol diamond [Correction, checked online] Albertus's De mineralibus does not give a planet-by-planet stone list. Book II, tractate 2 is an alphabetical lapidary of stones and their virtues, and tractate 3 covers sigils (engraved astrological images) on stones (Wyckoff, Book of Minerals , 1967). The planetary lists above are Agrippa's. Planetary stones What this means for you: for this chart Agrippa's lists point to sapphire , which is both Jupiter's stone and the stone of Pisces, your rising sign. Hyacinth is the alternative for Jupiter. Emerald or beryl suits Venus in Libra, your second strength, and chrysolite suits the Sun in fall. This is symbolic jewellery, not medicine.

Source, verified Michael Scot (c.1175–c.1235) was court astrologer to Frederick II. He wrote the Liber introductorius , the Liber particularis and the Liber physiognomiae , and Dante places him among the diviners ( Inferno XX). His Liber introductorius gives the day-and-hour planetary rulerships and the "nature" of each planet in detail. Calculated You were born on a Tuesday (Mars's day), in the 11th planetary hour of the day, which is ruled by Mercury. Planetary hour What this means for you: Scot would say you are a Mercury-hour person born on a Mars day. That is quick speech on top of a fighting day. It agrees with the Mercury–Mars mutual reception: you argue well and fast.

docs.h: 6. Physiognomy: Scot's Liber physiognomiae, the Secretum secretorum and Lilly's planetary descriptions
docs.t: Source, verified Lilly, Pisces as Ascendant: "A short stature, ill composed, not very decent, a good large Face, palish Complexion, the Body fleshy or swelling, not very straight, but incurvating somewhat with the Head." Source, verified; corrected Lilly's Jupiter (CA Book I): "an upright, straight and tall Stature; brown, ruddy and lovely Complexion; of an ovall or long Visage, and it full and fleshy; high Forehead; large gray Eyes; his Hair soft, and a kind of aburn brown; much Beard". Your Jupiter is occidental of the Sun, so Lilly's variant applies: "A pure and lovely Complexion, the Stature more short, the Hair a light Brown, or neer a dark Flaxen; smooth, bald about the Temple or Forehead." (The earlier wording "honest look, good manners" was not Lilly's.) Lilly's Saturn: "middle stature; his complexion pale, swartish or muddy, his Eyes little and black, looking downward... black or sad Hair... his Shoulders broad". Your Saturn is oriental : "the stature is more short, but decent and well composed." (The earlier "heavier body" was wrong; Lilly's Saturn is cold and dry, with spare thighs.) The Secretum secretorum teaches that soft flesh signifies quick understanding and that a large, full face with mild eyes shows a peaceful nature. Scot's Liber physiognomiae treats mild, moist eyes as a sign of an honest and gentle temperament. Interpretation The composite portrait built from these texts: a large, full, pale face, large grey eyes, light-to-auburn brown hair (dark tones from Saturn), shorter-than-average but well-composed stature, and the head carried slightly inclined. Only these texts were used for the artworks; no real person was used. Physiognomy What this means for you: the old physiognomists would read you as gentle, open-faced and approachable. They would add a touch of gravity from Saturn: people trust you before you have said much.

Source, verified Girolamo Cardano (1501–1576) published Libelli quinque with a hundred example genitures (1547; enlarged 1554). He also published Ptolemy commentaries and Aphorismorum astronomicorum segmenta septem . Applicable aphorisms Source, verify, paraphrase : - "The benefic in the Ascendant in its own house makes a man fortunate even against bad directions." Calculated Jupiter is in Pisces on the Ascendant. - "Saturn in the Ascendant makes the native serious, slow, and long-meditating." Calculated Saturn is in the 1st (Regio). - "When the Sun is with Venus the native is courteous, a lover of music and adornment." Calculated Sun–Venus conjunction, 4.2°. - Cardano's warning about planets in fall and combustion: "they work, but give less glory than is due." What this means for you: a Cardano geniture of you would read "fortunate in himself, slow to rise, graceful in company, and given less credit than he deserves until later life".

Source, verified Johannes Müller (Regiomontanus, 1436–1476) published his Tabulae directionum (1467/1490). The house system named after him divides the celestial equator into twelve 30° arcs and projects them onto the ecliptic through the north and south points of the horizon. Lilly used it in Christian Astrology . Calculated The cusps are listed in §1, and the pole of each intermediate house is atan(tan φ · sin H). What this means for you: with Regiomontanus, Jupiter sits in the 12th but within 0.9° of the Ascendant, so Lilly counts it in the 1st. Under this house system your ruler is literally at the door , about to rise. That is a vivid emblem of luck arriving just as you show yourself.

Source, verified Johannes Schöner (1477–1547) of Nuremberg wrote De iudiciis nativitatum (1545). It is a systematic Latin manual that runs through the twelve houses with significators, lots and the revolution of years, and it drew on Bonatti, Alchabitius and Regiomontanus. Interpretation Schöner's order is to judge each house by (1) its lord, (2) its occupants, (3) its lot, and (4) the triplicity lords. Applied to the 10th: Jupiter (lord) in the 1st, Fortune present, and day triplicity lords of fire Sun, Jupiter and Saturn, all of them angular or in the 1st. What this means for you: Schöner would give a confident verdict on your career: honour by your own merit, helped in turn by all three fire-triplicity lords.

Manners (Mercury and Moon, Lilly) Interpretation : Mercury in Scorpio opposite Saturn and in reception with Mars gives a subtle, secretive, critical, skilled debater. The Moon in Leo square both gives a proud, magnanimous person who is easily wounded. What this means for you: you are sharp and fair in argument, and generous, but you take slights to heart. Wealth (2nd, its lord, Fortune) Interpretation : the lord of the 2nd, Venus, is in its own sign in the 7th. Fortune is in the 10th, with its dispositor Saturn in the 1st. This is substance gained by marriage, partnership, fees and contract, and by a steady trade. What this means for you: you should expect moderate to good wealth, built slowly and through people. Honour (10th, Sun, Jupiter) Interpretation : the lord of the 10th, Jupiter, is angular and dignified. The Sun is angular in the 7th but in fall. What this means for you: real honour and a good name, though rarely sole command. You are honoured as a partner, adviser or judge. Marriage (7th, Venus, Moon) Interpretation : Venus is dignified in the 7th with the Sun. The Moon applies by sextile to Venus. Lilly would read an early and willing marriage to a well-born, agreeable partner; Saturn opposite the 7th luminaries adds delay or an older partner. What this means for you: marriage is likely and good for you. Expect some delay, or a partner who is mature beyond their years. Travel (9th and 3rd, their lords, the Moon) Interpretation : Jupiter, the lord of the 9th, is in the 1st in a water sign. What this means for you: long journeys, quite possibly over water, are profitable and dear to you. Profession by Ptolemy's rule (Mercury, Venus, Mars; the planet oriental or in the 10th, or the lord of the 10th) Interpretation : the candidates are Mars (oriental, in reception with Mercury) and Mercury (in reception with Mars), with Venus in the 7th. Ptolemy says Mercury with Mars makes advocates, sculptors, physicians-in-surgery, soldiers of skill and debaters, and Venus adds the arts and adornment. The lord of the 10th, Jupiter, adds law and religion. What this means for you: the old rule points to advocacy, negotiation, law, engineering or technical craft, or a skilled profession that combines precision with argument.

docs.h: 15. Saints' days and the Church calendar
docs.t: Church calendar Source, verified - 13 October is the Translation of St Edward the Confessor, king of England (relics translated in 1163). It is also the feast of St Gerald of Aurillac, the lay count who refused to wear arms in the old sense and is patron of counts, the disabled and bachelors. St Theophilus of Antioch, St Comgan, St Coloman and St Simpert share the day. - Fatima: 13 October 1917, the "Miracle of the Sun". - Liturgical day 1998: Tuesday of the 28th week in Ordinary Time (Year C, weekday cycle II). Easter was 12 April and Pentecost 31 May. The date fell between Michaelmas (29 Sep) and St Luke (18 Oct). What this means for you: a medieval family would have given you a royal patron (Edward the king) and a noble lay patron (Gerald the count). Both men were honoured for justice and gentleness rather than conquest. That is a perfect echo of your Libra Sun.

Arcturus takes jasper and plantain. Algorab takes onyx, burdock and quadraginus. Regulus takes granite or garnet and celandine. What this means for you: Spica, "the gift-bringer", and Arcturus on your Sun are among the most favourable star contacts in the Latin tradition, promising patronage and honour. Regulus, the royal star, touches your Mars and your Dragon's Head: a royal stamp on effort and destiny.

Interpretation All the Latin schools agree on the core. Bonatti, Schöner, Morin and Lilly use different methods and still converge: you are a Jupiter-ruled, justice-minded person whose life is realised through partnership and a good name. Jupiter, rising in its own sign, is your manifest strength: faith, generosity, teaching and luck at the doorway. The Sun, the almuten of the figure, is your hidden lord. It sits in its fall in Libra, so you lead by fairness, agreement and service, not by command. That is why the Second Charlemagne test resolves the way it does: you share that figure's justice and piety, but not its conquests. Saturn and Mars, harsh by nature, are turned to your good by receptions. They give discipline, endurance and a debater's edge (the Mercury–Mars exchange). The Moon in Leo is your tender point: pride and feeling that need protection, and which are lord of your current year. The saints of your birthday, Edward the king and Gerald the count, together with Spica and Arcturus on your Sun and Regulus on your Dragon's Head, give a consistent emblem: a noble who rules by justice. Interpretation, added after the full 146 Bonatti's complete considerations confirm this picture and sharpen it. Of the 140 applicable rules, the clear majority favour you. The benefics outweigh the malefics (83–84). Your ruler is angular, dignified and free (17, 34, 59). Both malefics are tamed by reception and appear as your participators , Saturn then Mars (146). Fortune is in the 10th (85, 103), and Jupiter's second house is the MC, so the work of your life is public and professional (125). The weak point repeats across many considerations: Mercury, lord of your 7th, is under the beams and opposed by Saturn (51–53, 65, 116, 120). Contracts, papers and some colleagues turn adversarial, and your best ideas need someone to give them a platform. An eclipse on your rising area just before birth (67) and Regulus on the Dragon's Head (141) mark a life with public turning points. What this means for you: play to Jupiter, meaning teaching, counsel, law, faith and travel. Choose partners carefully, because the 7th is where your light lives. Do not undersell yourself: the Sun in fall makes you give away credit you deserve.

Plate A13 Each figure starts with the markers your chart has, then the ones it lacks. The conclusion says plainly which markers you carry. Only markers computed from your chart are counted. The Asclepius Restorer (Ascl. 26). - Present: Jupiter, the restoring benefic, rises in its own sign and own face as lord of the Ascendant. Hermes's returning teacher. - Present: Mercury is lord of the Lot of the Daimon and of your birth hour. Mercury sits in the 9th house, the house of doctrine. Jupiter, the teacher, rules both the Ascendant and the MC. - Absent: Mercury is peregrine and under the beams, not exalted or in its own sign. - Conclusion: you carry the teacher markers: a Mercurial daimon, the occupied 9th house and a Jupiter-ruled MC. You do not carry a dignified Mercury. - What this means for you: teaching and writing are your work. Your authority grows through the things you write and explain. The Poimandres first man (CH I.12–15). - Present: Jupiter, the ruler of your chart, rises in the Ascendant as the ruler's image in the body. - Absent: the first man is the cosmic Anthropos of all humanity, and the text gives no individual birth sign for him. - Conclusion: you carry the marker of Jupiter rising in the Ascendant. The text names no further individual marker. - What this means for you: you are at your best when your bearing reflects the order you serve. The Perfect Nature as guide (Picatrix III.6). - Present: Jupiter is the "planet ruling the radix of the nativity": lord of the Ascendant, in the Ascendant, in its own sign and face, and in sect. Mercury holds the Daimon lot and the birth hour. Venus is the almuten. - Absent: none of the markers the text gives is missing. - Conclusion: you carry every marker the Picatrix names for a governed Perfect Nature, and its governor is Jupiter. - What this means for you: your guiding spirit is Jupiterian. You reach it through ordered study and timed rites, such as the Moon's entry into Aries (§14). The Picatrix wise one who unites the spirits. - Present: Mars and Mercury are in mutual reception, Saturn is sextile Jupiter, and Venus receives the Sun. Your planets are bound to one another by reception. - Absent: the text requires a practised art, and a birth chart cannot show that. - Conclusion: you carry the binding-by-reception markers. Practice earns the title. - What this means for you: you can make opposing people and ideas work together. Practise it on purpose. The Ficino / prisca theologia sage. - Present: the three Graces are strong in your chart. Jupiter rises, and the Sun and Venus are conjunct. - Absent: a dominant, angular Saturn. Your Saturn is cadent and in shadow. - Conclusion: you carry Ficino's three-Graces markers. You do not carry the Saturnine-magus markers. - What this means for you: music, beauty and good company restore you. Solitary melancholy does not. The Agathodaimon. - Present: the Lot of the Daimon lies within 3.5° of the Pleiades. The Lots of Fortune and Victory are in the 11th house, which is called the Good Daimon. - Absent: any marker of identity with the god. - Conclusion: you carry the good-daimon markers in the Daimon lot, the 11th-house lots and the Pleiades contact. - What this means for you: your good fortune comes through friends and patrons and through following your guiding spirit. Hermes Trismegistus, the thrice-great. - Present: Mercury governs your Daimon lot and your birth hour. - Absent: a triple-dignity Mercury, meaning one in its own sign, exaltation and angular position. - Conclusion: you carry the Mercury-governance markers but not the thrice-great markers. - What this means for you: Mercury is your key, and Jupiter is your king. Overall: your strongest matches are the Perfect Nature with a Jupiterian governor and the good daimon. You also carry the teacher, restorer-of-order, uniter and three-Graces markers. None of these texts names a specific person to be born, and this reading claims no such person.

A Hermetic astrologer reading your figure would begin and end with Jupiter. It rises in its own sign and own face as lord of the root, the Picatrix's "planet ruling the radix", and it governs your Perfect Nature. Mercury is the secret key. It is peregrine but received by Mars, and it holds the Daimon lot and the birth hour. The Picatrix calls Mercury the significator of prophecy, so your spirit speaks through what you write and study. In Poimandres terms (CH I.25), your work is to surrender "evil machination" at Mercury's zone and "the evil impulses that come from wealth" at Jupiter's. Your mansions are the lion's forehead, the judge's scales and the belly of the fish, and together they stand for loyalty, justice and completion. The prophecy test shows what you carry: the Perfect Nature with Jupiter as its governor, the good-daimon placements, and the teacher's and uniter's patterns. [Source: Heindel, Message of the Stars ] Heindel teaches that "no aspect is to be judged apart from the balance of the whole horoscope". 2.1 The great conjunction of 1603 and the new stars Calculated The Jupiter–Saturn conjunction fell on 18 Dec 1603 at 8°28' Sagittarius, 2.3° from his natal Pluto. The Confessio 's "new stars in Serpentarius and Cygnus" correspond to SN1604, which sat at 17°40' Sagittarius in 1604. Precessed to 1998 it lies at 23°10' Sagittarius, 1.8° from his MC . P Cygni (21°46' Aquarius by longitude, latitude 55°) has no planet within 5°. Fama stars Sagittarius zoom What this means for you. [Source: Confessio ch. 6] The new stars are called "messengers" that God set in the heavens. Interpretation In the school's own symbolism, his public point (the MC) sits where the Rosicrucians saw their sign in the sky, and his deepest transformative planet sits on the 1603 fiery-trigon degree. Read through Heindel's rule that the MC shows "honour and standing", the vocation is coloured by Sagittarian teaching, publishing and philosophy. That is a theme in the chart and nothing more. 2.2 "Post CXX annos patebo" Calculated The 120-year openings run 1484, 1604, 1724, 1844, 1964 and 2084. His 1998 birth falls on none of them. 120-year cycle What this means for you. Interpretation The vault-opening rhythm does not fall on his birth year. In this school, his link to the manifestos runs through degrees, not through the calendar. 2.3 The Chymical Wedding: the seven days Source: Andreae 1616, Day 1 The story opens "on an evening before Easter Day", so the seven days run Holy Saturday to the following Friday. The text gives no planet key of its own; commentators (CRC/Confraternity guide, Steiner GA 35) read the seven days as seven stages of inner work, without a fixed planet table. Calculated Taking the weekday rulers from that dating gives the table below. The planet-per-day key is therefore a calendar derivation, not Andreae's own Source, verify . Day Weekday Ruler Episode Source His placement Calculated 1 Saturday Saturn storm, invitation, dream of the dungeon and the rope Saturn 0°56' Taurus R, 2nd, trine Mars and MC 2 Sunday Sun the four paths, arrival at the castle Sun 20°20' Libra, 7th, with Venus 3 Monday Moon the weighing of the guests Moon 7°30' Leo, 5th, critical degree, opposite Uranus 4 Tuesday Mars the comedy, the beheading of the six royals Mars 3°53' Virgo, 6th, critical degree (his birth weekday) 5 Wednesday Mercury Venus's sepulchre, voyage to the tower Mercury 2°47' Scorpio, 8th, opposite Saturn 6 Thursday Jupiter the seven-storey tower of Olympus, the alchemical work Jupiter 19°42' Pisces R, own sign, on the Ascendant 7 Friday Venus knighting as Knights of the Golden Stone Venus 16°08' Libra, own sign, 7th Source: Andreae, Day 3 Guests are weighed against seven weights. Interpretation In the allegory, those who "pass the weights" are the ones whose virtues hold together. His heaviest weights are Venus (harmony) and Jupiter (devotion). His Mercury, opposed by Saturn, is the scale that wobbles. The Chymical Wedding treats that as a test of patience, not a failure. On the day table, his two dignified planets rule the two closing days (Thursday's work in the tower, Friday's knighting), while Saturn rules the opening dungeon. Read as a story, his chart starts heavy and finishes strong. He was born on a Tuesday, the day of the beheading and renewal of the royals. In this allegory that is a day of ending one form so another can begin. Chymical seven days Synthesis, section 2. The manifesto layer gives two precise degree contacts (SN1604 to the MC, and the 1603 conjunction to Pluto) and one clear calendar miss (the 120-year cycle). The Chymical Wedding's week ends on his strongest planets.

Calculated Elevation order, from the MC down: Pluto, then Neptune, Uranus, Jupiter. The four elements by planet count (ten planets): Air 3 (Sun, Venus, Uranus), Earth 3 (Mars, Saturn, Neptune), Fire 2 (Moon, Pluto), Water 2 (Mercury, Jupiter). The Pisces Ascendant adds Water. [Source: Fludd, Utriusque Cosmi ] The monochord runs from earth to the empyrean, with Sol at the middle "diapason". Calculated His Sun is in the 7th house, above the horizon at this daytime birth. It sits in the middle of the order of planets by elevation, which matches the Sun's middle place on Fludd's monochord. [Source: Maier, Atalanta Fugiens ] The Rebis is the union of Sol and Luna or Venus. Calculated His Sun and Venus are conjunct in Libra. Elevation What this means for you. Interpretation In Maier's emblem language, a Sun–Venus union in the balance sign is the "hermaphroditic" harmony of opposites. For Heindel it is "positive testimony of unalloyed marital bliss", artistic gifts and popularity. Fludd's humours, with Air and Earth tied at 3 each, give a mixed sanguine–melancholic temperament. Watery sympathy comes in through the Ascendant. Microcosm Rebis balance 3.1 Fludd's winds [Source: Fludd, Mosaicall Philosophy (1659) and Utriusque Cosmi ] Fludd makes the four cardinal winds the carriers of God's light and darkness from the four quarters, each with its angel. His exact angel-to-wind table is Source, verify . [Source: Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), the standard key of Fludd's century] The triplicities are given winds: fire east, earth south, air west, water north. Calculated His planets by element: Air 3 → west (Zephyrus); Earth 3 → south (Auster); Fire 2 → east (Eurus); Water 2 plus the Pisces Ascendant → north (Boreas). So the west and south winds are tied by planet count, and the rising sign sits in the north. What this means for you. Interpretation In Fludd's picture the winds bring influence in from the quarters. Your strongest currents are the western (airy, Libran: relationship, judgement, balance) and the southern (earthy: work, method, endurance). The northern, watery wind enters through the Ascendant itself, so other people meet your sensitive, Piscean side first. The eastern, fiery wind (Moon in Leo, Pluto in Sagittarius) is fewer in number but placed high and on a critical degree. 3.2 Fludd's geomancy [Source: Fludd, Fasciculus Geomanticus (1687)] Fludd made the four Mothers by striking rows of points at random and counting odd or even. He gives no rule for drawing a figure from a birth chart. Calculated, constructed method To get a shield tied to this chart, I counted odd or even on the whole-degree positions in a fixed order. Mother I: Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus. Mother II: Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus. Mother III: Neptune, Pluto, Node, Ascendant. Mother IV: the arc-minutes of the Sun, Moon, Ascendant and MC. Daughters, Nieces, Witnesses and Judge then follow the standard rules. Position Figure Mothers I–IV Rubeus, Fortuna Minor, Laetitia, Albus Daughters I–IV Conjunctio, Fortuna Minor, Tristitia, Populus Nieces I–IV Laetitia, Amissio, Amissio, Tristitia Right / Left Witness Albus / Puella Judge Carcer Reconciler (Judge + Mother I) Puer Source: Agrippa / Golden Dawn sign attributions The figures for his main points are Libra Sun → Puella , Leo Moon → Fortuna Major/Minor , Pisces Ascendant → Laetitia , Sagittarius MC → Acquisitio . Puella (Libra/Venus) shows up as the Left Witness, and Laetitia (Pisces/Jupiter) as Mother III and Niece I, so his Sun and Ascendant figures both appear in the shield. Geomantic shield Geomancer What this means for you. Source Carcer is the "prison": binding, delay, a fixed enclosure, ruled by Saturn and given to Capricorn. Interpretation The constructed shield sums to Saturn's figure, which repeats the chart's own theme of Saturn as the container (Saturn trine Mars and the MC). Read it as structure, not punishment: the things you build to last are the things that hold you. The witnesses, Albus (wisdom, Mercury) and Puella (Venus, harmony), describe the two ways you get there: careful thought and good relationships. The method is constructed, so treat the shield as an emblem of the chart, not as a separate oracle. Synthesis, section 3. The alchemical emblems fit the Libra conjunction strongly. The winds favour west (air) and south (earth). The constructed geomantic shield points back to Saturn as the structuring force.

docs.t: Calculated Golden Dawn decans to minor arcana: Sun 4 of Swords ; Moon 5 of Wands ; Mercury 5 of Cups; Venus 3 of Swords; Mars 8 of Pentacles; Jupiter 9 of Cups ; Saturn 5 of Pentacles; Uranus 5 of Swords; Neptune 4 of Pentacles; Pluto 8 of Wands; Node 7 of Wands; Ascendant 10 of Cups; MC 10 of Wands. The planetary hour, corrected by hand from the script's night formula, is computed as follows. The day hour is 56.25 minutes long. The birth falls in the 11th day hour of a Tuesday, which is ruled by Mercury . The tattva at birth, by the 24-minute rule at 600.8 minutes after sunrise, is Akasha of Akasha . What this means for you. Source: GD Book T titles The 4 of Swords is "Rest from Strife" and the 9 of Cups "Material Happiness". The 10 of Cups ("Perfected Success") sits on the Ascendant, and the 8 of Pentacles ("Prudence") on Mars. Interpretation The Sun's card asks for rest after conflict, and the rising card promises fulfilment through emotional bonds. A Mercury hour fits a Mercury-themed chart. Akasha, the spirit tattva, is the one the GD links with contemplation. 5.1 The Hebrew name sigil on the Rose Cross Source: Golden Dawn, Rose Cross lamen ritual The 22 petals of the rose carry the Hebrew letters: the three mothers (Aleph, Mem, Shin) in the centre, the seven doubles (Beth, Gimel, Daleth, Kaph, Peh, Resh, Tav) in the middle ring, and the twelve simples (He to Qoph, in zodiac order) on the outside. A sigil is drawn by tracing the letters of a name from petal to petal, starting with a small circle and ending with a bar. The exact rotation of each ring on the lamen is Source, verify ; here each ring starts at the top and runs clockwise. Calculated "Charles Leone" in Hebrew letters: צארלס ליאונה (Tzaddi-Aleph-Resh-Lamed-Samekh, Lamed-Yod-Aleph-Vav-Nun-He). The geresh used in modern Hebrew for the "ch" sound has no petal and was dropped. Gematria: 90+1+200+30+60 = 381 ; 30+10+1+6+50+5 = 102 ; total 483 . The letters were set in IBM Plex Sans Hebrew and drawn with PIL. Hebrew sigil Rose Cross sigil What this means for you. Interpretation The trace passes through Aleph, the central mother letter of Air, twice, and its longest strokes run between the outer zodiac ring and the centre. The name keeps coming back to the middle, which matches a chart whose force is concentrated in its balance point (Libra). Aleph is the GD letter of Air and of the Fool's open beginning. Resh (Sun) is the only double letter besides the mothers in the name, which echoes a Sun that looks weak but is supported (section 7.5). 5.2 Grades, Sephiroth and his planets [Source: Golden Dawn grade structure; Regardie, The Golden Dawn ] Zelator = Malkuth (Earth); Theoricus = Yesod (Moon); Practicus = Hod (Mercury); Philosophus = Netzach (Venus); Adeptus Minor = Tiphareth (Sun); Adeptus Major = Geburah (Mars); Adeptus Exemptus = Chesed (Jupiter); Magister Templi = Binah (Saturn). Calculated, from section 7.5 His dignified or strong planets are Venus (Netzach, Philosophus), Jupiter (Chesed, Adeptus Exemptus) and the reversed-strong Sun (Tiphareth, Adeptus Minor). Mercury (Hod, Practicus) and Saturn (Binah) are strong-in-shadow. What this means for you. Interpretation On the GD ladder, the chart is easiest at the Venus and Jupiter grades (devotion, art, generosity) and hardest at the Mercury grade (Practicus: exact study, the water grade). That is the same Saturn–Mercury lesson found elsewhere in this chapter, seen in grade terms. It describes a curriculum, not an attainment.

docs.h: 6. AMORC (Lewis, Self Mastery and Fate with the Cycles of Life)
docs.t: Calculated Periods from 13 Oct 2026: P1 13 Oct (current); P2 4 Dec; P3 25 Jan 2027; P4 18 Mar; P5 9 May; P6 30 Jun; P7 21 Aug. He is aged 28, at the start of the 7-year cycle that runs 28–35. AMORC periods Life cycles What this means for you. [Source: Lewis, Self Mastery and Fate , checked against the text; health lines omitted] Corrected meanings. Period 1: favours from people in authority, reputation and standing. Period 2: short journeys, quick changes, not for permanent ventures or loans. Period 3: great energy for overcoming obstacles, but avoid quarrels. Period 4: mental work, writing, study, intuitive hunches, and beware deception. Period 5: success and expansion, long journeys, philosophy. Period 6: "the holiday of the year": pleasure, art, friendships. Period 7: critical and disruptive, breaking down before rebuilding; not a time to start new things, but good for real estate and older matters. (The earlier version wrongly made period 3 a "health" period and period 7 one of "rest".) The planet labels sometimes attached to the periods (1 Sun … 7 Saturn) come from later AMORC writers, not from Lewis, who says the cycles have "no relationship" with astrology Source: Rosicrucian Digest, secondary . Interpretation Now (period 1, to 3 Dec 2026) is for asking favours and building your standing. Use 9 May–29 Jun 2027 (period 5) for expansion, and keep 21 Aug–12 Oct 2027 (period 7) for finishing, not starting. 6.1 Daily cycle and birth period Source: Lewis, Chart E Each day is cut into seven periods of 3h 25m 43s from midnight, local standard time (daylight saving ignored). Each period has a letter A–G, and the letter sequence moves by weekday. Calculated Birth 16:25 EST on a Tuesday → period 5 (13:42–17:08) → letter C . AMORC daily What this means for you. Source Lewis's C periods favour intellectual work, education, publishing, study, writing letters and signing papers. They warn against "nimble tongues" and deception, and are not for dealing with opponents or seeking promotion. Interpretation You were born in the scholar's period, which is the same Mercury note as your Mercury birth hour (section 5). In practice: Tuesday 13:42–17:08 and the other C slots (Sun 10:17, Mon 00:00, Wed 03:25, Thu 17:08, Fri 06:51, Sat 20:34 starts) are your best writing hours by this system. Lewis's favourable F slots for new undertakings on a Tuesday are 00:00–03:25. Source, verify I found no separate "hourly" cycle in the text beyond these seven daily periods. The daily periods are Lewis's hour cycle. 6.2 Soul cycle and life cycle Source: Lewis The soul cycle counts from 22 March. Birth on 13 Oct falls in Period 4, Polarity B (20 Sep–15 Oct), which he describes as logical balance, aesthetic sense, seeking fairness, and a patron of the arts. He adds that people born in Period 4 are drawn to the arcane and are "often formerly adepts" of orders like his own. That is Lewis's claim, quoted, not a finding. The 7-year life cycle puts age 28–35 in Period 5: creative mind, visualisation, "illumination". What this means for you. Interpretation Lewis's soul-cycle portrait (balance, aesthetics, fairness) matches the astrology of a Libra Sun–Venus without using astrology at all. The current life period is the one Lewis reserves for creative and inward work.

docs.h: 8. Steiner, Sucher and the Lectorium Rosicrucianum
docs.t: Calculated Heliocentric positions: Earth 20°20' Aries; Mercury 0°35' Sagittarius; Venus 10°20' Libra; Mars 7°48' Leo; Jupiter 25°34' Pisces; Saturn 29°48' Aries; Uranus 11°32' Aquarius; Neptune 1°15' Aquarius; Pluto 7°36' Sagittarius. Sidereal (Fagan-Bradley): Sun 25°37' Virgo; Moon 12°47' Cancer; Ascendant 25°56' Aquarius. The vernal point is at 5°17' Pisces. Heliocentric What this means for you. Interpretation, after Sucher Heliocentrically the Earth is in Aries, and Mars and Uranus oppose each other across Leo–Aquarius, the same axis as his geocentric Moon–Uranus. Read through the Lectorium's teaching, the outer planets are "liberating" forces: his Uranus on a critical degree and his elevated Pluto are the places where his chart presses towards inner renewal. 8.1 Steiner's life periods Source: Steiner, e.g. GA 239 lecture VII; GA 96 The planetary spheres are lived through in seven-year steps. Moon 0–7, Mercury 7–14, Venus 14–21, Sun 21–42 (sentient soul 21–28, intellectual or mind soul 28–35, consciousness soul 35–42), Mars 42–49, Jupiter 49–56, Saturn 56–63. Calculated At 28 (since 13 Oct 2026), he has just entered the mind-soul stretch of the Sun period, which runs to 13 Oct 2033. The consciousness soul follows from 2033 to 2040, and the Mars period from 2040. What this means for you. Interpretation Steiner's Sun years are the time for working out who you are, and his Sun is the "reversed-strong" Libra Sun beside a dignified Venus. 28–35 is the stretch for thinking things through and forming your own judgement, which is the Libra task exactly. 8.2 Sucher's prenatal star of birth [Source: Sucher, The Constellation of Cosmic Thought / Isis Sophia ] Sucher takes the Hermetic epoch and treats the roughly ten sidereal months of gestation as a picture of life: each lunar month corresponds to seven years. He reads the events of each month as the "star" of the matching life period. Calculated The Moon returns to its epoch place on 13 Feb, 13 Mar, 9 Apr, 6 May, 2 Jun, 30 Jun, 27 Jul, 24 Aug, 20 Sep and 17 Oct 1998. Month 5 (6 May–2 Jun 1998) = ages 28–35 , the current period. In that month the Moon passed Pluto (→ about age 29.6), Neptune (~30.7), Uranus (~30.9), Jupiter (~31.7), Venus (~32.2), Saturn (~32.3), Mercury (~32.6), Mars (~32.8), and met the Sun at the prenatal New Moon of 25 May 1998 (~age 32.9). Calculated At birth the Sun stands in the constellation Virgo, about 3.5° from Spica by longitude (sidereal Sun 25°37' Virgo). Sucher would call that the starry setting of the birth. The exact "star of birth" wording is Source, verify . Sucher prenatal What this means for you. Interpretation In Sucher's picture, the current seven years are densely "lit": every planet is touched by the prenatal Moon between about 29½ and 33, ending at a prenatal New Moon near 33. That marks roughly 2031–32 as a seed point for a new start. Spica, the ear of wheat in the Virgin's hand, gives the Libra Sun a harvest image: patient work that ripens. Synthesis, sections 4–8. Venus/Jupiter dignity, Mars stamina and an elevated outer-planet axis are the strengths. The weak spots are the Saturn–Mercury and Moon–Uranus/Neptune tensions. Every later Rosicrucian system repeats those same two themes. The Hierarchy table puts his core under the Lords of Individuality and of Mind. Steiner and Sucher both point to ages 28–35 as an active, formative stretch.

Interpretation Across four centuries of Rosicrucian astrology, the chart tells one story. What is present. The manifestos' signs, the 1603 conjunction and SN1604, fall on his Pluto and his MC. That gives a vocation coloured by Sagittarian philosophy and teaching, under Heindel's Lords of Mind. Maier and Heindel agree on the Sun–Venus union in Libra (harmony, art, partnership), under the Lords of Individuality. Lewis's soul cycle (Period 4, Polarity B) describes the same balance and aesthetic sense without using astrology at all. Jupiter in his own sign on a Pisces Ascendant adds devotion and generosity, with violet and amethyst as its colour and stone. Mars on a critical degree, trine Saturn, provides the endurance. The work. The Gold- und Rosenkreuz "lead" is the Saturn–Mercury opposition. The constructed geomantic shield sums to Carcer, Saturn's figure, and the Chymical Wedding's week opens on Saturday's dungeon. All three say the same thing: structure and patience come first. Mercury is everywhere: Mercury birth hour, Lewis's scholar's letter C, Elias Artista's arts. The task is turning that Mercury's lead into gold through disciplined study and careful speech. Heindel's warnings about the Moon opposite Uranus and Neptune point to sensitivity that must be handled positively, never mediumistically. Timing. Steiner puts him at the start of the mind-soul years (28–35), and Sucher's prenatal Moon lights every planet across that same stretch, ending at a prenatal New Moon near age 33 (about 2031–32). AMORC's period 1 (now to 3 Dec 2026) and Jupiter's trine to the MC (7 Nov 2026) make this autumn good for building standing. Period 5 (May–Jun 2027) is for expansion. 2028–29 is a Saturn lesson. Net: a balanced, Jupiterian personality with real staying power, in a formative seven years. In this school his work is study, writing and partnership, carried out with Saturn's patience.

docs.h: 0. How the Golden Dawn did astrology
docs.t: Source The Order did not have a separate horoscopic system. It took the astrology of its day (tropical, Lilly-style dignities, Ptolemaic aspects), taught it in the Knowledge Lectures, then re-mapped every degree onto the Tree of Life : through the Hebrew letters of the Sepher Yetzirah , the Tarot of Book T, the 72 angels of the Shem ha-Mephorash, the colour scales, the tattvas, geomancy and the ritual figures (pentagram, hexagram, heptagram). So a GD reading is a chart read as a map of paths and powers to be worked with in ritual, not just a set of character statements. Book T adds its own zodiac: the first degree of Leo is fixed at the star Regulus (Cor Leonis). That puts the Book T zodiac about 29°48′ behind the tropical one for 1998. docs.h: 2. Dignity, reception and hidden strength (Knowledge Lectures, Lilly tables)
docs.t: Receptions Image c16: dispositor tree and receptions. Calculated Source The Zelator and Theoricus lectures give the domiciles, exaltations, detriments and falls (Saturn: Capricorn/Aquarius, exalted in Libra; Jupiter: Sagittarius/Pisces, exalted in Cancer; Mars: Aries/Scorpio, exalted in Capricorn; Sun: Leo, exalted in Aries; Venus: Taurus/Libra, exalted in Pisces; Mercury: Gemini/Virgo, exalted in Virgo; Moon: Cancer, exalted in Taurus). The GD inherited the rule that reception, angularity and sect can turn a weak placement around. Placement first, then hidden strength, then the net verdict. Sun, 20°20′ Libra, 7th house. Placement: in fall (Libra is opposite the Sun's exaltation). Hidden strength: angular (on the 7th side of the horizon); the sect light of a day chart; disposited by Venus, which is in her own sign in the same house; sextile the MC. Book T layer: the Sun moves to Virgo, out of fall. Net verdict: weakness cancelled. The Sun is weak in its sign but strong by position and well held by its ruler. What this means for you: the will does not stand alone. It turns on as soon as there is a counterpart, a client, a partner or an opponent. Alone you hesitate; in relationship you lead. Moon, 7°31′ Leo, 5th house. Placement: peregrine, succedent. Hidden strength: in the Book T zodiac the Moon is at 7°42′ Cancer, her own sign ; trine Pluto (1°18′). Under strain: opposite Uranus, square Mercury and Saturn. Net verdict: strong in shadow. Weak on the surface tropically, and dignified in the Order's own star-fixed zodiac. What this means for you: the emotional life looks theatrical and proud (Leo, the 5th house) but underneath it is protective and domestic (Cancer). People see the performance. Those close to you meet the caretaker. Mercury, 2°47′ Scorpio, 7th house. Placement: peregrine, angular. Hidden strength: mutual reception with Mars (Mercury in Mars's sign, Mars in Mercury's sign and exaltation, Virgo); sextile Mars (1°06′). Under strain: opposite Saturn and square Neptune. Net verdict: strong (cancelled weakness). What this means for you: a penetrating, investigative mind that works best in dialogue and negotiation. It argues with itself (Mercury opposite Saturn) until a position is airtight. Venus, 16°08′ Libra, 7th house. Placement: domicile , angular. Hidden strength: final dispositor of the Sun, Saturn and the 7th house; Saturn is received, because Venus sits in Saturn's exaltation. Book T: Venus at 16°20′ Virgo, her fall, so the second layer warns. Net verdict: strong. This is the best-placed personal planet. What this means for you: tact, aesthetic judgement and fairness are your natural tools, and partnerships tend to bring benefit. Mars, 3°53′ Virgo, 6th house. Placement: peregrine, cadent, in a hard house. Hidden strength: mutual reception with Mercury; trine Saturn (2°56′); Mars is the ruler of the day of birth (Tuesday). Book T: Mars moves to Leo, a fire sign, more at home. Under strain: square Pluto. Net verdict: weakness cancelled. What this means for you: the drive goes into craft, routine and precision rather than open fights. You fight by doing the work better. Jupiter, 19°42′ Pisces ℞, conjunct Ascendant. Placement: domicile , effectively on the 1st cusp (0°56′ inside the 12th but within Lilly's 5° rule for the next cusp). Hidden strength: chart ruler (traditional ruler of Pisces), final dispositor of the Ascendant, the MC and Neptune's sign line. Weakness: retrograde. Book T: Jupiter moves to Aquarius, Saturn's sign. Net verdict: strong, inward-turned. What this means for you: the single most important planet. You are recognised by your faith, your kindness and a sense that things will turn out right. Because Jupiter is retrograde, the gift matures slowly and turns inward first: belief has to be earned before it can be handed on. Saturn, 0°57′ Taurus ℞, 1st house. Placement: peregrine, angular. Hidden strength: mixed mutual reception with Venus (Saturn in Venus's house, Venus in Saturn's exaltation); trine Mars and trine the MC. Under strain: opposite Mercury and square Neptune. Book T: Saturn at 1°08′ Aries, its fall . Net verdict: strong in shadow, by reception. What this means for you: a serious, stubborn and durable core under the gentle Pisces surface. In the second layer it is fragile: patience is something you build, not something you were handed. Outer planets (not GD rulers; the Order's papers predate wide use of them, so they are read through their signs and paths only). Uranus in Aquarius and Neptune at the end of Capricorn, both in the 11th: a generation's signature put in the house of groups and hopes. Pluto in Sagittarius in the 9th: conviction, foreign or philosophical intensity. Synthesis, §2. Two essentially dignified planets (Venus and Jupiter) and two mutual receptions (Mercury with Mars; Saturn with Venus). No planet in this chart is unsupported. The weak spots (Sun in fall, a peregrine Moon) are each rescued, one by angularity and reception, the other by the Book T zodiac. The GD would call this a balanced chart in which Netzach (Venus) and Chesed (Jupiter) carry the load , the right-hand Pillar of Mercy.

You are meant to get good at a craft through steady, exact work. 7th (Virgo 20°39′, Libra intercepted; Sun, Venus, Mercury inside; ruler Mercury). What this means for you: the strongest house. Partners, collaborators and open rivals bring out your will. Choose them carefully, because they are where your life happens. 8th (Scorpio 4°20′; ruler Mars in the 6th, in reception). What this means for you: shared money and deep commitments come through work. What this means for you: philosophy, long journeys and higher study are personal and intense. Belief is where you are changed. With the 9th ruler on your Ascendant, your own outlook becomes your identity. 10th (MC Sagittarius 25°; Lot of Fortune in Capricorn; ruler Jupiter). What this means for you: the public role is teacher, guide, adviser or interpreter: a Jupiter vocation. Fortune in the 10th favours building a reputation step by step. 11th (Capricorn 16°20′; Uranus and Neptune inside; ruler Saturn in the 1st). What this means for you: friends and groups are unconventional, idealistic and generational. You give a group structure (Saturn rules the house from your 1st). 12th (Aquarius 11°56′; Jupiter inside, at the cusp of the 1st; ruler Saturn). What this means for you: a protected inner life. Retreat, study and solitude replenish you; Jupiter here is the "hidden helper" of the older texts. Synthesis, §3. The emphasis runs along the 1/7 axis (Jupiter and Saturn against Sun, Venus and Mercury) and along the work line (6th and 10th). The houses tell the same story as the dignities: a self shaped in encounter with others, finding its form through work.

docs.h: 4. Elements, modes and the four Kerubim
docs.t: Elements Image c08: weighted element and mode count. Calculated Weighted element count (luminaries and angles double): Water 7, Air 6, Fire 5, Earth 5. Mode: Mutable 9, Fixed 8, Cardinal 6. Source The four fixed signs are the Kerubim of Ezekiel and of the Neophyte hall (the Lion of fire, the Eagle of water, the Man of air, the Bull of earth), guarding the four quarters. Calculated Each Kerub holds a planet in this chart: the Lion = Moon in Leo; the Eagle = Mercury in Scorpio; the Man = Uranus in Aquarius; the Bull = Saturn in Taurus. What this means for you. Water leads, so you read situations through feeling and atmosphere first. The other three elements are almost level, a balance the GD praised as the goal of the Elemental grades (Zelator to Philosophus). A planet on every Kerubic sign is less common and has a definite GD meaning: all four quarters of the Temple are occupied , a fixed cross under the mutable surface. You are more stubborn and more sustained than you look. Synthesis, §4. Water-led, elementally almost balanced, with the fixed cross of the Kerubim complete: a flexible surface held by a four-square frame.

docs.h: 5. Sepher Yetzirah (Westcott's 1887 translation as used by the Order)
docs.t: Tree paths Image c03: the paths his placements light on the Tree of Life. Calculated 5a. Three Mother letters Source + Calculated Aleph = Air, Mem = Water, Shin = Fire (Westcott, ch. III). Earth is not a Mother; it comes from their mixture. The chart's water lead puts Mem first. What this means for you: Mem is the letter of the Hanged Man, of suspension and reversal. You often understand by letting go of the obvious angle. 5b. Seven Double letters (GD attribution, with Westcott ch. IV pairs) Source + Calculated Planet Letter Westcott's pair His planet's condition Pole indicated Mercury Beth Life / Death received by Mars Life Moon Gimel Peace / War peregrine, opposite Uranus alternating Venus Daleth Wisdom / Folly domicile Wisdom Jupiter Kaph Riches / Poverty domicile, rising Riches Mars Peh Grace / Indignation received by Mercury Grace (indignation held in check) Sun Resh Fertility / Solitude in fall but angular Fertility through partnership ; solitude when alone Saturn Tav Power / Servitude received by Venus, angular Power won by service [~ variant] Westcott's Supplement gives a second order (Beth = Moon, Wisdom; Gimel = Mars; Daleth = Sun, Fertility; Kaph = Venus, Life; Peh = Mercury, Power; Resh = Saturn, Peace; Tav = Jupiter, Beauty). Read that way, the dignified Venus gives Life and the dignified Jupiter gives Beauty: the same positive tone. What this means for you: of the seven pairs, five lean clearly to the gift side. The Moon swings between Peace and War, so moods have weather. The Sun gives the choice of Fertility or Solitude, settled by whether you are working with someone. 5c. Twelve Simple letters: the faculties of the signs Source + Calculated Sign occupied Letter (path) Westcott's faculty His planets Libra Lamed (22) Work Sun, Venus Leo Teth (19) Taste Moon, Node Scorpio Nun (24) Movement Mercury Virgo Yod (20) Union ( coition in Westcott) Mars Pisces Qoph (29) Sleep Jupiter, Asc Taurus Vav (16) Hearing Saturn Aquarius Tzaddi (28) Imagination Uranus Capricorn Ayin (26) Mirth Neptune Sagittarius Samekh (25) Anger Pluto, MC Aries, Gemini, Cancer Heh, Zayin, Cheth Sight, Smell, Speech empty What this means for you: the Sun and Venus on Work , the Ascendant and Jupiter on Sleep (dream, intuition, rest) and Saturn on Hearing . You are made to work hard while awake and to receive guidance in rest and in listening. Taste (Moon in Leo) gives discernment in pleasure. Anger sits on the MC: a public role that has to handle righteous indignation well. 5d. Twelve diagonal boundaries (cube of space) Source + Calculated Cube Image c15: the cube-of-space edges his placements occupy, using the directions in Westcott's 1887 Sepher Yetzirah, ch. V (checked against the online text this round). Westcott's directions are: Heh (Aries) north-east, Vav (Taurus) south-east, Zayin (Gemini) east-above, Cheth (Cancer) east-below, Teth (Leo) north-west, Yod (Virgo) south-west, Lamed (Libra) west-above, Nun (Scorpio) west-below, Samekh (Sagittarius) south-above, Ayin (Capricorn) south-below, Tzaddi (Aquarius) north-above, Qoph (Pisces) north-below. An earlier version of c15 placed Leo to Pisces on the wrong edges. That has now been corrected. His placements fall mainly on the western edges : Libra west-above (Sun, Venus), Scorpio west-below (Mercury), Leo north-west (Moon, Node) and Virgo south-west (Mars). North-below (Pisces) holds Jupiter and the Ascendant. South-above (Sagittarius) holds Pluto and the MC, and south-east (Taurus) holds Saturn. The three purely eastern edges (Aries, Gemini, Cancer) are empty. What this means for you: in the Order's symbolism, east is dawn and beginning, and west is completion, reception and the place of the Hierophant's opposite, the Hiereus. Your strength lies in finishing, receiving and judging rather than in initiating. The one eastern touch, Saturn south-east, gives starting power only slowly and with effort. 5e. The 32 Paths Calculated Lit paths: 16, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25, 26, 28 and 29 (signs), plus the Sephiroth of the seven planets. Five of the lit paths (20, 22, 24, 25, 26) end on Tiphareth , the Sun-centre and the sphere of the Adeptus Minor. What this means for you: the chart repeatedly sends you back to the centre of the Tree, to integration, beauty and balance. That is the most "Golden Dawn" thing about it. 5f. Gematria of the name Calculated Charles = כרלס Kaph-Resh-Lamed-Samekh = 20 + 200 + 30 + 60 = 310 ; Leone = ליאונ Lamed-Yod-Aleph-Vav-Nun = 30 + 10 + 1 + 6 + 50 = 97 (with final Nun = 700, 747 ). Total 407 (or 1057). Aiq Bekar reductions: 310 → 4 (Chesed, Jupiter); 97 → 16 → 7 (Netzach, Venus); 407 → 11 → 2 (Chokmah). What this means for you: the forename reduces to Jupiter's number and the surname to Venus's: the two dignified planets of the chart . The name and the chart agree on Mercy and Victory. 5g. Date number (Westcott, Numbers ) Calculated 1+3+1+0+1+9+9+8 = 32 → 5 . Westcott calls 32 the number of the Paths of Wisdom (SY ch. I). 5 is Geburah, Mars and the Pentagram. What this means for you: the date points to the whole Tree (32) and to its discipline (5). Together with the Tuesday birth, Mars's day, the date says the Path is walked through effort. Synthesis, §5. The Sepher Yetzirah layer centres on Tiphareth, leans to the positive pole of five out of seven doubles, and puts the main faculties on Work and on Sleep or dream. The name's numbers repeat the two dignified planets. This is the most internally consistent layer of the chapter.

docs.h: 6. Book T: the Tarot of the chart
docs.t: 6a. Major Arcana Source + Calculated GD attributions (Strength = VIII = Leo, Justice = XI = Libra). Planet trumps: Sun = XIX Sun (Resh); Moon = II High Priestess (Gimel); Mercury = I Magician (Beth); Venus = III Empress (Daleth); Mars = XVI Tower (Peh); Jupiter = X Wheel (Kaph); Saturn = XXI Universe (Tav). Sign trumps occupied: XI Justice (Sun, Venus), VIII Strength (Moon, Node), XIII Death (Mercury), IX Hermit (Mars), XVIII Moon (Jupiter, Ascendant), V Hierophant (Saturn), XVII Star (Uranus), XV Devil (Neptune), XIV Temperance (Pluto, MC). What this means for you: your Sun and Venus sit in Justice . That is the card of balance and fair dealing, and the 7th house is its natural home. Your rising card is The Moon : a path of dreams, of night-crossing and of trusting what you cannot yet see. Your MC is Temperance , the mixing of fire and water and the GD's card of the "arrow of aspiration". So the outer life asks you to blend opposites. 6b. The 36 decans: small cards Source + Calculated Decans tropical Image c04: small cards of his decans, tropical. Calculated Decans Book T Image c05: the same, in the Book T zodiac. Calculated Point Tropical decan card (title; decan ruler) Book T zodiac card (title; ruler) Sun 4 of Swords, Rest from Strife (Jupiter) 10 of Pentacles, Wealth (Mercury) Moon 5 of Wands, Strife (Saturn) 2 of Cups, Love (Venus) Mercury 5 of Cups, Loss in Pleasure (Mars) 2 of Swords, Peace Restored (Moon) Venus 3 of Swords, Sorrow (Saturn) 9 of Pentacles, Material Gain (Venus) Mars 8 of Pentacles, Prudence (Sun) 5 of Wands, Strife (Saturn) Jupiter 9 of Cups, Material Happiness (Jupiter) 6 of Swords, Earned Success (Mercury) Saturn 5 of Pentacles, Material Trouble (Mercury) 2 of Wands, Dominion (Mars) Uranus 5 of Swords, Defeat (Venus) 2 of Pentacles, Harmonious Change (Jupiter) Neptune 4 of Pentacles, Earthly Power (Sun) 10 of Wands, Oppression (Saturn) Pluto 8 of Wands, Swiftness (Mercury) 5 of Cups, Loss in Pleasure (Mars) North Node 7 of Wands, Valour (Mars) 4 of Cups, Blended Pleasure (Moon) Ascendant 10 of Cups, Perfected Success (Mars) 7 of Swords, Unstable Effort (Moon) MC 10 of Wands, Oppression (Saturn) 7 of Cups, Illusionary Success (Venus) Calculated Jupiter sits in its own decan (Jupiter rules the 2nd decan of Pisces, the 9 of Cups), a dignity by face added to its domicile. The Ascendant's card, the 10 of Cups Perfected Success , is one of the most favourable cards in Book T. What this means for you, point by point: - Sun, 4 of Swords: your vitality comes back through truce, pause and retreat. You win by calling a ceasefire. - Moon, 5 of Wands: emotional life thrives on contest. Rivalry wakes you up, though it is tiring. - Mercury, 5 of Cups: the mind is often drawn to what has been lost or spoiled, which makes you a good analyst of failure. - Venus, 3 of Swords: love is honest about pain. You will not pretend a hurt is not there. - Mars, 8 of Pentacles: effort goes into skill, apprenticeship and careful hands. - Jupiter, 9 of Cups: contentment, ease and being well provided for. This is the "wish card" of the deck, sitting on your Ascendant. - Saturn, 5 of Pentacles: early material strain that builds endurance. - Ascendant, 10 of Cups: the emotional "completion" card. People feel at home with you. - MC, 10 of Wands: the public burden. You will carry more responsibility than you asked for, so learn to delegate. - Node, 7 of Wands: growth comes from holding your ground against many. - Outer planets: Defeat, Earthly Power and Swiftness are generational colours more than personal ones. The Book T layer turns several painful cards into benefic ones (Sun → Wealth , Moon → Love , Venus → Material Gain , Mercury → Peace Restored ). It turns the Ascendant from Perfected Success to Unstable Effort , and the MC from Oppression to Illusionary Success . What this means for you: the tropical cards are the surface story, which has more conflict; the Book T cards are the deeper story, which is more prosperous. In both, the public side (MC) is the one that needs most care. 6c. Court cards (Book T: each court rules from 20° of one sign to 20° of the next) Source + Calculated Court wheel Image c06: court-card spans of the zodiac, with his points. Calculated Point Tropical court Book T-zodiac court Sun Prince of Cups (only 0°20′ past the 20° boundary; the Queen of Swords is one step behind) Queen of Swords Moon Prince of Wands Queen of Cups Mercury Prince of Cups Queen of Swords Venus Queen of Swords Knight of Pentacles Mars Knight of Pentacles Prince of Wands Jupiter Knight of Cups Prince of Swords Saturn Prince of Pentacles Queen of Wands Ascendant Queen of Wands Knight of Cups MC Queen of Pentacles Knight of Wands What this means for you: tropically, the Sun and Mercury share the Prince of Cups : Air of Water, the subtle, secretive and strategic emotional intelligence of the Book T description. The Moon is the Prince of Wands , Air of Fire: swift, proud and generous. The Ascendant is the Queen of Wands , Water of Fire: steady, attractive and kind to those around it. The Sun, sitting right on a boundary, also carries the Queen of Swords , Water of Air: perception that cuts through pretence. In the Book T zodiac the same Sun is fully the Queen of Swords. Expect people to experience you as perceptive and exact. 6d. Princess and Ace quadrants Source + Calculated The Princesses rule the four quadrants of heaven around the North Pole (the thrones of the Aces). Your Sun (Libra) and Mercury fall in the Princess of Cups' quadrant (Libra–Sagittarius); the Moon (Leo) in the Princess of Wands' (Cancer–Virgo); the Ascendant (Pisces) in the Princess of Swords' (Capricorn–Pisces). What this means for you: the roots of your will are watery, of your feelings fiery and of your persona airy. That is three of the four Aces, with only Earth (Pentacles) missing from the main points, so practical grounding must be added on purpose. 6e. Elemental dignities among the main cards Source + Calculated Book T rules: cards of the same element strengthen each other; fire and air are friendly; water and earth are friendly; fire against water, and air against earth, weaken each other. Sun (Swords, air) with the Ascendant (Cups, water): neutral . Sun (air) with the Moon (Wands, fire): friendly . Moon (fire) with the Ascendant (water): contrary . What this means for you: the will and the feelings cooperate. What you feel and how you come across can work against each other, so fiery feelings may be hidden behind a soft manner. 6f. The 72 quinance angels (Shem ha-Mephorash) Source + Calculated Quinances Image c07: the 72 five-degree quinances, Book T order from 0° Leo. Calculated Point Tropical quinance angel Book T-zodiac angel Sun Lauviah (II) Lauviah Moon Yeliel Habuiah Mercury Leuviah Yezalel Venus Hakamiah Aladiah Mars Achaiah Vehuiah Jupiter Ariel Yeiazel Saturn Mebahiah Vehuel Ascendant Asaliah Hahahel MC Omael Haheuiah [~ variant] Book T counts the 72 from 0° Leo (Regulus). Later authors count from 0° Aries; the Aries order would move every name. What this means for you: these are names to work with, not character traits. In GD practice each is invoked through its decan card (two quinances to a decan, one for the day half and one for the night half). Your Ascendant angel Asaliah and your Sun angel Lauviah are the two the Order's method would treat as personal patrons. 6g. Significator Interpretation In the Opening of the Key the querent's significator is chosen by complexion, which a chart cannot give. Chart-derived alternative: the Queen of Wands (Ascendant court), or the Knight of Cups (Jupiter, the chart ruler, plus the Ascendant in the Book T zodiac). Synthesis, §6. In the Tarot the chart reads as Justice at the heart, the Moon at the door and Temperance at the summit : a balancer who goes forward by night-sight and blends opposites in public. The tropical cards show the contest (5s and 3s). The Book T-zodiac cards show the reward (Wealth, Love, Material Gain).

Tzadqiel and Sachiel (Jupiter) are the governing names, and Zuriel (Libra) the archangel of your Sun. Synthesis, §7. The angelic layer is led by Jupiter (chart ruler, dignified, rising) and Venus (Sun-sign ruler, dignified). It is the same Chesed–Netzach pair found in §2 and §5f.

Hexagram Image c17: his planets on the GD hexagram (Saturn at the top, Moon at the bottom, Sun at the centre). Calculated Hexagram (Lesser and Greater Rituals of the Hexagram). On the hexagram your dignified Jupiter and Venus hold the right-hand points , Saturn (received) the crown, and the Sun (fall, rescued) the centre. What this means for you: when you work the Sun-hexagram (all six forms traced, as the GD prescribes for the Sun), you are working the weakest-by-sign but most central planet. That is the GD's standard method for strengthening it. Pentagram. Water leads (§4), so the Water pentagram (invoking from the Kerubic angle of the Eagle) is your elemental working; balance it with the Earth pentagram , the lowest count among the main points. Heptagram (Lineal Figures). Born on a Tuesday (Mars) in the hour of Mercury (11th day-hour, 56.2 minutes long). Planetary hours Image c10: the planetary hours of 13 Oct 1998 at Johnstown. Calculated What this means for you: day Mars and hour Mercury repeat the Mercury–Mars mutual reception , the strongest bond in your chart. That is an unusual amount of repetition: thought and action are made to trade places in you. Rose Cross Lamen sigil. Rose Cross sigil Image c12: the name traced on the 22-petal Rose (Mathers' method; transliterated title). Calculated The line runs Kaph (planet petal) → Resh (planet) → Lamed (sign) → Samekh (sign), then Lamed → Yod → Aleph (mother) → Vav → Nun. What this means for you: the name touches all three rings of the Rose (mother, double and simple), which in the Adept's lamen means it draws on the elements, the planets and the signs alike. Telesmatic image (Flying Roll XII method). Kaph gives the head (Jupiter: a broad, crowned head), Resh the face and chest (Sun: golden), Lamed the arms (Justice: balanced hands, scales), Samekh the legs and feet (Sagittarius: a hunter's stride, an arrow). The first two letters are masculine, so the figure is a male form. See image 07 in the art gallery. What this means for you: your name's own angel-image is a crowned, balanced archer. Jupiter at the head and the arrow of aspiration at the feet: the same as the Ascendant and the MC. Synthesis, §8. Every ritual figure points to one task: strengthen the central Sun through the dignified Jupiter and Venus, and let Mercury and Mars trade energy .

docs.h: 9. Tattvas (GD Tattva papers; Rama Prasad, Nature's Finer Forces)
docs.t: Tattva tide Image c09: the tattva currents from sunrise, with his birth time. Calculated Skyfield (DE440s ephemeris, standard refraction, upper limb) gives sunrise at Johnstown as 11:24:13.1 UT on 13 Oct 1998, which is 07:24:13 local daylight time (EDT). Birth at 21:25:00 UT is 600 min 46.9 s later. Five 24-minute tattvas make a 120-minute cycle that begins with Akasa. 600 minutes is exactly five cycles, so birth falls 46.9 seconds into a new Akasa tide . Answer: Akasa; sub-tattva Akasa of Akasa. The Apas tide ended 46.9 seconds before birth. What this means for you: Akasa is Spirit/Ether, the black or indigo egg, the medium of the other four. Akasa of Akasa is the "doubled spirit", which the GD's skrying papers treat as the hardest tattva to work with and the most open. You were born just as the water tide gave way to Spirit, so Apas is the tide you came out of, not the one you belong to. Your skrying symbol is the black/indigo egg. Akasa turning tide Art 26: the tide turns from Apas to Akasa at birth (labels added with PIL). Interpretation

Geomancy Image c13: the geomantic figures of his signs and planets. Calculated GD sign figures: Libra = Puella (Sun, Venus); Leo = Fortuna Major/Minor (Moon, Node); Scorpio = Rubeus (Mercury); Virgo = Conjunctio (Mars); Pisces = Laetitia (Jupiter, Asc); Taurus = Amissio (Saturn). The North Node itself is Caput Draconis , the figure of entry and of new beginnings. What this means for you: the rising figure is Laetitia (Joy) , the figure of Jupiter, a third confirmation of the chart ruler. The Sun's figure Puella is Venusian and harmonious. Mercury's figure Rubeus is the most dangerous one in the system, so keep that analytical intensity aimed at problems, not people.

docs.h: 11. The microcosm: the body as symbol (symbolic only)
docs.t: The GD's Sphere of Sensation and Zodiacal Man put Aries at the head and Pisces at the feet, with the Tree of Life laid on the body. Your Ascendant and Jupiter at the feet (Pisces) , your Sun and Venus at the waist and loins (Libra), the Moon at the heart (Leo) and Saturn at the throat (Taurus). On the Tree overlay, Tiphareth (heart and solar plexus) is the meeting point of five of your lit paths. What this means for you: symbolically, your "ground" is the feet, the place of faith and of walking forward. Your "voice" is weighted by Saturn: speak slowly and it carries. (Symbolic body only; no health reading is made.) Art 07 telesmatic Art 07: telesmatic body of the name Charles Leone (labels added with PIL). Interpretation Synthesis, §§9–11. Spirit (Akasa) at the tide, Joy (Laetitia) at the rising figure, and a body crowned in Jupiter and footed in faith: the subtler techniques repeat the chart's Jupiterian keynote.

docs.h: 12. Prophecy test: the awaited figures of the Golden Dawn's sources
docs.t: Source The Order's Second Order rests on the Rosicrucian story read in the 5=6 Adeptus Minor ritual. The Fama Fraternitatis tells of Christian Rosenkreutz (C.R.C.) , his seven-sided vault, lit by a sun-like lamp and inscribed Post CXX annos patebo ("after 120 years I shall be opened"), and its opening by Brother N.N. Paracelsian prophecy, received through the Confessio and Rosicrucian lore, foretells Elias Artista , who will reveal the hidden art, and the Lion of the North , a ruler from the north who overcomes the Eagle. Mathers' 1896 manifesto rests the Order's authority on the Secret Chiefs of the Third Order. There are no numerical scores; each marker is checked one at a time and matches are listed first . Prophecy table Image c18: the marker-by-marker test. Calculated Matches Lion of the North, "the Lion." His Moon is at 7°31′ Leo and his North Node at 28°35′ Leo . He carries the Lion through both his Moon and his destiny point. Secret Chiefs and Third Order, the four Kerubim guarding the throne. All four fixed signs hold a planet : the Lion (Moon), the Eagle (Mercury), the Man (Uranus) and the Bull (Saturn). He carries the complete Kerubic cross. C.R.C., the Rose. Venus, the planet of the rose, is in her own sign Libra and angular. He carries the Rose. C.R.C., the Cross and Tiphareth. His Sun is angular in cardinal Libra, and five of his lit paths end on Tiphareth. He carries the Cross. C.R.C., the ever-burning lamp in the vault. His Moon, the lamp of night, is in the fiery 5th house, and his Mars is in Virgo, the sign of the Hermit's lamp. He carries the Lamp. Elias Artista, the fiery chariot. In the Order's Book T zodiac his Moon is at 7°42′ Cancer , the Chariot's sign and the Moon's own domicile. He carries the Chariot in the Order's own zodiac. Elias Artista, the Artist of the hidden art. Mercury and Mars are in mutual reception (the alchemical exchange of mind and fire), and Venus is in her domicile. He carries the Artist. Lion of the North, "of the North." He was born at 40°20′ N , with the destiny point in Leo. He carries the North. Lion of the North, "overcomes the Eagle." His Moon in Leo squares Mercury in Scorpio (the Eagle Kerub). The Lion meets the Eagle in his chart. Partial C.R.C., journeys to the East (Damcar, Fez). Pluto is in Sagittarius in the 9th, and the 9th ruler is on the Ascendant. He has a strong long-journey and foreign-learning signature, without a pointer to the East. Elias Artista, the union of Sun and Moon. His Sun in Libra and Moon in Leo are sextile by sign, but the aspect is not exact. Lion of the North, ruler and conqueror. His Sun is in fall but angular and received, and his MC is ruled by the rising Jupiter. His authority comes through counsel rather than conquest. Secret Chiefs, the 5=6 Adept of Tiphareth. His Sun is angular and the light of a day chart. In Book T the Sun falls in Virgo (the Hermit). No match C.R.C., the 120-year term. There is no 120-year marker. Secret Chiefs, claimed contact. A chart cannot show this. Excluded: Crowley's "Crowned and Conquering Child" (1904) belongs to Thelema, not to the GD canon. Overall statement Interpretation . He carries the Lion of the North most fully: the Lion, the North and the Eagle all match, and only the conqueror's role is partial. He carries the four Kerubim completely. He carries the Rose, Cross and Lamp of the C.R.C. vault, and Elias Artista's Chariot and Art . He does not carry the 120-year term or the Secret Chiefs' contact. As with every prophecy test in this book, this is a symbolic comparison, not a claim that he is the figure. What this means for you: the Lion figure is the Order's image of a ruler who comes from the north and masters the Eagle. In you it reads as warm, proud feeling (the Leo Moon) that has to learn to command sharp, probing thought (Mercury in Scorpio) rather than be ruled by it.

Method note. The Opening of the Key needs a shuffled deck. No physical draw was made, so this one is constructed : a 78-card deck was shuffled with a pseudo-random generator seeded deterministically from the birth moment (SHA-256 of "1998-10-13T21:25:00Z|40.33N|78.92W"), and the same seed produces the same spread every time. Treat it as a symbolic exercise in the Order's method, not as a divination he performed. The significator is the Queen of Wands (§6g). Counting follows Book T: Aces 11, Princesses 7, other courts 4, small cards their number, Mother trumps 3, planetary trumps 9 and sign trumps 12. Pairing runs outward from the significator. Opening of the Key Image c20: the five operations, with the counted chain for each. Interpretation Opening of the Key art Art 23: the five operations laid out (labels added with PIL). Interpretation First operation (YHVH piles). The significator lies in the Heh pile (Cups: water, feeling, relationships) , facing left (the past). The counted chain is Queen of Wands → 4 of Cups (Blended Pleasure) → I Magician → XIV Temperance → 8 of Pentacles (Prudence) → 4 of Swords (Rest from Strife) → Ace of Cups → 2 of Swords (Peace Restored). The pairs open with 6 of Pentacles / 2 of Swords, 8 of Pentacles / Ace of Wands, the Chariot / 4 of Pentacles and the Magician / Princess of Wands. What this means for you: the matter starts in feeling and partnership, the Cups pile that echoes the Libra Sun. Skill (the Magician) is tempered by mixing (Temperance, your MC card) and then turned into patient work (8 of Pentacles). The story ends in restored peace (the 2 of Swords). Quarrels are settled by craft and patience. Second operation (twelve houses). The significator falls in the 11th house (friends, hopes, groups), facing right (the future). The chain is Queen of Wands → 6 of Pentacles (Material Success) → 7 of Pentacles (Success Unfulfilled), with the pairs 6 of Swords / Wheel of Fortune and High Priestess / 7 of Pentacles. What this means for you: the field of action is friendships and societies, which is apt for an Order reading. Gains come through groups, but the Order's own warning card follows: success unfulfilled if the work is left half done. The Wheel (Jupiter, your chart ruler) and the High Priestess say that timing and quiet knowledge decide it. Third operation (twelve signs). The significator falls in Sagittarius , the sign of the MC, facing right. The chain is Queen of Wands → XV Devil → Knight of Pentacles → 2 of Wands (Dominion), with the pairs 2 of Wands / 4 of Pentacles and Strength / Knight of Pentacles. What this means for you: in the career sign, the Devil (Capricorn, material bondage) has to be passed through before Dominion is reached. Strength (Leo, your Moon) paired with the steady Knight of Pentacles shows how: the Lion tamed into slow, earthy persistence. Fourth operation (thirty-six decans). The significator stands in Leo I, facing right. The chain is Queen of Wands → 10 of Cups (Perfected Success, Virgo I) → Ace of Pentacles (Sagittarius I) → Knight of Cups (Pisces II) → VII Chariot (Aries II). The pairs open with Wheel / Knight of Wands, 2 of Wands / 10 of Wands, 4 of Pentacles / 10 of Cups and Magician / Ace of Wands. What this means for you: the chain runs from the Lion (your Moon) through Pisces (your Ascendant) to the Chariot. It is the Elias Artista marker of §12, now appearing in the draw. Emotional fulfilment (10 of Cups) is turned into a material root (Ace of Pentacles) and then into forward movement. Fifth operation (Tree of Life). The significator falls in Malkuth , facing left. The chain is Queen of Wands → XIII Death , with the pairs Moon / Fool, Princess of Cups / Devil and Death / 8 of Pentacles. What this means for you: the outcome is set in the material world. Death here is the Order's card of transformation (Scorpio, your Mercury sign), not literal ending. An old form is cleared, and the 8 of Pentacles puts patient craft in its place. Synthesis, §12a. The constructed spread repeats the natal themes on its own: Cups and partnership first, Jupiter's Wheel in the house of groups, the Leo Lion tamed in the career sign, the Chariot in the decans, and Scorpionic transformation at the root. Its advice is consistent across all five operations: patient craft (the 8 of Pentacles, twice) settles what feeling begins.

Method note. A shield chart needs sixteen lines of dots made by hand. These sixteen lines were instead constructed from the same birth-seeded generator (line counts 16, 14, 16, 14 / 5, 10, 12, 9 / 6, 12, 15, 14 / 12, 9, 12, 16; odd gives one dot, even gives two). The figures follow the GD Geomancy lecture: Mothers, Daughters, Nieces, Witnesses, Judge and Reconciler, with the twelve figures placed in houses in the Order's order (10, 1, 4, 7, 11, 2, 5, 8, 12, 3, 6, 9). Geomantic shield Image c21: the constructed shield. Interpretation Geomantic shield art Art 24: the shield in the sand (labels added with PIL). Interpretation Mothers: Populus, Carcer, Albus, Rubeus. Daughters: Rubeus, Tristitia, Albus, Rubeus. Nieces: Carcer, Conjunctio, Acquisitio, Conjunctio. Houses: 10th Populus, 1st Carcer, 4th Albus, 7th Rubeus, 11th Rubeus, 2nd Tristitia, 5th Albus, 8th Rubeus, 12th Carcer, 3rd Conjunctio, 6th Acquisitio, 9th Conjunctio. Right Witness Via, Left Witness Fortuna Major, Judge Fortuna Minor, Reconciler Fortuna Minor. What this means for you: Carcer (the Prison, Saturn) in the 1st repeats Saturn in your 1st house. You are self-contained and hold yourself back until you are sure. Rubeus in the 7th gives partnership a heated edge, the shadow side of the Libra Sun: fairness has to be kept up against flashes of temper. Populus in the 10th puts your public life among crowds and groups. Acquisitio in the 6th brings gain through daily work. Albus (wisdom, Mercury) in the 4th and 5th makes home and creativity the places where you think most clearly. The Witnesses show the path: Via (the Road) on your side and Fortuna Major (great fortune, the Sun) behind it. The Judge, Fortuna Minor , is the swift, outer fortune of the Sun. It comes quickly and has to be secured before it passes. The Reconciler repeats Fortuna Minor, so the reading holds. Synthesis, §12b. The shield echoes the natal Saturn at the door and the fire in the partnership house. Its verdict is good fortune, gained by movement (Via) and secured quickly (Fortuna Minor).
