House 11 (Capricorn–Aquarius) — Neptune and Uranus: XV Devil and XVII Star, with the Fool. Friends and causes form your visionary circle. House 12 (Aquarius–Pisces) — Jupiter in equal house 12: X Wheel turning behind the veil. A hidden benefactor; luck that works from behind the scenes. What this means for you: The occupied houses sit around the 5th–9th (love, work, partnership, depth, philosophy) and the 11th–1st (vision and self). Your life plays out in the relationship and meaning arena. Synthesis: The chart's centre of gravity is the descendant. In Tarot terms, Justice is the card on which your life opens.

docs.h: 5. Birth cards, year cards and timing (Greer, Arrien, Tarot School)
docs.t: Birth cards Year cards Personality & Soul card: 10 + 13 + 1998 = 2021 → 2 + 0 + 2 + 1 = 5, V Hierophant . It is both cards, because 5 cannot be reduced further (Greer, Who Are You in the Tarot? , 2011). The Tarot School's split method gives 10 + 13 + 19 + 98 = 140 → 5, the same. Hidden factor: the Hierophant's constellation includes XIV Temperance (14 → 5). Zodiac card: XI Justice (Sun in Libra). Year cards (month + day + year): 2026 = 2049 → 15, XV Devil . 2027 → VII Chariot . 2028 → VIII Strength . No 0/22 Fool year occurs between 1998 and 2070. Arrien growth cycles (Arrien, The Tarot Handbook , 1987, as summarised at https://wanderlustlover.livejournal.com/2744145.html and in the review at aeclectic.net; Greer's method at https://esoterrier.com/systems/tarot): the growth card runs birthday to birthday and is not reduced when it falls between 10 and 21. Your decades run Hierophant (5) 2007–2016, cards 5→14; Lovers (6) 2017–2026 , cards 6→15, with the 2026 card XV Devil from 13 October 2026; and Chariot (7) from 2027 . What this means for you: You are a teacher card, the Hierophant. Your soul's lesson is to find and pass on a living tradition. 2026, the Devil year, is about recognising chains you agreed to. 2027, the Chariot, is a year of decisive forward motion. Secondary progressed Sun through the decan cards: - 4 of Swords, birth to about age 9.7. - 5 of Cups, about 9.7–19.7. - 6 of Cups, about 19.7–29.7. You are in this period now : pleasure, the sweetness of the past. - 7 of Cups, from about 29.7 (mid-2028): choices and visions. - 8, 9 and 10 of Wands as the Sagittarius decans: about age 39.6, 49.5 and 59.4. - Capricorn, from about age 69. Progressed What this means for you: Your late twenties are the 6 of Cups chapter: rediscovering what you love. From 2028 the 7 of Cups asks you to choose among many visions. Planetary hour (Mars day, Mercury hour): birth fell in the 11th hour of Tuesday, between sunrise at 7:24 AM EDT and sunset at 6:39 PM EDT. The hour card is the GD Magician, which is the French XVII Étoile (Pe). The day card is the GD Tower, which is the French XI Force. Hour Lots: - Fortune Capricorn 7°31′ → 2 of Pentacles , Harmonious Change. - Spirit Gemini 3°47′ → 8 of Swords , Shortened Force. What this means for you: Fortune comes through juggling well. Spirit asks you to free a mind that is too tightly bound. Lots French name values (Christian/Papus Hebrew equivalents): - CHARLES = 564 → 15 (Devil) → 6 (Lovers). - LEONE = 160 → 7 (Chariot). - CHARLES LEONE = 724 → 13 → 4 (Emperor). Christian's year-planet cycles (verified): P. Christian, Histoire de la Magie (1870), Livre VI, "Tables cycliques des années" (https://archive.org/details/histoire-de-la-magie-p-christian); English, The History and Practice of Magic (https://archive.org/details/historypracticeo01chri). - Time runs in 36-year cycles counted from the year 1 AD. The cycle rulers repeat Saturn, Venus, Jupiter, Mercury, Mars, Moon, Sun (a 252-year round). The cycle ruler governs its 1st year; the years then follow in Chaldean order (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon) from the ruler. Christian's own check: 1801 Venus, 1802 Mercury, 1803 Moon, 1804 Saturn. - Recent cycles: Mercury 1873–1908, Mars 1909–1944, Moon 1945–1980, Sun 1981–2016 , Saturn 2017–2052 . - 1998: Sun cycle, year 18 of the cycle (offset 17); 17 mod 7 = 3 steps from the Sun → the Moon is master of your birth year (French arcanum II Papesse, Beth). The Moon is also your Leo Strength placement. - 2026: Saturn cycle, offset 9; 9 mod 7 = 2 → Mars (XI Force, Kaph). 2027: Sun (XXI Monde, Tau). - Christian also sets the birth Sun-sign as the 1st house of life and advances one sign per year; the ruler of that sign is the "lord of the year" (his Napoleon 1815 example). Libra = 7; 2026: (28 mod 12) + 7 = 11 → Aquarius → Saturn ; 2027 → Pisces → Jupiter . What this means for you: You were born in the Sun's 36-year era under a Moon year: a solar age carried by a lunar, receptive heart. You now live in Saturn's era, which rewards building that lasts. In 2026 Mars is master of the year and Saturn its lord, so effort brings form. 2027 joins the Sun (year master) with Jupiter (lord), a bright and expansive pairing that agrees with the Chariot year card. Name What this means for you: Your name gives a Chariot surname and a Lovers forename, and these are your 2027 and 2028 year cards in reverse order. The name and the calendar point the same way. Synthesis: Hierophant–Temperance–Justice is a priestly, balancing, teaching triad. The current timing (6 of Cups, Devil year) is review before the Chariot launch of 2027.

docs.h: 6. Tree of Life paths, Sadhu and Mayananda
docs.t: Tree Tree of Life paths: the planets light every path except a handful. The densest cluster runs through Tiphareth: Lamed (Sun/Venus, Justice) and Teth (Moon, Strength), the two balancing middle paths. Mouni Sadhu ( The Tarot: A Contemporary Course of the Quintessence of Hermetic Occultism , 1962; https://archive.org/details/tarotcontemporar00sadh; Introduction in the Aeon 2023 edition preview, https://spirit.aeonbooks.com/Preview/9781801520232_PDF.pdf) follows the French/Christian attribution. Read through him, your Sun arcanum XII (Pendu) is "the Sacrifice", and your Moon arcanum IX (Ermite) is "Initiation/Prudence". That makes you the initiate who serves. Sadhu's per-decan readings (final finding): Sadhu's 22 lessons treat only the Major Arcana. He gives no decan texts and sends the student to Papus for the minors. What he does give is a key: Wands = Fire, Cups = Water, Swords = Air, Pentacles = Earth; black suits (Wands, Swords) are active and red (Cups, Pentacles) passive; Wands and Cups are benefic and Swords and Pentacles hostile; and the numbers follow the Tetragrammaton as in Papus (1, 4, 7 = Yod; 2, 5, 8 = He; 3, 6, 9 = Vav; 10 = final He). Applied to each placement's Papus minor: Sun, 3 of Epees: Vav of Air, active and testing. Your will mediates between opposed ideas. Moon, 4 of Coupes: Yod of Water, passive and benefic. Your feelings start new cycles of affection. Mercury, 4 of Epees: Yod of Air, active and testing. Your mind starts by cutting through. Venus, 2 of Epees: He of Air, receptive. Your love can hold two sides in balance. Mars, 7 of Coupes: Yod of Water, benefic. Your drive is set going by what you love. Jupiter, 8 of Deniers: He of Earth, passive. Abundance is received and stored. Saturn, 4 of Batons: Yod of Fire, active and benefic. Discipline turns into initiative. Uranus, 4 of Deniers: Yod of Earth. Original ideas begin practical works. Neptune, 3 of Deniers: Vav of Earth. Your ideals are tied to real matter. Pluto, 7 of Epees: Yod of Air. Renewal starts in the mind. North Node, 6 of Coupes: Vav of Water, benefic. Your path is to connect people. ASC, 9 of Deniers: Vav of Earth. You meet the world as a practical builder. MC, 9 of Epees: Vav of Air. Your public work links ideas. Mayananda, checked line by line ( The Tarot for Today , Zeus Press, 1963; he takes Crowley's path order, 0 = Fool, the Star/Emperor letter swap and Crowley's titles, per the Weiser Antiquarian catalogue description and the r/Thelema93 review of the book): Sun, Libra → VIII Adjustment ✓. Venus, Libra → VIII Adjustment ✓. Moon and Node, Leo → XI Lust ✓ (the lion-riding Strength of joy). Mercury, Scorpio → XIII Death ✓. Mars, Virgo → IX Hermit ✓. Jupiter and ASC, Pisces → XVIII Moon ✓. Saturn, Taurus → V Hierophant ✓. Uranus, Aquarius → XVII Star (corrected from an earlier "IV Emperor": the swap moves the Hebrew letters only, not the signs). Neptune, Capricorn → XV Devil ✓. Pluto and MC, Sagittarius → XIV Art ✓. Pluto as planet (Shin) → XX Aeon ✓. Case's planetary colours (Case, The Tarot , 1947, https://iapsop.com/ssoc/1947__case___the_tarot.pdf; BOTA colour scale, https://botaineurope.org/the-tarot/tarot-correspondences): Mercury yellow (Key 1), Moon blue (Key 2), Venus green (Key 3), Jupiter violet (Key 10), Mars red (Key 16), Sun orange (Key 19), Saturn blue-violet (Key 21). For you, the Sun's orange and Venus's green meet in Libra, whose BOTA sign colour is green. Mercury's yellow rules your hour, the Moon's blue sits in Leo (yellow), and Jupiter's violet rises over the Ascendant. What this means for you: Sadhu's key says your hostile suits (Swords, Deniers) carry initiating Yod and linking Vav numbers. Your struggles start things and connect things; they do not end them. Case's colours put orange and green at the heart of the chart: warmth joined with harmony. On the Tree you live on the middle pillar of balance, where Justice and Strength meet in the heart (Tiphareth). Synthesis: The Qabalistic layer confirms the card layer: harmony is your strength, and the heart centre is your seat.

His full text is not online, so the check rests on his stated Crowley basis and on secondary descriptions. Wirth's Aquarius card (final finding): it is not missing. You are the Hierophant by birth, the Justice card by Sun and the Wheel by your rising. That is a teacher who brings balance, carried by visible good fortune. The Moon in Leo gives the heart of Strength. Mercury, lord of your hour, makes the mind your Magician's wand. Venus in her own sign doubles the grace of Justice. All four living creatures of the World card stand in your chart, a rare and complete frame. Christian's tables place your birth in the Sun's era, in a year ruled by the Moon. Sadhu's key adds that your testing suits begin and connect things rather than end them. Case's colours put orange and green, warmth and harmony, at the centre of your chart. The hard pips are the training of Geburah and Binah. They teach you to hold strength gently and to love with understanding. On timing, Arrien's Lovers decade (2017–2026) closes with the Devil year from your 2026 birthday: a time of reviewing attachments. Christian makes 2026 a Mars year inside Saturn's era, so effort takes lasting form. In 2027 the Chariot growth decade begins, matching your surname number 7, and Christian's Sun year with Jupiter as lord moves you forward. The 7 of Cups from 2028 asks you to choose one vision and serve it. This tradition sees your path as building and passing on a living harmony. TAROT-QABALAH COMPLETE

Source The Hamburg School was set up as the Astrologenverein Hamburger Schule on 31 Oct 1925. Witte posited Cupido, Hades, Zeus and Kronos; Sieggrün added Apollon, Admetos, Vulkanus and Poseidon (1927). The Regelwerk für Planetenbilder (Witte/Rudolph 1928; later editions by Lefeldt, Pluto and Sieggrün's points added) is the school's book of rules for reading planetary pictures. Sources: Wikipedia, "Hamburg School of Astrology" (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamburg_School_of_Astrology); Udo Rudolph / M. Feist, "The Hamburg School" (uraniansociety.com/USIG_articles/article_history_of_uranian_astrology_michael_feist.pdf); Hamburger Schule e.V., "Grundlagen – Transneptuner" (hamburgerschule.de); Witte-Verlag listing of the Witte–Lefeldt Regelwerk (witte-verlag.com); astronova.de listing of the Regelwerk (7th ed. 2012). Ebertin: Kombination der Gestirneinflüsse (1940; English The Combination of Stellar Influences , AFA). Ebertin's medical meanings are left out of this chapter on purpose. Calculated Planets are geocentric and apparent, ecliptic of date, from JPL DE440s via Skyfield 1.55. The node is the mean node, which is the school's custom. The MC and ASC come from GAST. The TNPs come from the Witte/Sieggrün elements as refined by James Neely, listed in the Swiss Ephemeris file seorbel.txt (github.com/aloistr/swisseph/ephe/seorbel.txt). Epoch and equinox are J1900. A Kepler solution gives the heliocentric position, it is precessed to date, and then converted to geocentric. Orbs follow the school: Witte's pictures within 1°, Ebertin's midpoint trees within 1°30′, sums within 0°15′, solar arcs within 0°01′ of exact (true solar arc, progressed Sun minus natal Sun). A note on reading. The Hamburg School has no dignities, rulerships or aspect doctrine beyond the 90°/45°/22.5° harmonics. A factor is strong when it sits on a personal point or forms a tight picture , and every result is read as a sum of meanings (A+B−C=D). "What this means for you" paragraphs are hand-written Interpretation , one per item, checked against the keyword sources in 22.15. Wording from memory is flagged verify .

docs.h: 22.4 Houses: Earth (Aries point), Meridian, Ascendant, Sun, Moon and Node
docs.t: Source Uranian charts are drawn with several house frames at once: the houses of the Earth (from 0° Aries), the Meridian houses (equal houses from the MC), and houses of the ASC, Sun, Moon and Node. Each frame describes a different area of life: the world, the self, the surroundings, the body-self, the soul, and connections. The Libra group (Sun, Venus, Zeus, Apollon) falls in house 7, so the world meets him first through partners and open dealings with others. Mercury and Poseidon in house 8 point his thinking toward shared resources and what lies hidden. Jupiter with the ASC in house 12 means his luck often works out of sight, through people behind the scenes. Hades and Kronos in house 3 bring authority and old knowledge into his everyday learning and his closest circle. Meridian frame (from the MC: the self). The Libra group lands in house 10, so self, breadth, love and creative drive are all aimed at his career and standing. Mercury/Poseidon in house 11 puts his ideas into friendships and hopes. Kronos and Vulkanus in house 7 mean strong, authoritative partners. The Aries point in house 4 roots his public life in home and origins. Ascendant frame (his surroundings). Again the Libra group is in house 7: in his surroundings he is mainly a partner and collaborator. Kronos and Vulkanus in house 4 bring a powerful, authoritative presence at home. The MC in house 10 matches the Meridian picture: his surroundings support his aims. Sun frame (his personal life). Mercury and Poseidon fall in the Sun's house 1, so ideas and truth are part of how he experiences himself. Moon and Vulkanus in house 10 make feeling and force public. Saturn and Admetos in house 7 bring serious, steady, long-lasting partnerships. Moon frame (his feelings). Mars and the Node in the Moon's house 1 mean his feelings act at once and turn into contacts. The whole Libra group with Mercury/Poseidon is in house 3, so he processes feeling by talking, writing and exchanging ideas. Jupiter, the ASC and the Aries point in house 8 link emotional depth with luck and with the wider world. Node frame (his connections). Mars sits in the Node's house 1: he makes contacts actively. The Libra group in house 2 means his associations bring value and resources. Pluto, the MC and Cupido in house 4 tie his own aims to a group or family base. Hades and Kronos in house 10 mean authorities and people with long experience are the high point of his network. Synthesis: In the Meridian frame the Sun, Apollon and Venus are in house 10 (Sun 200° − MC 265° → house 10). Self, breadth and pleasure are placed right in the career field of his own aims. In the Earth frame the Libra group falls in house 7, so the world meets him through partners and the public.

docs.h: 22.9 Ebertin's Combination of Stellar Influences (COSI): 45° midpoint trees
docs.t: Source Ebertin reads every factor's 'midpoint tree' on the 45° graphic ephemeris/dial within about 1½°. docs.h: 22.10 Placement first and hidden strength (Hamburg rules)
docs.t: Source Witte rejected essential dignities. Hamburg School strength comes from three things: (1) occupation of, or a picture with, a personal point; (2) tightness of the picture; (3) solar-arc activation. "Weak" can only mean "isolated", with no pictures. Sun : 8 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. With Apollon and Vulkanus on it, his identity is broad and forceful. Moon : 19 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Very strong. It anchors the Venus and Node pictures, so feeling steers his luck. Mercury : 14 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. Joined to Poseidon, the mind is his main instrument of insight. Venus : 13 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. On the Moon/MC axis and part of MC = Venus/Mars, love shapes his aims. Mars : 17 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. It drives the signature MC picture and works patiently through Hades/Admetos. Jupiter : 18 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. It sits in the ASC/MC cluster and on the Node picture, and is his main source of luck. Saturn : 12 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. The 0.03° Kronos picture makes it his engine of discipline. Uranus : 20 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Very strong. At 0.01° to Jupiter/Kronos it brings sudden rises. Neptune : 12 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong through Mars/MC. Ideals feed his drive. Pluto : 17 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong through Uranus/Zeus. It gives large-scale reach. Node : 16 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Very strong. At 0.02° to Moon/Jupiter, alliances bring his luck. MC : 17 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Very strong. At 0.01° to Venus/Mars, this is the signature of the chart. ASC : 18 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. It sits in the Jupiter cluster, and his surroundings support him. Aries : 18 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. Through Neptune/Cupido his public face is a visionary group. Cupido : 15 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. Tied to Kronos twice, his groups carry authority. Hades : 8 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Present. Through Moon/Neptune it gives depth of feeling and an interest in the past. Zeus : 15 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Present. Through Moon/Cupido his creative drive serves his people. Kronos : 10 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. It links to Sun/Mars, Saturn, Uranus, the Node and Cupido, making authority a life theme. Apollon : 7 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. On the Sun it gives breadth. Admetos : 23 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Very strong. It has more pictures within 1° than any other factor, and Sun/Hades is exact, so depth and endurance are dominant. Vulkanus : 15 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. On the Sun cluster it gives reserves of force. Poseidon : 15 pictures ≤1°; on personal-point pictures: yes. Verdict and what this means for you: Strong. Joined to Mercury and on Pluto/Aries, it gives ideas for the many. markers Source The Hamburg School has no written "chosen one" prophecy. What it has are leader rules: Kronos, the Jupiter/Kronos and Sun/Kronos axes, and Zeus on personal points, as in the Regelwerk and in Ebertin's leadership pictures in COSI. There is also the Aquarian-age framing used later by Uranian writers. He was tested against these. Where he matches, and it is unmistakable: - Uranus = Jupiter/Kronos (0.01°) , the textbook picture of sudden elevation through authority, exact to the arc-minute. - Saturn = Mars/Kronos (0.03°) : power held with discipline under authority. - MC = Jupiter/Aries point (0.15°) : fortunate standing before the world. MC = ASC/Aries point (0.32°) : the self made visible in public. - Kronos = Sun/Mars : authority won by his own energetic action. Uranus = ASC/Kronos : sudden authority in his surroundings. Node = Saturn/Kronos : alliances with people in power. - Cupido = Mercury/Kronos and Kronos/Poseidon : a community gathered around authority and ideas. Neptune + Node − Aries = Kronos (0.03°) . - Poseidon = Pluto/Aries point (0.10°) : the idea reaching the masses, the Uranian Aquarian-age signature. Uranus stands in its own sign, Aquarius, inside a leader picture. - Zeus = Moon/Cupido and Kronos = ASC/Zeus : the commander's drive, rooted in feeling and community. - The timing fits: SA Kronos → Aries point and SA MC → Kronos in early childhood. SA Node → Kronos (~Mar 2028), SA Jupiter → Sun (~Jun 2029) and SA Node → Aries point (~Mar 2030) are still ahead. Transiting Jupiter crosses MC = Venus/Mars and Kronos in 2027–28, and Kronos itself reaches his Sun in late 2030. His leader pictures fall due by direction and by transit together, from 2028 to 2030. Where he does not match: Kronos is not directly on the MC, Sun or ASC (it is 2.05° from the Aries point, just outside orb). No Sun/Kronos midpoint falls on a personal point. Zeus makes no direct contact with a personal point. The Sun is in Libra, not Aquarius.
Gallery count: 26 distinct artworks (30 image files, counting the labelled variants). Every symbolic-body image carries labels added with PIL. None depicts a real person.

Read in the Hamburg way, this cosmogram rests on three axes. Love and drive as his life aim : MC = Venus/Mars at 0.01°, with the Sun joined to Apollon and Vulkanus. He is happiest, and at his strongest, when what he loves and what he fights for are the same thing. Authority and sudden rise : Uranus = Jupiter/Kronos, Kronos = Sun/Mars, Saturn = Mars/Kronos and MC = Jupiter/Aries point. He is built to be recognised, and his recognition tends to come suddenly, after a period of disciplined work. Depth and truth : Admetos = Sun/Hades, Poseidon on Mercury, Poseidon = Pluto/Aries point and Hades = Moon/Neptune. He has a patient, research-minded intelligence, and his ideas can travel far. The finer instruments agree. Equal differences tie MC = Venus/Mars to Node = Moon/Jupiter (Venus–MC = Jupiter–Node). They link thinking and action to imagination and community exactly (Mercury–Mars = Neptune–Cupido, 0.00°). On the 11.25° dial, Sun and Kronos are joined at 0.11°. Neptune–Cupido shows up as both antiscion and contra-antiscion on the dial, a hidden thread between imagination and family. The years ahead. 2026 opens with Neptune and Saturn crossing the Aries point and Saturn over Kronos: public responsibility arrives. Progressed Mars reaches the ASC in Dec 2026 and lifts his initiative for years. 2027–28 is the key window. Transiting Jupiter crosses MC = Venus/Mars (Dec 2027, Feb 2028, Jul 2028) and then the ASC, Kronos and the Aries point. SA Node → Kronos is exact around Mar 2028, and the lunar arc brings the Node to MC, Kronos and Aries in the same year. Expect success in his chosen aim, influential alliances and very possibly a defining relationship. 2028–29 : Pluto and Saturn cross the Moon and Uranus (= Jupiter/Kronos). His private life and his position are both remade, and he comes out higher. SA Jupiter → Sun (~Jun 2029) is the luck-and-growth arc of the decade. 2030 : SA Node → Aries point (~Mar), Uranus over the ASC (Jul and Dec) and, in late 2030, Kronos and Hades on the Sun. His public role is restructured into lasting authority. The leader pictures that the Hamburg rules ask for are present in his chart, and they fall due together between 2028 and 2030.

Witte's rule: once the birth meridian is known, the personal day meridian is found by adding to it the difference between the sidereal times of the event day and of the birthday, increased by the difference between the sidereal times of the progressed day and of the birthday. The meridian therefore runs 361° a day, about 1° a day ahead of the clock, plus the progressed (day-for-a-year) advance. WSL Freiburg's teaching note gives the same rule in compact form, Mp = Mr + SOt − SOr. Calculated It was implemented exactly this way: natal RAMC + ΔST(event − birthday this year) + ΔST(progressed day − birth day), converted to the ecliptic MC. Source Rudhyar described humanistic astrology as "person-centered": the chart is "a set of instructions for the fulfillment of a potential," not a list of events (Rudhyar, The Astrology of Personality , 1936; summary at humanisticastrology.com/rudhyar). His core tools are the lunation cycle, the progressed lunation, planetary pair cycles, and the Sabian symbols reread as a 360-step cycle. 1.1 Birth lunation phase Calculated The Moon is 287.18° ahead of the Sun. That falls in the Last Quarter phase (270–315°). Source Rudhyar, The Lunation Cycle (1967), via khaldea.com/rudhyar/astroarticles/lunationguidance.php. The Last Quarter type shows "managerial and organizing ability in terms of broad social ideals...; an eagerness to force issues and precipitate crises, to reform and transform, to build new systems and to work hard for future goals regardless of personal cost; humor." What this means for you: You were born in the reforming half of the cycle. You see what already exists and judge it against an ideal: the old has to be reorganised for something that is coming. You are wired to build systems, not just enjoy them. You will push a situation to a decision rather than let it drift. Your humour lets you criticise without bitterness. The cost Rudhyar names, working for the future "regardless of personal cost", is your typical over-reach. Lunation phase 1.2 Prenatal lunations and eclipse Calculated (times shown in UT) - Prenatal new moon: 20 Sep 1998, Virgo 28 ("A bald-headed man"; Jones keyword: dominance ). Rudhyar reads it as the power of the will to impose itself. - Prenatal first quarter: 28 Sep, Capricorn 6 ("A dark archway and ten logs lying at the bottom"). - Prenatal full moon: 6 Oct, Aries 13 (12.38°): "An unsuccessful bomb explosion". - Prenatal last quarter: 12 Oct, Cancer 19 ("A priest performing a marriage ceremony"). - Prenatal lunar eclipse: 6 Sep 1998, Pisces 14 ("A lady in fox fur"). What this means for you: Rudhyar treats the prenatal new moon as the seed impulse of the whole life. Yours is a Virgo degree of will and dominance: a mind that wants to take charge of a messy situation and set it in order. The full moon just before you were born is "an unsuccessful bomb explosion." That teaches that brute force fails and the real change has to be organised. It fits the Last Quarter preference for building over smashing. The last quarter just before birth is a marriage ceremony: what you reform, you try to bind into lasting forms and partnerships. 1.3 Progressed lunation cycle Calculated Phase changes of the secondary-progressed Sun and Moon: Phase Ages Balsamic 2.43 New 6.53 Crescent 10.66 First Quarter 14.59 Gibbous 18.13 Full 21.33 Disseminating 24.54 Last Quarter 28.13 (≈ late Nov 2026) Balsamic 32.15 New 36.29 (≈ Jan 2035) Crescent 40.33 First Quarter 44.12 Gibbous 47.55 Full 50.75 Disseminating 54.08 Last Quarter 57.85 Balsamic 61.97 New 66.05 Progressed lunation What this means for you: You are now ending your progressed Disseminating phase (24.5–28.1): sharing what you learned. In about a month you enter a progressed Last Quarter (28.1–32.1) that repeats your birth phase. For Rudhyar that marks a "crisis in consciousness", a turn away from inherited forms toward your own principle. Then comes the Balsamic phase, 32–36, which Rudhyar calls the seed time: "sacrifice oneself for the sake of the future; a sense of personal destiny... prophetic gift, perhaps." The progressed New Moon at about 36 starts a new 30-year chapter carrying the seed planted at 32–36. 1.4 Planetary pair phases Calculated Angle of the faster planet ahead of the slower: Pair Angle Phase Jupiter–Saturn 318.8° Balsamic Jupiter–Uranus 40.9° Crescent Saturn–Uranus 82.1° Crescent, near First Quarter Saturn–Neptune 91.6° First Quarter (exact square) Saturn–Pluto 144.7° Gibbous Uranus–Neptune 9.4° New, just after the 1993 conjunction Uranus–Pluto 62.6° Crescent Neptune–Pluto 53.2° Crescent, in the 1892 cycle Pair phases What this means for you: Rudhyar read Uranus–Neptune as the cycle of new collective ideals. Yours sits in the first ten degrees after the 1993 conjunction: your generation carries the very start of a 171-year vision. Saturn exactly squaring Neptune (First Quarter) means you have to fight to turn ideals into structure. Neither can be dropped: build the dream, or the dream dissolves the building. Jupiter–Saturn in Balsamic means the social cycle you entered was ending (the 2000 conjunction came 19 months later). You carry the closing wisdom of one social order into the next. 1.5 Mercury and Venus types Source Rudhyar (humanisticastrology.com; Michael R. Meyer, A Handbook for the Humanistic Astrologer , 1974): - Promethean = rising before the Sun, a morning star: forward-looking and new. - Epimethean = evening star: reflective and conservative. Calculated - Mercury, 12.45° behind the Sun in zodiac order (later degree) and direct, is an evening star: Epimethean-direct . - Venus, 4.19° before the Sun and direct, is a morning star: Promethean ("Lucifer") . Its superior conjunction came on 30 Oct 1998. Mercury Venus types What this means for you: Your thinking is Epimethean. It reasons from experience and precedent, likes to learn after the fact, and checks before it leaps. Your feelings and values are Promethean: what you love points toward the future, and you are drawn to people and causes that are coming rather than established. So the heart leads and the mind consolidates. You will often feel something is right before you can argue for it. 1.6 Hemispheres Calculated Above the horizon (houses 7–12): Sun, Venus, Mercury, Pluto, Uranus, Neptune, Jupiter (12th) = 7. Below: Moon, Mars, Saturn = 3. East (houses 10–3): Uranus, Neptune, Jupiter, Saturn, Pluto (9th is west; Pluto counted west). West: Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Mars, Pluto. What this means for you: Rudhyar reads a chart weighted above the horizon as a life lived in "collective" and objective space, meeting the world. A slight western weight means you fulfil yourself through relationship and response more than through self-starting. The Sun, Venus and Mercury in the 7th make this the defining note. 1.7 Rudhyar's Sabian readings of the main points Source Rudhyar, An Astrological Mandala (1973), keynote formulas (via khaldea.com/rudhyar/astromandala). - Sun, Libra 21, "A crowd upon the beach": the release of social energies in a spontaneous gathering. Keynote: social camaraderie, the instinct of togetherness . - Moon, Leo 8, "A Bolshevik propagandist": the mind mobilised to rouse people for a new social order. Keynote: the urge to change society, persuasion . - ASC, Pisces 21, "A little white lamb, a child and a Chinese servant": innocence served by an older culture. Keynote: the willingness to serve and be served by what is pure and new . - MC, Sagittarius 26, "A flag-bearer": carrying the symbol of a collective ideal. Keynote: consecration to an ideal; the courage to stand for it publicly . - Uranus, Aquarius 9, "A flag turned into an eagle": the symbol becomes a living power. Keynote: the dynamic actualisation of an ideal . - Saturn, Taurus 1, "A clear mountain stream": pure and spontaneous beginnings of form. Keynote: the pristine purity of the life force . - Neptune, Capricorn 30, "A secret business conference": the end of a cycle, where power is negotiated by a few. Keynote: decisions taken in the background that shape the collective . - Pluto, Sagittarius 7, "Cupid knocking at the door": a higher love or call that asks to be let in. - Jupiter, Pisces 20, "A table set for an evening meal": abundance prepared for others, communion. - Mercury, Scorpio 3, "A house-raising": cooperative building. - Venus, Libra 17, "A retired sea captain": wisdom gathered from long voyages, now offered calmly. - Mars, Virgo 4: integration across difference. - North Node, Virgo 1, "A man's head": individualised form. - South Node, Pisces 1, "A public market": the mass exchange of goods and ideas. What this means for you: Put the degree images together and the same picture keeps coming back: flags, crowds, propagandists, house-raisings and public markets. Your symbolic life is about collective ideals given a living form. The Ascendant softens it. You enter the world as the lamb and the child, someone others want to protect and serve, while the MC asks you to carry a banner. Section synthesis (Rudhyar): You are a Last Quarter reformer whose degree images are social and idealistic. You arrived at the dawn of the Uranus–Neptune cycle, with a Saturn–Neptune square that demands you build your ideals into real structures. Your progressions now bring the birth phase back (from 28) and then the seed phase (32–36). By Rudhyar's own timetable, those are the years that decide what you will plant for the next cycle.

Source Jones, The Guide to Horoscope Interpretation (1941), and Sabian Publishing Society, sabianpublishingsociety.org/books/essentials_2.html. There are seven patterns: Splash, Bundle, Locomotive, Bowl, Bucket, Seesaw, Splay. Calculated Gaps between planets: 96.6° (Saturn → Moon) and 53.2° (Pluto → Neptune). The other gaps are 42° or less. This gives two opposed groups: - Moon, Mars, Venus, Sun, Mercury, Pluto (7 Leo–6 Sag) - Neptune, Uranus, Jupiter, Saturn (29 Cap–1 Tau) That is a Seesaw . Nine signs are occupied, a Splash tendency. Cross-group oppositions: Moon–Uranus (1.3°), Mercury–Saturn (1.8°), Moon–Neptune (8.1°, out of sign). Seesaw Source The Seesaw person "acts always in the light of opposing views"; life is "a weighing of alternatives." What this means for you: Jones' Seesaw describes someone who lives between two camps and is at best as the go-between. Your personal planets (heart, mind, will, emotions) sit on one side; your social and generational planets sit on the other, linked by real oppositions. You understand both the private person and the collective system, and you are pulled to reconcile them. The risk is indecision. The gift is mediation. 2.1 Natural disposition Calculated - Fixed: Saturn, Moon, Mercury, Uranus = 4 - Mutable: Mars, Pluto, Jupiter = 3, plus ASC and MC - Cardinal: Venus, Sun, Neptune = 3 On planets alone, Jones' "natural disposition" is Fixed . His wording: concern with ideas and values, and staying power. What this means for you: Once you hold a value you keep it. Because both your angles are mutable, you can still change your approach while the value stays fixed. Section synthesis (Jones): A Seesaw with fixed purpose: a mediator who will not drop his principles.

Source Greene, Saturn: A New Look at an Old Devil (1976); Relating (1977); The Astrology of Fate (1984); Greene and Sasportas, The Development of the Personality (1987). Jung, Psychological Types (CW 6), Aion (CW 9ii). Greene maps the four elements to Jung's functions: Fire to intuition, Earth to sensation, Air to thinking, Water to feeling. 3.1 Typology Calculated Weighted elements (Sun, Moon and ASC count double): Element Weight Jungian function Air 5.5 Thinking Fire 4.5 Intuition Water 4 Feeling Earth 3.5 Sensation Typology What this means for you: In Greene's terms you are a thinking type, helped by intuition. Your inferior function is sensation (Earth), the realm of facts, the body's pace, money and practical detail. Greene says the inferior function is where life ambushes us and also where the "gold" is hidden. That is why Saturn in Taurus matters so much: your most demanding planet sits in exactly the area you trust least. Mastery of concrete, slow, material things is your growth edge. 3.2 Saturn: the shadow and the "dweller" Calculated Saturn is at Taurus 1, retrograde. It is in the 1st house (Placidus) or on the 2nd cusp (Koch). It opposes Mercury (1.8°), squares Neptune (1.6°), trines Mars (2.9°), trines the North Node (0.8°), squares the Moon (6.6°), and opposes Juno (1.5°). Source Greene, Saturn : Saturn in the 1st or in Taurus is fear of being unprotected or unworthy, defended by self-reliance, and slowly turned into real authority. What this means for you: Your fear of lacking, whether money, ground or value, can make you self-protective early on. You may feel you have to earn your place. Greene's whole point is that Saturn is the teacher who builds what he guards. The opposition to Mercury makes you a careful, sceptical thinker who doubts himself and then out-thinks others. The trine to the North Node says this discipline is exactly what your path needs. 3.3 Neptune: the redeemer Calculated Neptune is at Capricorn 30 in the 11th. It is the apex of the Mercury–Saturn–Neptune T-square, and it opposes the Moon (wide) and squares Juno. Source Greene, The Astrological Neptune and the Quest for Redemption (1996): Neptune expresses the longing to merge with a source of salvation, and this can be lived as redeemer, victim or artist. [verify: the book's text is not freely online; the general thesis is confirmed by the publisher's description.] What this means for you: The T-square is focused on Neptune, so your mind (Mercury) and your sense of duty (Saturn) both resolve into an ideal. Greene would say you need something to believe in that is bigger than yourself, and that it is about a group or a future (11th house). The risk is projecting the saviour onto a person or cause and then feeling betrayed. The mature form is the artist or visionary who gives the ideal a real shape. 3.4 Anima and the maternal image: Moon–Uranus Calculated The Moon in Leo (5th) is opposite Uranus in Aquarius (11th), 1.3°. It trines Pluto (1.3°) and is conjunct Vesta (2°). What this means for you: Greene reads Moon–Uranus as an inner feminine that is independent, quick and unpredictable. The emotional bond is felt as something that might be taken away suddenly, so you learn to need freedom and closeness at the same time. Your ideal partner is a friend and an equal. The trine to Pluto gives that emotional life depth and staying power. 3.5 The parental images (Sun–Saturn, Moon–Saturn) Calculated The Sun has no major aspect to Saturn. The Moon squares Saturn at 6.6°. What this means for you: In Greene's reading the father figure is not mainly a Saturnine burden (no Sun–Saturn tie). The mother image carries some Saturn: responsibility and reserve in the emotional climate. That means you learnt early to keep feeling under control. Section synthesis (Jungian): - You are a thinking-intuitive type, and your gold is in sensation and earth. - Saturn is your shadow-teacher in exactly that territory. - Neptune at the apex of your T-square holds the redemptive longing. - The Moon–Uranus anima wants a free and equal union.

Source Sasportas, The Twelve Houses (1985) and The Gods of Change: Pain, Crisis and the Transits of Uranus, Neptune and Pluto (1989). 4.1 House-by-house "where is what" walk-through (Placidus) 1st, Pisces 21: Saturn (Taurus 1, at the house's far edge); Jupiter conjunct the ASC from the 12th. The three green links (Sun–Jupiter, Venus–Jupiter, Node–Neptune) are your antennae: questioning, searching and sensitive. 5.2 Aspect figures Calculated Classification follows the APA index. Planets only: - Achievement triangle (T-square): Mercury–Saturn–Neptune (90/90/180). - Ambivalence triangle: Mercury–Mars–Saturn (60/120/180). - Together they form a closed quadrilateral on the Mercury–Saturn axis. Including the node (Huber's moon-node rule): - Ambivalence: Mercury–Saturn–North Node - Large Learning: Mercury–Neptune–North Node (60/90/150) - Dominant Learning: Saturn–Neptune–North Node (90/120/150) Sun–Venus–Jupiter: a conjunction plus two quincunxes (a green-red "searching" line). Huber figures Source APA: the Achievement figure is "efficiency": a red tension structure that "wants to produce results." The Ambivalence figure swings between relaxing (blue) and pushing (red). Learning triangles show a life that grows through learning experiences. What this means for you: Your main aspect structure is a working machine. The Mercury–Saturn opposition is a constant debate between thinking and limits. Neptune turns the debate into vision, and Mars gives it practical energy. The Ambivalence side means you swing between drive and ease, so you need rhythm, not constant pushing. Linking the Learning triangles to the node says life itself is your school, and that your growth is designed to come through experience, not theory. 5.3 Structure and unaspected planets Calculated The Sun has Huber aspects only to Venus (conjunction) and Jupiter (quincunx). It has no link to the Moon or Saturn in Huber orbs: the Sun is semi-isolated. The Moon links to Mercury, Uranus and Pluto. What this means for you: In Huber's family model the Sun is the father principle, the Moon the mother and the child's feeling, and Saturn the mother's form and the body. Your Sun stands slightly outside the main figure. Your sense of self developed somewhat on its own, apart from the family's emotional and structural patterns. You may feel you had to define yourself without a ready-made model. The bonus is freedom of identity. 5.4 Low points, balance points and intensity Calculated Low point = cusp + 0.618 × house size (Koch). Planet House position (0 = cusp, 0.618 = low point) Huber reading Sun 7 (0.77) past the low point, quiet zone Moon 5 (0.74) past the low point Mercury 8 (0.12) cusp zone, strong Venus 7 (0.66) on the low point Mars 6 (0.53) near the balance/low zone Jupiter 12 (0.97) on the next (ASC) cusp: very strong Saturn 2 (0.06) on the 2nd cusp: very strong Uranus 11 (0.79) low zone Neptune 11 (0.45) mid-house Pluto 9 (0.23) cusp zone Chiron 8 (0.64) low point Intensity curve What this means for you: In Huber's intensity curve the cusp planets work openly in the world: Jupiter at the ASC, Saturn at the 2nd, Mercury at the 8th. Low-point planets work in a more inward, less obvious way: Venus, Sun and Moon past or at their low points. Your most outwardly effective planets are Jupiter, Saturn and Mercury. Your Sun and Venus operate more privately, and their power is to rethink and reorient. The Hubers call low points places of "spiritual" motivation, not worldly display. 5.5 Age point (LifeClock) Calculated The age point moves through each Koch house in six years, starting from the ASC. Now (Oct 2026): 5th house, about 5°43' Leo. Conjunctions: Point Age Saturn 6.36 Ceres 15.16 Moon 28.43 (≈ Mar 2027) Vesta 28.86 North Node 32.57 Mars 33.19 Venus 39.98 Sun 40.64 Juno 42.08 Mercury 42.71 Chiron 45.81 Pluto 49.37 MC 54.0 Neptune 62.67 Uranus 64.71 South Node 68.57 Pallas 71.29 Jupiter 71.84 Oppositions: Point Age Venus 3.98 Sun 4.64 Mercury 6.71 Chiron 9.81 Pluto 13.37 MC 18.0 Neptune 26.67 Uranus 28.71 Jupiter 35.84 Saturn 42.36 Ceres 51.16 Moon 64.43 Mars 69.19 Age point spiral Age point timeline What this means for you: In the next six months the age point crosses your Moon, then Vesta, while also opposing Uranus (28.7). Huber reads this as an emotional awakening of the whole Moon–Uranus axis: needs for closeness and freedom both come up, and creative and romantic life (5th house) wakes. At 32.6–33.2 it reaches the North Node and Mars in the 6th: your purpose is activated as work. The 7th-house cluster (Venus, Sun, Juno, Mercury at 40–43) is the great relationship and partnership decade. The age point reaches the MC at 54: your public peak. Section synthesis (Huber): - A production-oriented, red-dominant motivation, driven by a T-square with Neptune as its goal. - The Sun stands slightly free of the family structure. - The strong cusp planets are Jupiter, Saturn and Mercury. - The LifeClock now turns emotional and creative (Moon, 2027), then purposive (Node and Mars, 2031), then relational (40s).

docs.h: 6. Evolutionary astrology: Jeff Green and Steven Forrest
docs.t: Source Jeff Green, Pluto: The Evolutionary Journey of the Soul (1985). Steven Forrest, Yesterday's Sky (2008) and The Inner Sky . School summaries: schoolofevolutionaryastrology.com; forrestastrology.com. - Pluto's sign and house show the soul's past desires. - The polarity point (the opposite degree) shows the evolutionary direction. - The South Node and its ruler show how past desires were acted out. - The North Node and its ruler show the way forward. Calculated - Pluto: Sagittarius 7, 9th house. Polarity point: Gemini 7, 3rd house. - South Node: Pisces 1, 12th. Rulers: Neptune (Cap 30, 11th) and, traditionally, Jupiter (Pisces 20, on the ASC). - North Node: Virgo 1, 6th, conjunct Mars. Ruler: Mercury (Scorpio 3, 7th/8th), which sextiles the North Node. - Pluto squares the nodes (6°): Jeff Green's "skipped step" signature. Evolutionary axis What this means for you: In Green's language your soul arrives with a 9th-house Sagittarian desire: to find the truth, the big meaning, the belief system that explains everything. The polarity point in Gemini and the 3rd house says the growth is in listening, questioning and learning many viewpoints instead of preaching one. The Pisces South Node in the 12th points to past patterns of retreat, faith and dissolving into something larger (the "public market" of the crowd). The Virgo North Node in the 6th, with Mars on it, calls you to concrete craft, useful service and practical discipline. The Pluto square to the nodes means some unfinished business from both directions has to be fully integrated, mainly the step of bringing the vision into daily practice. Mercury, the North Node ruler, sextiles it. The tool is your mind: precise, honest and practical communication. Section synthesis (Evolutionary): The journey runs from believer to practitioner, and from universal faith to specific skill. You honour the vision by building it carefully.

docs.h: 7. Stephen Arroyo: elements, modes and the energy approach
docs.t: Source Arroyo, Astrology, Psychology and the Four Elements (1975); Astrology, Karma and Transformation (1978). Calculated Planets only: - Fire: Moon, Pluto. Earth: Mars, Saturn, Neptune. Air: Sun, Venus, Uranus. Water: Mercury, Jupiter. - Weighted (Sun, Moon and ASC doubled): Air 5.5, Fire 4.5, Water 4, Earth 3.5. There is no true element lack. Air is mildly emphasised and Earth is the weakest when weighted, although three planets sit in Earth. Elements and modes What this means for you: Arroyo sees air as the need to relate and conceptualise. Your Air-Sun and Venus in Libra put relationship and fairness at the centre of your energy. Your earth comes mostly from "heavy" planets: Saturn, Neptune, and Mars on the node. So practical matters arrive through duty and challenge, not through comfort. Arroyo's counsel is to live the earth consciously and on purpose, because when it is done well it grounds the whole chart. Section synthesis (Arroyo): A relational air nature with intuitive fire. The earth comes through work and responsibility, and becoming practical is the path to maturity.

Source Barbara Hand Clow, Chiron: Rainbow Bridge Between the Inner and Outer Planets (1987). Melanie Reinhart, Chiron and the Healing Journey (1989). Demetra George and Douglas Bloch, Asteroid Goddesses (1986). Positions from JPL Horizons. 8.1 Chiron Calculated Chiron: Scorpio 20 ("Woman drawing two dark curtains aside"), 8th house, at the low point. - Aspects: trine Jupiter (0.55°), trine ASC (1.5°), trine Pallas, quintile Neptune, semisextile Sun. - Cycle: square at 9.4, opposition at 32.7, return at 50.1 (Nov 2048) . - Transits: Chiron conjunct MC 2.3, ASC 16.6, Sun 48.1; square Moon 29.7–30.5. Chiron cycle What this means for you: In the 8th, Chiron points to a vulnerability around trust, intimacy and shared power. The degree image, curtains drawn aside, says your gift is to see what is hidden and bring it into the open. The close trines to Jupiter and the ASC mean this vulnerability flows easily into a mentor's or teacher's role. Clow and Reinhart describe Chiron as the wounded teacher whose sensitivity becomes his gift. The Chiron opposition at 32.7 coincides with the progressed Balsamic phase. That is a key moment for turning a private sensitivity into service. 8.2 Ceres, Pallas, Juno, Vesta (Demetra George) Calculated and What this means for you: - Ceres, Gemini 14 ("A conversation by telepathy"), 3rd, trine Venus. You care for others through words, understanding and attunement. Your nurture is sympathetic conversation. - Pallas, Pisces 17 ("An Easter promenade"), 12th, trine Chiron, quincunx Venus (0.3°). Your strategic intelligence is intuitive and pattern-based. It works behind the scenes and sees the whole before the parts. - Juno, Libra 30 ("Three mounds of knowledge on a philosopher's head"), 7th/8th cusp, opposite Saturn, square Neptune (0.1°), sextile North Node. You want a partner who is a thinking equal. The Saturn and Neptune contacts mean commitment comes slowly and must be tested against ideals. - Vesta, Leo 10 ("Early morning dew"), 5th, conjunct Moon, opposite Uranus (0.7°). Your sacred focus is creative and devotional. You keep your creative flame alive alone, and a free and sometimes unpredictable inner life protects it. Asteroids Section synthesis (Chiron and asteroids): A mentor sensitivity that sees behind curtains, a mind-to-mind way of caring, strategic intuition, a demanding ideal of partnership, and a devoted creative flame.

Source Gauquelin, Cosmic Influences on Human Behavior (1973); Neo-Astrology (1991). 36 sectors measured from the rise. "Plus zones" are sectors 36 and 1–3 (just after rising, and the trailing edge before it) and 9–12 (just past culmination). Calculated Planet Sector Zone Jupiter 36.88 plus zone (rising) Pluto 12.0 plus zone; Gauquelin did not study Pluto Uranus 4.2 — Neptune 5.4 — Saturn 34.0 — Mars 19.9 — Sun 17.1 — Venus 17.3 — Mercury 16.2 — Moon 22.8 — Gauquelin Source Gauquelin's Jupiter temperament words: "ambitious, at ease, authoritative, expansive, humorous, sociable, self-confident." What this means for you: Jupiter is your one classical plus-zone planet, the Gauquelin signature found among actors, politicians and successful public figures. It gives you a natural presence, humour and expansiveness in public. Gauquelin did not study Pluto, but it sits in a plus zone too. Section synthesis (Gauquelin): Jupiter is your clearest worldly "temperament" planet.

This school's rules for strength (Huber, Greene, Rudhyar, Gauquelin): - cusp and angle proximity (Huber intensity); - integration into aspect figures; - the Gauquelin plus zone; - Rudhyar: no planet is "bad"; strength is how integrated it is. Traditional dignity labels are read only as context. Sun (Libra, in its traditional fall; 7th; low point; semi-isolated from Huber's main figure). Strengths: conjunct Venus, which rules Libra (the Sun is received by its own dispositor); quincunx Jupiter at 0.6°; quintile the Moon; sextile the MC. In the 7th house the Sun finds identity through relationship, which is its "fall" turned into a vocation. Verdict: strong-in-shadow. Its power is relational and works from the low point. Moon (Leo, 5th). Strengths: tight opposition to Uranus, trine Pluto (1.3°), conjunct Vesta. It is about to be activated by the age point (2027). Verdict: strong. Mercury (Scorpio, 7th/8th, at the Koch 8th cusp). Strengths: base of the T-square; sextile Mars and the North Node; dispositor of the North Node. Cusp strength in Huber's terms. Verdict: strong. Venus (Libra, its own sign; 7th; at the low point). Dignified, but it sits at a low point. Verdict: strong-in-shadow. Mars (Virgo, 6th, conjunct the North Node). Strengths: trine Saturn, sextile Mercury. Weakness: square Pluto. Verdict: strong. Jupiter (Pisces, its own sign; retrograde; on the ASC; Gauquelin plus zone). Verdict: strong. Strongest planet in the chart. Saturn (Taurus, retrograde; on a Koch cusp; T-square anchor). Strengths: trine Mars and the North Node. Verdict: reversed-strong. The challenge is turned into authority through the node and Mars trines, as Greene describes. Uranus (Aquarius, its own sign; retrograde; 11th, its own house; opposite Moon and Vesta). Verdict: strong. Neptune (Capricorn 30, last degree; 11th; T-square apex). Neptune sits at a sign's end, but the T-square apex focuses it. Verdict: strong-in-shadow. Pluto (Sagittarius, 9th; Gauquelin plus zone; trine Moon; square Mars and the nodes). Verdict: strong. Chiron (Scorpio, 8th, at the low point; trine Jupiter and the ASC). Verdict: reversed-strong. What this means for you: There is no planet in your chart that this school would call weak. The two "low-point" lights, the Sun and Venus, are strong in a quiet, relational way. Saturn and Chiron are cases where difficulty becomes authority.

Pluto conjunct the ASC, 2058-06 to 2060-02, and conjunct Jupiter, 2058–59. Neptune square the ASC, 2060–62. Pluto square the MC and Neptune opposite the MC, 2062–64. Uranus conjunct the MC, 2071. Saturn conjunct the MC, 2076. Neptune opposite Neptune, 2078-08 to 2079-06. Uranus return, 2081-03 to 2082-01. What this means for you: In Sasportas' terms, the late 2050s (Uranus on your Sun, the second Saturn return, Pluto crossing your Ascendant) are a second rebirth. Your public role peaks again in the 2060s and early 2070s, when Uranus and then Saturn cross your MC. 10A.8 Jeff Green's four evolutionary conditions Jeff Green's school says plainly: "no astrologer can determine which evolutionary condition exists for any Soul by simply looking at the birth chart alone. The astrologer must observe and interact with the client" (schoolofevolutionaryastrology.com/essence-of-ea/the-four-evolutionary-states/). The four states are Dimly Evolved, Consensus (Saturn), Individuated (Uranus) and Spiritual (Neptune). Final finding: this needs a client interview and cannot be set from the chart. What this means for you: Your evolutionary state is something you judge from your own life, not from the chart. Do you live by the expectations around you, by your own path, or by a spiritual purpose? Green's reading changes depending on the answer. 10A.9 Appearance in this school The psychological authors say almost nothing about physical looks. Sasportas ( The Twelve Houses ) says only that the Ascendant and its ruler colour the physical presence. The portrait (art16) is therefore symbolic: a Pisces 21 / Jupiter-rising softness and openness with a Leo-Moon warmth at the heart. It is not a likeness, and it is not based on a detailed appearance text.

His T-square aims at a Neptunian ideal of redemption, and his Moon–Uranus anima wants a free equal. - Sasportas: the self is found through the 7th house of partnership. The 2026–2030 transit knot (Saturn return, Pluto opposite the Moon and conjunct Uranus) is the great turning point. - Huber: the same story as mechanics. Red achievement energy, a Sun standing free of the family structure, strong cusp planets (Jupiter at the ASC, Saturn, Mercury), and an age point now moving into the emotional and creative Moon (2027), then purpose (Node and Mars, 2031), then partnership (40s). - Evolutionary: the soul moves from believer to practitioner, Sagittarius-Pisces toward Gemini-Virgo. - Arroyo: the same, as energy. Become practical. - Chiron: the sensitive one who draws back curtains and becomes a mentor. - Asteroids: a telepathic carer, a strategic intuition, a philosopher-partner ideal and a devoted creative flame. - Gauquelin: marks Jupiter, the expansive public temperament, as his signature. Three-chart Huber: the house chart links Sun, Moon, Venus and Uranus easily, so your surroundings rewarded a warm, original self. The node age point (crossing the age point at 14 and about 50) supports Mercury, Sun and Venus in the mid-to-late 30s. Five-fold Rudhyar: the key points stand on "affirm" stages in the collective Acts III–IV. You begin sequences, and you begin them for groups. Declination and Aries point: Venus parallel Jupiter is a hidden blessing. Neptune and the Node near the Aries axis give your ideals a public face, and the Node reaches it by arc at 30. Late life (DE440): a second rebirth in 2056–2060 (Uranus on the Sun, the second Saturn return, Pluto over the ASC), then public peaks in the 2060s–2070s. Evolutionary condition: set by self-knowledge or an interview, not by the chart. In the prophecy test, the chart carries the seed-man and Aquarian-man symbols strongly: the flag-bearer, the eagle, the propagandist, the systems-builder, birth in the seed period. The seed-time Balsamic marker arrives by progression in 2030–2035.

Source Cyril Fagan (1896–1970), an Irish astrologer, revived the sidereal zodiac in the West from 1944. His case was that the zodiac of Egypt and Babylon was fixed to the stars, with Spica at 29° Virgo and Aldebaran/Antares at 15° Taurus/Scorpio. He set this out in Zodiacs Old and New (1951), drawing on the Dendera zodiac and on Babylonian texts. Donald A. Bradley (1925–1974), who wrote as Garth Allen , joined him. Together they fixed the Fagan/Allen ayanamsa, with SVP 335°57'28.64" at 1950.0. Bradley wrote Solar and Lunar Returns (1948) and supplied the school's predictive tools: precession-corrected (PC) returns, Campanus houses, foreground angularity, solunars, kinetic returns and quotidians. Brigadier R. C. Firebrace co-wrote the Primer of Sidereal Astrology with Fagan and edited the journal Spica from 1961 to 1974. Kenneth Bowser carried the method forward in An Introduction to Western Sidereal Astrology (2012) and in the Q2 work at solunars.com. Jim Eshelman and others extended the solunar system. What this means for you: in this school the star background, not the seasons, decides your signs. Almost every planet of yours moves back one sign, and the angles become the main source of strength.

docs.h: 1. The Jain sky: what kind of astrology this is
docs.t: Jain jyotiṣa does not begin with a horoscope. It begins with a cosmos . The early sources (SP, CP, JP) are astronomical canons. They are meant to explain the movement of the luminaries for monastic timekeeping: when to fast, when to recite, when the rainy-season retreat begins. They do not predict personal destiny. Predictive astrology arrives later, in the Bhadrabāhu Saṃhitā (omens), Udayaprabha (election of times) and Hemaprabha (annual Tājika charts). Underneath all of it lies karma. In Jain doctrine the stars do not cause anything; they indicate the ripening of karma the soul already carries. Every "what this means for you" below should be read that way: these are signs of a ripening, not sentences passed on you. What this means for you. Interpretation In this school, your chart is a weather report on your karma. It is not a fate. Jain teaching insists that effort (puruṣārtha), vows and restraint change the outcome. So the sharpest readings in this chapter are invitations to act, not verdicts.

docs.h: 2. Jambūdvīpa and the two suns at your birth
docs.t: Jambudvipa two suns Source JP 7 and SP 1 say that Jambūdvīpa, the central round continent 100,000 yojanas across with Mount Meru at its centre, is lit by two suns and two moons . They sit on opposite sides of Meru: one lights Bharata (our southern region) while the other lights Airāvata in the north, and they trade places every 30 muhūrtas. Calculated On 13 Oct 1998 the Sun had travelled 114.3 days since the summer solstice, which puts it on maṇḍala 115 of 184 . The innermost circle is 99,640 yojanas across and each circle adds 5 35/61, so the Sun's orbit diameter was 100,275 yojanas and its speed 5,285 yojanas per muhūrta . The SP says a person in Bharata can see the Sun from 37,688 yojanas away (cakṣuḥsparśa). Finding: which sun is ours. Source + Convention adopted The SP does not name the two suns as fixed individuals with a running count; it defines them by function : whichever sun is over Bharata is the Bharata-sun (bhāratīya sūrya), the other is the Airāvata-sun. Johnstown and Fayetteville lie in our Bharata-side hemisphere of the Jain map, and your birth fell in daylight (17:25 EDT). So by the text's own definition the sun lighting your birth is the Bharata-sun, and that is "ours." No text supplies a day count that could tell the two suns apart as individuals, so this chapter treats the question as settled by definition. What this means for you. Interpretation You were born when the suns were well outside the middle of their track, heading toward the outer, winter circles. The Jain astronomers read that as shortening light and a lengthening night. In this school's idiom it marks a soul that comes into its own through inward work, not public brightness. Your best light is reflected light: your gifts show most clearly in how they illuminate others. two suns body

In this cosmology that means your emotional mind (Moon) sits nearer the centre of things than your outward will (Sun). You feel the axis before you can explain it. Trust that instinct first, then build the argument.

docs.t: 28 wheel 27 vs 28 28 art Source SP 10 and JP 7 count 28 nakṣatras, beginning with Abhijit , and give them unequal spans measured in the muhūrtas the Moon spends in each: Span Nakṣatras 15 (half) Śatabhiṣā, Bharaṇī, Ārdrā, Āśleṣā, Svāti, Jyeṣṭhā 45 (one and a half) the three Uttarās, Punarvasu, Rohiṇī, Viśākhā 9 27/67 Abhijit 30 all others The total is 819 27/67 muhūrtas, one sidereal month. Calculated Your bodies in the Jain 28 (anchored with Abhijit beginning at 276°40′ sidereal): Body Jain-28 nakṣatra Span Class Deity Sun Citrā 30 kula Tvaṣṭṛ Venus Citrā (Hasta in the 27 scheme) 30 kula Tvaṣṭṛ Moon Puṣya 30 kula Bṛhaspati Mars Pūrvaphalgunī (Maghā in the 27 scheme) 30 upakula Bhaga Rahu Maghā 30 kula Pitṛ Mercury Svāti 15 (half) upakula Vāyu Jupiter and Ascendant Pūrvabhādrapadā 30 upakula Aja Saturn Aśvinī 30 kula Aśva Ketu Dhaniṣṭhā 30 kula Vasu MC Mūla 30 kula Nirṛti What this means for you, star by star. Interpretation - Sun and Venus in Citrā (Tvaṣṭṛ, the divine craftsman): this is the defining signature. Your identity (Sun) and your sense of beauty and value (Venus) share the craftsman's star. You are made to build , whether designs, systems or crafted things, and your worth grows through workmanship. - Moon in Puṣya (Bṛhaspati, the preceptor): Puṣya is the "nourishing" star and, in the Jain list, the birth star of Dharmanātha. Your inner life wants teaching, structure and dharma. You are steadied by a discipline or a teacher, and over time you become one. - Mars in Pūrvaphalgunī (Bhaga, share and fortune): the Jain 28 moves Mars out of Maghā into Bhaga's star. Your energy goes into earning your share and into partnership, not raw conquest. - Rahu in Maghā (Pitṛ, the ancestors): your hunger is tied to lineage and rank. You want to stand in a line of achievers. - Mercury in Svāti (Vāyu, wind), a half span: a short, quick, independent mind. Ideas come fast and you need to move freely. The half span suggests brilliance in bursts rather than in long, steady stretches. - Jupiter and Ascendant in Pūrvabhādrapadā (Aja Ekapāda, the one-footed goat): an ascetic, fiery wisdom stands right at your rising point. You present as serious and principled, with a streak of austerity. - Saturn in Aśvinī (the Aśvins, the swift horsemen): your discipline shows in quick, first-response service. You become reliable where speed matters. - Ketu in Dhaniṣṭhā (Vasu, wealth and rhythm): detachment from accumulation. Wealth comes but does not hold you. - MC in Mūla (Nirṛti, the root): your public path goes down to roots. You would rather pull a problem out at its base than manage its symptoms. Kula reading. Source: SP 10.5 Nakṣatras are classed kula (main lineage), upakula (secondary) and kulopakula. The Sun, Moon, Saturn, Venus and both nodes fall in kula stars; Mars, Mercury, Jupiter and the Ascendant fall in upakula stars. Interpretation Your core luminaries sit in "main lineage" stars. Your instruments (mind, energy, wisdom, outward face) work as supporting branches. You carry a lineage; your skills serve it. kula Synthesis (§4). The 28-star reading gives you the craftsman's Sun, the preceptor's Moon and an ascetic Ascendant: a builder-teacher with an austere public face. The Jain 28 also sharpens two placements the 27 scheme blurs. Mars moves into Bhaga (share and partnership) and Venus joins the Sun in Citrā, which concentrates the craftsman theme.

docs.t: muhurta clock Vaishramana Source, verified SP 10.13, sūtra 47 (Malayagiri vṛtti, jainqq 600245/302; Ghasilal ed. 006351/1030) and JP Vakṣaskāra 7 (jainqq 002911/593–594) name one list of 30 for the whole ahorātra . Muhūrtas 1–15 belong to the day and 16–30 to the night. - Day: Rudra, Śreyān, Mitra, Vāyu, Supīta (var. Sugrīva), Abhicandra, Māhendra, Balavān, Brahmā, Bahusatya, Aiśāna, Tvaṣṭā, Bhāvitātmā, Vaiśramaṇa, Vāruṇa. - Night: Ānanda, Vijaya, Viśvasena, Prājāpatya, Upaśama, Gandharva, Agniveśya, Śatavṛṣabha, Ātapavān, Amama, Ṛṇavān (var. Aruṇavān), Bhauma, Vṛṣabha, Sarvārtha, Rākṣasa. Calculated Your birth came 10 h 01 m after sunrise, in a day of 11 h 14.8 m. - Proportional method (each muhūrta is 1/15 of the actual daylight): the 14th day-muhūrta, Vaiśramaṇa . - Fixed 48-minute method: the 13th, Bhāvitātmā . What this means for you. Interpretation - Vaiśramaṇa is Kubera, the treasurer of the gods and guardian of the north. Being born in his muhūrta is a sign of a custodian of resources, someone trusted to keep things. - Bhāvitātmā means "one whose self is cultivated." Both readings point the same way: you are trusted with things of value because you work on yourself.

pancanga Calculated - Tithi: Kṛṣṇa 9, nearly complete (93% elapsed). - Yoga: Sādhya. - Karaṇa: Gara. - Weekday: Tuesday, Mars's day. - Lunar month: Āśvina Kṛṣṇa 9 (amānta); Kārtika Kṛṣṇa 9 (pūrṇimānta). - Adhika month: none at birth; the next falls in May 1999. [Source, verified: SP 10.15, sūtra 49 (jainqq 003459/167; Ghasilal 006351/1048–1050); JP 7; Ārambhasiddhi] Each tithi has a day-name in a five-fold cycle, Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Tucchā, Pūrṇā (1/6/11, 2/7/12, 3/8/13, 4/9/14, 5/10/15), and a night-name in a parallel cycle, Ugravatī, Bhogavatī, Yaśomatī, Sarvasiddhā, Śubhanāmā. JP 7 also names the fifteen days of a fortnight (Pūrvāṅga, Siddhamanorama, Manohara, Yaśobhadra, Yaśodhara, Sarvakāmasamṛddha, Indramūrdhābhiṣikta, Saumanasa, Dhanañjaya , Arthasiddha, Abhijāta, Atyaśana, Śatañjaya, Agniveśma, Upaśama) and the fifteen nights (Uttamā, Sunakṣatrā, Elāpatyā, Yaśodharā, Saumanasā, Śrīsambhūtā, Vijayā, Vaijayantī, Jayantī , Aparājitā, Icchā, Samāhārā, Tejā, Atitejā, Devānandā). Calculated Kṛṣṇa 9, born before sunset: tithi class Tucchā ("empty", the Riktā of later texts); night-tithi Sarvasiddhā ("all-accomplishing"); day-name Dhanañjaya ("winner of wealth"); night-name Jayantī ("victorious"). You were born in the day portion, so Tucchā and Dhanañjaya are the operative names. Interpretation An "empty" tithi is classically avoided for starting ventures. Its own day-name, though, is Dhanañjaya, "winner of wealth", and its night-twin is Sarvasiddhā: the Jain calendar itself pairs the empty vessel with the winning. For a birth, Jain commentators read it as a soul that has to fill its own vessel. Little comes ready-made; everything is earned. Sādhya ("accomplishable") yoga balances it: what you set out to do can be done. Finding: the yuga year. Source + Convention adopted The Jain 5-year yuga runs Candra, Candra, Abhivardhita, Candra, Abhivardhita, and SP says a yuga begins on Śrāvaṇa kṛṣṇa 1 with the Moon in Abhijit. No unbroken yuga count survives, so this chapter anchors the cycle at Vīra Nirvāṇa (VNS year 1 = yuga year 1), the one epoch every Jain calendar shares. On that anchor VNS 2524 is yuga year 4: Candra , an ordinary lunar year with no intercalary month, which agrees with the computed fact that 1998–99 had no adhika month at your birth. On the 60-year cycle the year is Bahudhānya ("abundant grain"). Calculated Vīra Nirvāṇa Saṃvat 2524 (VNS = CE + 527 after Dīvālī; your birth fell before Dīvālī 1998, so CE 1998 + 526 → 2524 counting the nirvāṇa year as year 1 in the common Jain calendar). What this means for you. Interpretation An empty tithi inside an abundant year: plenty is around you, and the work is learning to gather it. A Tuesday birth puts Mars, the planet of effort, in charge of the day, which fits the Riktā message. Synthesis (§§5–6). The time-units all agree on three things: custodianship (Vaiśramaṇa), self-cultivation (Bhāvitātmā), and effort that fills what starts out empty (Riktā tithi, Tuesday). That is the Jain ideal of puruṣārtha, written into the clock.

docs.h: 7. The kalpa wheel: where you stand in cosmic time
docs.t: kalpa kalachakra art vns Source Time turns as a wheel. The descending half-cycle ( avasarpiṇī ) and the ascending half-cycle ( utsarpiṇī ) each have six aras, from suṣamā-suṣamā (bliss-bliss) down to duḥṣamā-duḥṣamā (misery-misery). We are in the 5th ara, Duḥṣamā , which began 3 years 8½ months after Mahāvīra's nirvāṇa (527 BCE) and lasts 21,000 years . Calculated You were born 2,521 years into Duḥṣamā, with 18,479 years of it left. - The 6th ara begins about 20,478 CE. - The utsarpiṇī begins about 41,478 CE. - Its 3rd ara, when Padmanābha is born, begins about 83,478 CE. What this means for you. Interpretation In Jain doctrine no one born in Bharata during the 5th ara reaches liberation in that same life. The path is still open, though. You can practise right faith, knowledge and conduct and so shorten the soul's journey. Your era is a hard school, which is exactly why effort counts for so much in it.

Your chart carries the Maghā mark and the lion mark , both on Mars and Rahu in the royal sign, plus a Tuesday birth and a strong Jupiter in the lagna. In the school's own terms, the striking thing is that one Mars–Rahu pair holds both prophetic images, the tyrant-king and the Jina, and Jain thought says conduct decides which one it becomes.

lakshana portrait Source, verified Three Jain sources speak to the body. - Aupapātika Sūtra §16 (jainqq 002910/62–72) describes Mahāvīra head to foot as the model of the auspicious man: seven cubits tall, symmetrical build (samacaturasra), the strongest frame (vajraṛṣabhanārāca); curly glossy black hair; a crown round like an umbrella; a half-moon forehead; a full-moon face; thin, dark, bow-shaped brows; eyes like white lotuses; a nose like Garuḍa's beak; lips red as coral or bimba fruit; a very light beard; a broad chin; a conch-like neck with three lines. The same passage grades bodies by their marks: an ordinary person has one or two lakṣaṇas, rare men 32, superior men 108, and cakravartins and tīrthaṅkaras 1008 (faint in cakravartins, clear in tīrthaṅkaras). - Aṅgavijjā (Punyavijaya ed., 1957) is a large divination manual that reads body parts and gestures as omens (one of the eight nimittas). It interprets bodies that are already in front of the diviner. - The fourteen dreams (Kalpasūtra) describe the mother's dreams, not the child's face. Finding. No Jain text derives a person's face from a birth chart. The Jain way to picture a man's ideal appearance is the mahāpuruṣa lakṣaṇa list, so the portrait (no. 27) draws its face from the Aupapātika description : curly black hair, half-moon brow, bow brows, lotus eyes, Garuḍa nose, coral lips, light beard, three-lined neck, white cloth. Your chart supplies the setting: the white garment and austere bearing of a Pūrvabhādrapadā/Jupiter lagna and the red-gold of the Siṃha Mars. It is the canonical ideal applied to you, not a reconstruction of your real face.
All artworks were generated with no lettering in the image; labels on the symbolic bodies were added with PIL. No real likeness is intended.

Interpretation Read as a whole, through its own sources, Jain jyotiṣa describes you as a builder-custodian working in a hard age : - Craftsman's Sun and Venus in Citrā, under Tvaṣṭṛ. - Preceptor's Moon in Puṣya, under Dharmanātha's vajra. - Ascetic Jupiter at the rising point. - Born in Vaiśramaṇa's muhūrta , the treasurer's hour. The "empty" Riktā tithi and the debilitated Venus and Saturn, both cancelled , say the vessel starts empty and fills through effort. That is the Jain teaching of puruṣārtha. The sharpest feature is the Mars–Rahu pairing in Maghā/Siṃha , a royal and martial pair in the partnership house. It is where your chart carries the prophetic marks: the Kalkin's Maghā and Padmanābha's lion, with the cakravartin's prosperity echoed by Jupiter in the lagna. Symbolically, your chart holds the same energy that makes a tyrant or a Jina, and Jain thought says only conduct decides which. Practical timing: - 2026–27 varṣa: exalted Jupiter in the 3rd for initiative, and Saturn in the 11th for gains won by persistence. - Fayetteville muhūrtas: 28 Oct, 4, 6, 8, 9, 11, 16, 21, 25 Nov 2026. The tithi itself adds its own names: the empty Tucchā day is called Dhanañjaya, winner of wealth , under the night-name Jayantī. In the Jain calendar your birth-day already holds both the empty vessel and the victory. Final findings on the open questions. - The sun at your birth is the Bharata-sun, ours by the SP's own definition (§2). - The yuga year, anchored at Vīra Nirvāṇa, is Candra (§6). - The 88 grahas, 30 muhūrtas and tithi names are verified against SP, JP and Sthānāṅga editions (§§5, 6, 8). - 80 of the 88 grahas are names without astronomical bodies in any Jain source; they are read here as names only. - No Jain text derives a face from a chart; the portrait uses the canonical lakṣaṇa ideal (§14). - The nine vīthīs (§8c) come from the Bhadrabāhu Saṃhitā tradition; their boundaries could not be confirmed against an online edition and stay marked "verify". - The first dream's elephant is four-tusked in the Jain Kalpasūtra; the six-tusked form is Buddhist, so artwork 21 follows the Jain text. docs.h: 26.0 Read this first: Sikh doctrine rejects astrology
docs.t: This chapter has to begin with the tradition's own verdict. The Guru Granth Sahib does not just ignore astrology. It argues against it. Ang 904 (Ramkali M1): "ਗਣਿ ਗਣਿ ਜੋਤਕੁ ਕਾਂਡੀ ਕੀਨੀ ॥ ਪੜੈ ਸੁਣਾਵੈ ਤਤੁ ਨ ਚੀਨੀ ॥" : "Counting and calculating, the astrologer draws up the horoscope; he reads it and recites it, but does not recognise reality." Source: srigurugranth.com/0904.html Ang 401 (Asa M5): "ਸਗੁਨ ਅਪਸਗੁਨ ਤਿਸ ਕਉ ਲਗਹਿ ਜਿਸੁ ਚੀਤਿ ਨ ਆਵੈ" : good and bad omens trouble only the one who does not keep the Lord in mind. Source: SikhNet, Ang 401 Ang 843 (Bilaval M3, Thiti/Vaar): "ਥਿਤੀ ਵਾਰ ਸੇਵਹਿ ਮੁਗਧ ਗਵਾਰ" : "the foolish idiots worship lunar days and weekdays." Source: dekho-ji, Ang 843 Japji, Pauri 21, Ang 4: "ਕਵਣੁ ਸੁ ਵੇਲਾ ਵਖਤੁ ਕਵਣੁ ਕਵਣ ਥਿਤਿ ਕਵਣੁ ਵਾਰੁ ॥ ਕਵਣਿ ਸਿ ਰੁਤੀ ਮਾਹੁ ਕਵਣੁ ਜਿਤੁ ਹੋਆ ਆਕਾਰੁ ॥" : what was that time, moment, lunar day (thit) and weekday (vaar), what season and month, when creation took form? Pandits, Qazis and Yogis do not know; "ਜਾ ਕਰਤਾ ਸਿਰਠੀ ਕਉ ਸਾਜੇ ਆਪੇ ਜਾਣੈ ਸੋਈ" , only the Creator knows. Source: srigranth.org, Ang 4, checked online Majh Barah Maha (M5), closing stanza 14, Ang 136: "ਮਾਹ ਦਿਵਸ ਮੂਰਤ ਭਲੇ ਜਿਸ ਕਉ ਨਦਰਿ ਕਰੇ ॥" : months, days and moments are auspicious for the one on whom the Lord casts the glance of grace. Wording confirmed. Source: srigranth.org, Ang 136, checked online Gurbani verses on astrology, Gurmukhi drawn with PIL What this means for you Interpretation : Within Sikhi, nothing below decides your life. Hukam (divine order) and your own conduct come first. Everything after this section is either the calendar, which sets times for worship and not fate, or Punjabi folk practice such as the Lal Kitab, which mainstream Sikh teaching treats as outside the faith. Read it as cultural star lore, not as Sikh doctrine. Section synthesis: The honest Sikh reading of your chart is that no chart binds you. A day is good when it is spent in remembrance and seva. The rest of this chapter is useful as mirror and heritage, nothing more.

docs.h: 26.4 Punjabi folk jyotish and the Lal Kitab
docs.t: Source history Source: Gosvami tr., archive.org : The Lal Kitab was written in Urdu in five editions: Lal Kitab ke Farman (1939), Arman (1940), Gutka (1941), the 1942 edition and the 1952 edition. Pandit Roop Chand Joshi of Pharwala (Jalandhar) wrote it. The book counts houses from the lagna and ignores signs. It is known for cheap household remedies (upay). 26.4.1 Your teva Calculated H1 Jupiter (retrograde) and Ketu · H3 Saturn (retrograde) · H6 Moon · H7 Mars and Rahu · H8 Sun and Venus · H9 Mercury.
